root_cause_summary: Inconclusive
investigation_details: Overall, I did not find any glaring issues in the logs for the “4-West MedSurg Primary Console” or the “UH-4W MedSurg Secondary Console”; all of the calls listed in the syslogs match up with the logs in 3CX. For the Primary console, there were plenty of alerts generated before the audio was reset, however, there is no indication (from the logs) that an attempt was made to open audio with a device; after resetting the audio, there was an audio call to 4-West MedSurg RCB3-4166 port 1 ASBC-A that lasted ten (10) seconds.

Between 1:45am and 3:45am, there were no audio calls to the Primary Console, however, there were six (6) audio calls to Secondary Console. One (1) of those audio calls is listed as “Not Answered” and this is most likely due to the fact that the Secondary Console was trying to open audio with (4-West MedSurg RCB3 4805-4810:2) while audio was already open between two GRS5’s (4-West MedSurg RCB3 4805-4810:2) and (4-West MedSurg RCB3 4839-4840-4802:1); the audio was open for forty-six (46) seconds between the two GRS5’s. It is worth noting that if audio is open between two devices and an attempt to call one of those devices is made, a pop-up should appear saying that the call cannot be completed; this pop-up will disappear from the screen after about twenty (20) seconds. It should also be noted that if a call is placed between two GRS5’s, audio is opened and the call is cancelled, then audio will still stay open until the “Hang-Up” button is pressed.
verification_summary: R&D conducted the investigation and found no issues.
rca_review_comments: RCA is inconclusive based on Embedded Engineerings review of the logs.

comment_summary: Multiple SRS units failed at a customer site and were returned for analysis; all four returned units had a shorted LM4675 audio amplifier, with the short between +5V and common, leaving the SRS apparently dead and unable to be rebooted. Database event review showed that around the time of the Lost Primary Audio Station alerts the affected rooms had various unrelated call types (Normal Call, Bed Disconnect, Pillow Speaker Disconnect, Staff Call), with some rooms looping in and out of the Lost Primary Audio Station alert until the SRS was replaced. The same pattern then appeared at a second customer, and syslogs were collected per device for several rooms, while acoustic settings were compared against a working system. The thread ends without an identified cause for the amplifier shorts.

=== KB Article ===
kb_article_id: 2629730338
title: Lost Primary or Secondary Audio Station
text: ## Problem

---

Used when there is a Lost Primary Audio Station or Lost Secondary Audio Station system alert on the primary console and in the Enterprise Configuration Tool's (ECT) 'Active Calls' section.

- Environment: Nurse Call - All versions
- This KB may require an RCB reboot

## Solution

---

1. Determine the audio station type, serial number and RCB port number by performing the following steps:
    1. On the GRS10 console navigate to Menu → System Alerts.
    2. Highlight the **Lost Audio Station** alert and click the **Show Details** button.
    3. At the bottom of the screen note if the Audio station is a GRS5 *(gas)* or SRS *(sas)*, its serial number and RCB Port number.

         For example:*** iob-0xxxxxxxWIS:gas-0xxxxxxxWIS:1*** - where ***iob-*** is RCB serial, ***gas-*** is GRS5 serial and ***:1*** or ***:2*** represent RCB ports that the audio station is connected to - RS1 or RS2 respectively.  
  
    4. If SRS, skip to **step 6**.  
    5. If GRS5 proceed to the next step.  
  
2. Determine if GRS5 is powered on or off, online or offline by performing the following steps:
    1. [Access the command line interface (CLI) of the parent RCB device](https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CTS/pages/888144057/How+to+connect+to+a+base+device+command+line+interface+CLI) (parent of the lost GRS5).
    2. Once at *iob *command prompt, use *ping* command. If GRS5 is in port 1 use *10.0.0.2* IP address, if in port 2 use *10.0.0.6.*
    3. If ping was unsuccessful, skip to **step 5.**
    4. If ping was successful, the GRS5 is powered on and online; proceed to the next step.  
  
3. Determine if the GRS5 is properly configured and on the correct software version by performing the following steps:
    1. [Access the CLI of the GRS5](https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CTS/pages/907903288/How+to+Access+GRS5+GRS7+Command+Line+Interface+CLI).
    2. Once at the  `gas-xxxxxwis $`command prompt, determine if the serial number in the prompt matches the serial number from **step 1.b**.
        1. If serial numbers are mismatched, make the necessary corrections in ECT.
        2. If they are the same, proceed to the next step.
    3. In the command prompt of the GRS, type ***nnc -v*** and hit enter. Note the application software version of the GRS5.
    4. Open Service Portal or SAMM Tool and determine if GRS5 is on the correct software version with the rest of the devices.
        1. If the software is mismatched, download and apply the correct version to the GRS5.
        2. If the software matches proceed to the next step.  
  
4. [Reboot the GRS5 and the parent RCB](https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CTS/pages/1030848709/How+To+Reboot+a+Base+Device) and wait up to 5 min for the alerts to clear.
    1. If the system alert has cleared, complete the CRM resolution fields using the tables below. If issue persists, engage a senior member of your team for further guidance before escalating.  
    2. If the system alert persists, **replace the GRS5**.  
  
5. If ping was unsuccessful, perform the following steps to determine if the GRS5 is powered off or offline.
    1. Power down the parent RCB and test cabling between RCB and GRS5 and visually inspect both ports for damage.
    2. If cable tests passed and no port damage is seen, temporarily swap RS1 and RS2 ports on the RCB and power on the RCB to determine if power is being delivered to GRS5 on the other port.
        1. If power is being delivered to GRS5 and both RS ports are being used, the RCB has a faulty RS port and it needs to be replaced.
        2. If RS2 port was open, configure the GRS5 for port 2 in ECT and publish configuration.
        3. If GRS5 still does not power on, **replace the GRS5**.  
  
6. SRS’s are not IP addressable so no ping command can be performed from its parent RCB to verify the connectivity. A simple way to confirm connectivity of an SRS is to try a PSoC software download to the SRS in Service Portal or SAMM Tool.
    1. If PSoC download is unsuccessful, skip to **step 8**.
    2. If PSoC download is successful the SRS is powered on and online. Proceed to the next step.  
  
7. In Service Portal or SAMM Tool, determine if SRS is on the correct PSoC software version.
    1. If the software matches, try rebooting the SRS via Room Reset on GRS10 or by [rebooting its parent RCB](https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CTS/pages/1030848709/How+To+Reboot+a+Base+Device).
    2. If none of the above fixes the issue, **replace the SRS**.  
  
8. If PSoC download was unsuccessful, perform the following steps to determine if the the SRS is powered off or offline.
9. If confirmed, complete the CRM resolution fields using the table below. If issue persists, engage a senior member of your team for further guidance before escalating.

## Cause

---

Misconfigured device  
Mismatched software versions  
Faulty cabling  
Faulty RCB RS port  
Faulty device

## Investigational summary fields

---

| If **correcting ****configuration of** **GRS5 or SRS** resolved your issue, use these values to close the case |  |
| Main - Sub Assembly | Problem/Resolution Reason |
| Navicare Nurse Call (NNC) : Enterprise Configuration Tool (ECT) Voalte Nurse Call : Enterprise Configuration Tool (ECT) | Device Settings Misconfigured |

| If **correcting mismatched device**** software version** resolved your issue, use these values to close the case |  |
| Main - Sub Assembly | Problem/Resolution Reason |
| Navicare Nurse Call (NNC) : GRS5 or SRS Voalte Nurse Call : GRS5 or SRS | Software Version Mismatch |

| If **correcting device cabling **resolved your issue, use these values to close the case |  |
| Main - Sub Assembly | Problem/Resolution Reason |

comment_summary: A code blue button reportedly had to be pressed very hard before it would alert, and the switch was returned for engineering investigation. In the lab the returned switch was fitted to an RCB in place of an identical switch and placed and cancelled calls normally under normal push pressure. root_cause_summary: The switch was most likely damaged due to improper insertion of the PSU, which caused physical damage to PSU slot A.
investigation_details: 1. Confirmed the switch failed to load RedBoot despite receiving power.
2. Captured logs for vendor analysis (Rubytech).
3. Conducted physical inspection of hardware; identified damage inside PSU slot A.
4. Performed controlled test by relocating PSU to slot B; switch booted successfully.
5. Correlated findings — slot A damage prevents proper PSU operation, slot B functions normally.

**Conclusion:** Damage to PSU slot A (likely caused by improper PSU insertion) prevented normal boot sequence.
troubleshooting_steps: 1. Powered on the switch — observed that it received power but failed to boot RedBoot.
2. Collected and forwarded system logs to Rubytech for vendor review.
3. Inspected PSU slots and found visible damage in slot A.
4. Relocated the PSU from slot A to slot B.
5. Verified the switch booted successfully and operated as expected.

**Result:** Switch restored to normal operation by using PSU slot B.
troubleshooting_results: * Switch was confirmed to receive power but failed to boot RedBoot.
* Physical inspection revealed visible damage to PSU slot A.
* Relocating the PSU to slot B allowed the switch to boot successfully and operate as expected.

summary: Gen 3 PoE switch uplink being shut off due to bdpu packets when STP disabled on uplink port
description: Customer: Mt Siani West 605106 – IE Discovered during implementation 
IE Contact: @Hennon, Thomas 
There are three Gen 3 PoE switches being implemented at a customer site. Each Gen 3 PoE is one it’s own (no stack) and has a single uplink to customer on Port 25. Out of box defaults are MSTP enabled on 1-24 and disabled on 25 and 26. Each switch is configured in this manner. 
Whenever the a switch boots, the customer side detects bpdu packets and shuts the port off. Once the customer reenables the port no further issue occurs until the Gen 3 PoE switch is rebooted. Then rinse/repeat.

root_cause_summary: The issue was caused by a firmware defect in the Gen 3 PoE switch software that allowed BPDU/STP packets to be transmitted during switch initialization, even when spanning tree had been explicitly disabled on the uplink port using the no spanning-tree configuration. As a result, customer switches configured with BPDU Guard interpreted the unexpected STP traffic as a loop-protection event and automatically disabled the connected uplink port.
investigation_details: See comments
troubleshooting_steps: Reboot PoE switch that is configured with spanning-tree disabled on port 25
troubleshooting_results: Cisco switch will shut uplink port.
rca_review_comments: _We observed that STP packets are transmitted during switch initialization._

_This issue has been logged in our Bugzilla under issue #25664._

_When the command "no spanning-tree" is applied to a port, it is intended to disable the STP function on that port completely, which means that the port should neither transmit nor receive STP packets._

_Based on our test results, the current behavior indicates that the STP mechanism is not properly handled by the software during switch initialization._

When measured, the PWRGD# Pin10 failed to output. This PWRGD# pin is the Active Low Power Good Output that signals the DC/DC converter and allows for the power supply operation of 36V to start. This pin is basically the POE switch that turns ON at approximately 50-52Vdc. The defective U1_POE (PN: LTC4264) was replaced and the RCB3 POE switch was able to turn ON and supply power to the board. The FCT test was executed and successfully passed all hardware tests. root_cause_summary: The 4 RCB3's that powered up fine were probably wrongly diagnosed by the installer and the failure was probably due to a bad Cat6 ethernet cable connection.  The RCB3's with the U1 and U2 failures may have failed because of a power surge on the POE Cat6 ethernet cable.  The POE switch may have been powered up when the RCB3s were  connected.  The POE switch should be powered down when connecting devices.  The Dart failure may have been a hardware failure of the module, with no root cause.
investigation_details: There were 8 RCB3's received. 4 of them power up fine and were tested on DFCT and there was no fault found. One had the C13_POE broken off the PCB, as reported by the installer.  This failure could have occurred at the manufacturer or by the installer because of rough handling.  One has a U1_POE short. Another has a U2_POE failure. The last one has a failed DART. This DART was investigated and found to be defective (Hardware failure).
verification_summary: Device replacement resolved issue.    
No corrective actions were identified; therefore, closing RCA.
rca_review_comments: The 4 RCB3's that powered up fine were probably wrongly diagnosed by the installer.  The other 4 each had a different failure.  The RCB3's with the U1 and U2 failures may have failed because of a power surge on the POE Cat6 ethernet cable.  The POE switch may have been powered up when the RCB3s were connected which can cause this type failure.  The POE switch should be powered down when connecting devices.  The Dart failure may have been a hardware failure of the module, with no root cause.  C13_POE broken off the PCB, as reported by the installer could have occurred at the manufacturer or by the installer because of rough handling.

case_summary.summary: A rounding due light stayed stuck for almost two hours, with the reminder service showing inconsistencies compared to a sister site's server. Investigation traced the cause to a lack of server hardware and an SQL monitoring service bogging down the database, and the fix was to eliminate the SQL monitor service and add hardware to the DB server. The site confirmed they were problem-free after the fix was implemented.
case_summary.reported_issue: A rounding reminder light was stuck and would not clear for an extended period.
case_summary.product: SQL Server database / rounding reminder service (Nurse Call)
case_summary.actions_taken: Disabled and re-enabled ASBC, which did not clear the stuck call
Reviewed logs and found pubsub and reminder service inconsistencies versus a sister site sharing the SQL server
Restarted supervisor, pubsub, and reminder services
Opened an RCA and temporarily disabled rounding at the site's request
Had the site stagger database backup jobs and disable the SQLExternalMonitoring scanning process
Re-enabled rounding reminders and monitored for recurrence
case_summary.resolution: Eliminated the SQL monitor service and added hardware to the database server, after which the site confirmed no further stuck rounding calls.
case_summary.status: resolved
case_summary.key_points: RA_Did_same_issue_occur is Yes, indicating this had happened before
Core issue was confirmed in SQL error logs and reminder service logs

summary: 3rd Fl Med Surg - Ent unit - Rounding Timers Do Not Clear
description: Account Name | Baptist Medical Center Clay

Account Number | **4837124**

Nursecall version | 4.0.402.0

* Rounding due calls types getting stuck and unable to be canceled from the room via the audio station or by locating.
* not every room every time just once or twice a day
* reminder logs showing error for failure to update SQL
* calls clear by bouncing the reminder service or by clearing the calls from the DB manually
root_cause_summary: Customer running monitoring tool that was dragging down the disk reads for sql server.
investigation_details: So we are going to need some help from the customer on this. I hav e attached several screenshots to this ticket as evidence for the customer. The service logs indicate we are getting time outs. When I checked the database server I found IO latency in the SQL Server logs and also a bunch of errors in the event viewer logs. So I checked to make sure the db server was setup correctly to rule out possible bottles necks as recommended by Microsoft.   
The data and log file for the databases are on drives  
Memory settings are set appropriately   
Tempdb files have been created one per core  
Tempdb file size has been set to equal amounts.  
Further research indicated this error can be caused by a few things which is where we need to get the customer db and network people to resolve the initial issues. Microsoft mentioned that SQL Server could be spawning more requests than the IO could handle. The recommendation was to check the IO subsystem driver configuration for a possible misconfiguration.   
Also looking at dm_io_virtual_file_stats the msdb and tempdb have high IO latency. I looked the backups and it seems that all the log files are running at the same time which is hammering write latency for the msdb database. Microsoft recommends staggering the database backups so they are not running all together but one after the other.  
Looking into the dm_db_session_space_usage view I found that there is an external monitoring process that is hammering the tempdb that is causing the IO latency. Its called “SQLExternalMonitoring” This process is creating almost 50GB in the Tempdb and creating excessive disk IO issues.  
This is probably why we are getting timeouts when updating the calls for rounding. We need the customer to stagger the backups and to turn off their monitoring tool. I have included screenshots in the attachment  section for reference. Please let me know if you have any questions.  
Additional info:  
The tempdb is being beat up by   
Azure SQL IaaS monitoring (SqlServerExtension.Service.exe) it is maintaining long-lived shared-memory sessions that are heavily allocating TempDB. It has had an open connection since “2025-11-02 00:32:10.430“. See screenshot.
troubleshooting_steps: * confirmed the consistent error in the reminder logs for the call failure to update
* bouncing reminder service temporarily alleviates issue
troubleshooting_results: issue keeps reoccurring
verification_summary: Site IT made the recommended changes, no further issues reported.

* Clicked Rounding Reminder, it went to hourglass image then stated that a timeout occurred
* Restarted Gateway, PatientStaff, and Integration services; timeout message persists- VNC'd to the GRS5 for Exam 02 and the same issue persists, timeout message keeps coming up when trying to initiate rounding

root_cause_summary: The majority of the issues of the reminder service not working / reminder button presses unresponsive were caused by:  
1) Uncaught exceptions on action blocks  
2) The grs-5 getting out of synchronization with the reminder service.  This would cause the grs-5 to send a completion message when the reminder was on hold.  The reminder service ignored this message.  
Fixes for these issues plus other corner cases were implemented.
investigation_details: We are able to reproduce several reminders defects in the lab - mostly reminders timing out - no longer responding to button pushes on the GRS-5.

We found multiple software defects in the reminder service and reminders gateway plugin:  
1.The gateway plugin was sending back to back reminder completion and reminder running messages to the grs-5's.  If the order of these messages got swapped, it caused a non responsive reminder icon. We eliminated the completion message in this case to eliminate the race.  
2.We added a try / catch / error log around all reminders processing occurring on action blocks.  Some processing was already protected but not all.  This is the cause of sites where reminders as a whole feature is no longer working until the reminder service is restarted.  
3.We eliminated the restart of elapsed on demand timers on reminder service restart.  This eliminated non-starting on demand reminders.  
4.We fixed cases of out of order message completion from the grs-5's.  If the reminder service receives a completion message when the reminder is on hold, it will now treat the message as an off-hold message instead of discarding it.  
5.We fixed a null reference exception that could kill an action block.  
6.We increased the maximum message received size for staff movement and location events.  
7.David G. corrected the scheduler type.  
8.We fixed code that was firing extremely rapid, repetitive sql statements.  
9.We fixed a bug in the reminders editing screen that could leave reminders in an incorrect state.
rca_review_comments: Defect logged and triaged.

summary: Reminders showing overdue despite being reset
description: North Florida (HCA) enabled reminders today to test them after being upgraded to 3.9.201.

We found that, in some cases, the reminder state in Status Board and the Reminders Admin web page would change to an 'Overdue' status despite being reset in the room.

These are visible in Status Board as reminders that are Overdue but do not have an active Round Due call.

Upon the next Reminder state change for the room, the Overdue status is removed and the Reminder begins appearing as expected in Status Board.

All other Reminder functionality has been tested and is working as expected.  HCA has elected to keep the Reminders feature turned off until the display issue in Status Board is resolved.
comment_summary: Rounding reminders were displaying as overdue on Status Board even after being reset, and refreshing Status Board did not correct the customer's case. Websocket captures showed reminder state change, hold change and completion messages arriving out of order through pubsub, revealing a race condition between the state change and hold change messages, and database task instance history initially appeared to show two interleaved task instances until a re-query ordered by insertion id showed the ordering artifact came from identical timestamps. Later testing on a test environment with a reminder service build that published to neither pubsub nor RabbitMQ reproduced the customer's exact symptoms - reminders staying black instead of turning orange, counting up in orange rather than showing red 'overdue', and correcting only after a manual Status Board page refresh - while the polling-based reminders admin page stayed correct, showing that reminder updates were not reaching Status Board. The thread concludes the fault was in the pubsub layer, which was removed from Nurse Call in version 4.1.00 and higher in favour of RabbitMQ messaging.

comment_summary: A site sporadically could not call a particular Linq device: Nurse Call to Nurse Call audio worked, Linq to Linq audio worked, and other stations could call the same badge, but one specific station to that Linq badge failed until the audio station was rebooted. Diagnostic steps were supplied to run fs_cli.exe -p voalte against the FreeSWITCH service on the Nurse Call Enterprise server to see whether RTC was routing the audio setup request to Nurse Call at all, with SIP-level tracing as the next step if it was. Because audio paths within Nurse Call, within Linq, and between them all worked, and because rebooting the audio station resolved it by forcing a re-download of staff wireless configuration, the theory settled on the audio station holding incorrect dialing information for that staff member, as happens when a staff member is assigned a Linq badge while CSA configuration in ECT is incorrect, since wireless device configuration updates do not trigger a staff mobile device assignment update. The site reported no known Wireless Device changes in ECT near the event, Gateway logs were not set to Verbose so data was limited, the issue was never reproducible, and no further occurrences were reported after an upgrade.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
This change affected behavior in state transitions for WCTP and CSA Mobile Device providers for Messaging Service as it pertains to the propagation of Nurse Call call status changes.   
Before  this change, a running notification procedure that observed a Nurse Call status change for the call associated with a notification procedure would not send notified devices an update regarding the state of the call.    
After the change, a message status update is provide to indicate a Nurse Call has transitions from New to Assigned and eventually to Canceled.  New and Cancel were already supported.  
The triggers associated with the revised behavior include the following:

* A user at a Nurse Call console answers the call and puts it on the wait list
* A mobile device user Accepts a notification and triggers the transition of the call to the wait list  
   A mobile device user calls back into the room based on a notification without the 'CancelOnHangup' setting enabled triggering a transition of the call to the wait list.  
  Impact Assessment:  
  NCP - Notification Procedures - Trivial  
  Platform Impact:  
  N/A  
  Date - AUG/18/2026  
  Attendees - David Girardeau(Development Engineering), Kate Papalava ( QE Lead), Rajini Choudhary (Quality Engineering) and Bhargav Bhalodia (Quality Engineering),   
  Minutes - Since the listed PF NCP - Notification Procedures is set to Trivial the team decided the new Test listed under Direct Tests should be sufficient to test the changes made to the code and the Test's listed under Regression are enough to regress the changes made to setting "Enable Clear Message ". Dev confirmed that State machine is not changed and it does not impact the origin where the accept action is performed from. Code changes impact the WCTP and Voalte LINQ. Call coming out of Reminder has different logic and this change will not impact that scenario.
steps_taken: Place a Normal Call.  
Wait for the 1st escalation.  
Wait for 2nd escalation.  
Answer the call from Nurse call (Console).  
Hang up the call and select Yes to the "needs more help" question.
actual_results: Call/Alert ‘END’ status of call being answered at Nurse call is **NOT** propagated to Linq devices.
expected_results: Call/Alert ‘END’ status of call being answered at Nurse call is propagated to Linq devices.
work_around: Dismiss alert on Linq device screen (clears stale alert for Linq user but does not address root problem)

root_cause_summary: I looks like when a staff logs in to a scotty badge CSA updates the practitioner bumping its version. Nurse Call's practitioner is now at a lower version. Nurse Call is detecting what it thinks is an unhealthy CSA via health check and triggering a reconciliation of the data. Since CSA practitioner is at a higher version, Nurse Call updates the staff record and nulls out the foreign key to the application user table (username/domain)
investigation_details: Found that there were active (DeletedOnUtc was null) staff in the ApplicationUser table that were not being returned by Staff_ListActiveWithExternalIDs_55 which is what is used to compare to the LDAP returned list to determine if staff are to be added, etc.

summary: TrunkAccessDialString column size in database functions causes exceptions and prevents Voalte Admin login
description: While logged into the Voalte Linq badge, if you also try to login to Voalte Admin Client, an exception caused by the database function NavicareEnterprise.PC.Staff_GetByUsernameDomainId appears in the PatientStaffService logs. This is because the TrunkAccessDialString column size (20) specified in the function is different from its column size (256) in MobileDeviceProvider when that table is joined. As a result, any TrunkAccessDialString length greater than 20 will be truncated and cause an exception.
impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
The database column size of the MobileDeviceProvider's TrunkAccessDialString was increased to 256. The login process for a staff, executes a stored procedure which joins to the MobileDeviceProvider table to include mobile device information if the staff has a mobile device assignment. The stored procedure was not changed to increase the TrunkAccessDialString and was still designating the size to be 20. This caused the stored procedure to throw an exception which resulted in a failed login. The fix was to increase the size of the TrunkAcessDialString to 256.

NCP - Authentication - trivial

N/A

summary: When a Duress Alert is placed from a Linq badge it appears to send the alert two times in rapid succession
description: At Carson Valley Health where we are piloting Linq with NC 4.1.210, when a Duress Alert is placed from a Linq badge it appears to send 2 identical alerts in rapid succession to Nurse Call. It appears that the 1st alert is written to the DB but the 2nd alert is not.

The MessageServiceHost log shows we are receiving and processing both alerts, resulting in 2 calls sent to the Wireless Provider ( Voalte Mobile via WAVE, in this case).

The 1st Duress Alert gets assigned a valid Notification id and Callid. i.e. notification id “5DF4E01” and Callid “384846”, which is seen in the attached logs.

The 2nd alert however is assigned a notification id of “1” and Callid of “0”.

The end result is that both alerts are sent within the same second to the Wireless Provider.

After speaking and reviewing this with David Girardeau and Alec Kaufman, they believe this is a defect.

I’ve attached the MessagingServiceHost log as well as the HillRom.LocatingServiceHost log for the test call captured.

Additionally there is s spreadsheet that shows the calls in question filtered out.
comment_summary: A Duress Alert placed from a Linq badge appears to be sent twice in rapid succession. Analysis of the logs shows two Duress events arriving roughly 75ms apart for the same location, with the Locating Service logs lacking detail and the Message Service logs showing a CallID of 0 on the second event, suggesting the second Duress published over RabbitMQ was associated with a database INSERT failure that did not stop delivery because of behavior added years ago after a transaction log overflow stopped PubSub processing. The thread reasons that the second Duress likely arrived while the first was still being processed, preventing the duplicate-detection logic from catching it, and notes that Messaging Service determines alert uniqueness from the CallID rather than the CallGuid, so two different CallIDs were treated as two different notifications. A further Duress test was captured with the HillRom.LocatingServiceHost log set to trace, and the thread raises a possible relationship to a more extreme case at another site covered by a separate defect.

root_cause_summary: during a single button press event of any button press combination, the system by design should not be sending more than 1 event per button press event. 

However in the listed affects version builds the customer was able to perform a workflow that resulted in a single button press event generating 64 button press events.
investigation_details: See comments
troubleshooting_steps: 1. Setup Duress Alert (Call Type 115) in VNC > ECT to send out to Excel WAVE. 
2. Notification Procedure used is the same as that used to for sending all other alerts to WAVE.
3. Tested Duress Alert from Linq badge. WAVE received 2 alerts from VNC.
4. Check MessagingServiceHost log and found both Alerts notifications recieved and processed.
5. Created a new Notification Procedure for the Duress Alert that sends to WAVE with Send Once checked. WAVE received 2 alerts from VNC.
6. Check MessagingServiceHost log and found both Alerts notifications recieved and processed.
7. Created new CallType with same values as default Duress Alert.
8. Set new Duress Alert Call Type to be sent with button press on Linq badge.
9. Tested new Duress Alert Call Type from Linq badge pointing to new Send Once Notification Procedure for the Duress Alert. WAVE received 2 alerts from VNC.
10. Check MessagingServiceHost log and found both Alerts notifications recieved and processed.
troubleshooting_results: Regardless of creating new Notification Procedures and Call Type. Each test resulted in 2 Duress Alerts being sent from VNC to WAVE.

Noted in log that the findings that were posted in the Description above in this RCA

summary: Button press events from Linq and PL do not generate alerts in Nurse Call after specific locating vendor configuration changes in ECT
description: When existing Linq or PL tags are assigned, and then PL is un-licensed and re-licensed, Nurse Call can fail to show alerts related to a button press event because it associates the event with a tag from an unlicensed vendor.



When a button press event is received from Linq or Precision Locating, Nurse Call checks its list of devices to find a corresponding BadgeName. BadgeName duplicates with the same vendor ID are allowed. Every time a current vendor is removed and then re-applied in ECT, a new Vendor record with a new Vendor ID is created, so without screening out the BadgeNames for inactive vendors, a button press event can be associated with a BadgeName for an inactive vendor.
impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:

summary: NC - Freeswitch - Avaya Callback not working
description: I logged in to the customer site, bumped up the message service log and watched for calls.

 The VoIP service configuration shows as per Config.jpg: Which is as expected.

This means that the alias we send should start with a 7 and the extension should be only 5 digits in length with a lifetime of 60 minutes.

This is what should limit us to extension ranges of 70000 - 79999

 In the Message service logs I was seeing that we were actually generating 6 digit aliases as per Old Message.jpg 

This along with the “21” prefix we prepend would result in us sending 8 digits as opposed to 7 digits. It is likely this would break callback because the Avaya is looking for only 7 digits.

 Because the VoIP service is responsible for generating the aliases I restarted the VoIP server service.

 The result is that we are now back to sending only 5 digits for the alias as per New message.jpg

It’s likely that callback is working again assuming there were no changes made to the Avaya callback rules

I then reached out to a colleague, the one on vacation, and he said he would look at the code.

 He did that and unfortunately identified a bug. He stated that 1 specific change is needed in one line of the code to correct it.

While the restart likely resolved the problem for now, as soon as the aliases hit 79999 the system will start generating 6 digit aliases again.

 Unfortunately because a code change is needed we will need to Nurse Call hotfix this or put it in the next release.
root_cause_summary: In thee code, the  root cause issue relates tot he interpretation of ‘Length’ in the appsettings.json file.  One place in the code interprets the length as the prefix+digits.  The other is just digits.  The prefix+digits interpretation is the correct one as the Length was intended to represent the full length of the alias including the prefix.

summary: NC - Freeswitch - Avaya Callback not working - Inconsistent extension length
description: In the code, the  root cause issue relates tot he interpretation of ‘Length’ in the appsettings.json file.  One place in the code interprets the length as the prefix+digits.  The other is just digits.  The prefix+digits interpretation is the correct one as the Length was intended to represent the full length of the alias including the prefix.

To force alignment, a single line in the VoIP Service code needs to be amended.  Basically, it is a change to **line 16 of EndpointAliasManager.cs** to read as follows:

```
Limit = (int)Math.Pow(10, length-1);
```

The current implementation for ‘Limit' utilizes the full length.  If the ‘length’ is used instead of ‘length-1’, the ‘Limit’ is calculated as 100000 instead of 10000.  The 'Limit’ value is later used in the code to calculate a modulus of a counter as LastValue%Limit for the alias.  With the current implementation and a Length of 5, the modulus doesn’t revert back to 0 until 999999 is reached.  prefix+digits would result in a value like 799999 (6 digits).

One might think, then, that it would be as simple as just using a Length of 4 rather than 5.  The problem with that thought process relates to how the alias is padded with zeros.  If the LastValue is 1 and the Length is 5, we want an alias of 70001.  If Length is changed to 4, we get a value like 7001 which is wrong.
impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Due to a calculation error, the alias values for wireless notifications were allowed to exceed the range from 70000-79999.  Instead of rolling back to 0000 after 9999, the code was letting 9999 to go to 10000 and continue to 99999 before rolling back to 0000.    
The fix involves adding unit tests to ensure that the Length (5 characters) is maintained when iterating through the full collection of possible alias extension values + 1.  In other words, the 10000th aliased extension must be 70000 rather than 710000.  
The Unit Test is located in the zep-voip GitHub repo (Voip Service) in Test.Voip->TestVoipAlias.cs->TestVoipAliasRollover().  The test does the following:

* Loop through 10000 alias values
* Ensure that the generated alias value matches the expected length (5 characters)
* Ensure that the alias prefix (7) is the first character of ever alias
* Ensure the first alias after the rollover is zero.  
  Impact Assessment:  
  NCP - Mobile Device Support - WCTP Voalte Mobile - Trivial  
  Platform Impact:  
  N/A  
  Product Labeling Impact:  
  N/A

  Date:  7/JAN/2026  
  Attendees - David Girardeau (Development Engineering), Kate Papalava (Quality Engineering)

When new RCB’s were programmed to replace them, they received extension 10000, 10001, and 10002 when the reality is the customers next available extension is 12468 (voip_entdb.png). comment_summary: After an upgrade to 4.1.101 from a pre-4.1 version, newly created devices receive VOIP extensions starting at the beginning of the VOIP extension range, colliding with extensions that already exist. The thread establishes that the extensions already exist in the NavicareEnterprise database while the HRCWSExtensionManager database is brand new and empty, so the ExtensionManager service hands out extensions from the start of the range with no knowledge of the pre-existing legacy extensions. A workaround using ECT to change the VOIP extension range resyncs the two databases but loses paging groups, and a PowerShell script was proposed to sync the ExtensionManager database with NavicareEnterprise during legacy upgrades. A later comment reports a related case where a replacement RCB picked up a temporary VOIP extension already in use, requiring a manual database update, and asks for a more reliable mechanism.

comment_summary: The thread investigates ECT creating duplicate VoIP extensions. Early suspicion fell on the Asterisk.GetNextAvailEndpoint scalar function in the HRCWSExtensionManager database returning extensions already in use, possibly via asterisk.RegistrationEndpoint_Save. Analysis showed that when a device created without a serial number is later serialized, the configuration service DeviceDAL.cs Delete() method calls VoipExtensionManager.DeleteRegistrationEndpoint(voipExtension), removing rows from ps_endpoints, ps_auths and ps_aors while the extension remains in use in the NavicareEnterprise database, so the extension manager reissues it. A minor-impact fix was developed to check the local database before deleting an extension, the safety score was reduced from 100 to 0, and formal testing completed with nc_pd_release_4.1.101_2.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Configuration Service - file ConfigurationService/DataAccess/Device/DeviceDal.cs - in method Delete(), before deleting a voip extension  
from the Extension Manager Database, check to see if the voip extension is still in use in the NavicareEnterprise database.  
If the voip extension is still assigned, do not delete it from the Extension Manager database.   This keeps the two databases in synch  
and prevents duplicate voip extensions from being issued.  
Before: duplicate voip extensions are issued.  
After: No duplicate voip extensions are issued.

Impact Assessment:  
NCP - Configuration - Organization and Devices - Trivial

Platform Impact:  
Windows

Regression Meeting:  
Date:  04/SEP/2024  
Attendees - Nick Jenkins (Quality Engineer), Clifford Feather (Development)  
Minutes - Testing indicated below was accepted without changes.

Additional Software Components:  
N/A
steps_taken: 1\. Create 4 new rooms, each with a grs7, do not assign serial numbers to the devices, do not use similar rooms feature yet.  
2\. Create primary console that is also the nursing unit controller for the nursing unit and save.  
3\. Add serial numbers to rcb3 devices and grs10h device and save.    
4\.  Add serial numbers to the grs7 devices and save.

Note: a query can be run against the table asterisk.ps_endpoints in the HRCWSExtensionManager database  (select \* from asterisk.ps_endpoints) at this point in the reproduction to verify the issue is occuring.  The ps_endpoints table will have 0 rows.  It should have a row for each voip extension in use in the navicare database  (select \* from v_voipextensions).

5\. Right click room 4, select create similar rooms.  Make 4 new rooms but do not serialize. click save.

Update July 9, 2024 - It is not necessary to use the create similar rooms feature to reproduce this issue.  The issue is reproduced when rcb(3) boards are saved without a serial number.  If these boards are created manually, one at a time, without using create similar rooms, the issue still occurs.  
Also, if 8 actual or simulated devices are not available as were used in the reproduction steps , fewer devices may be used.  
The issue occurs when unserialized devices are saved, then those devices are given a serial number, and saved, then more devices are added after the second save.
actual_results: The newly created rooms have duplicate VOIP addresses.  Results vary each time this test is run.
expected_results: No duplicate VOIP extensions.
work_around: From the field - the 3CX import file is split into smaller pieces and the duplicate is found and fixed.

root_cause_summary: Defect against requirements.

No additional investigation is required for this record, as case is over a year old, and unlikely additional information will be available; as such, the record will be closed.  Reference CONC11778
investigation_details: **Why does a Disconnected Switch call get placed?**  The room is configured in ECT but physically not connected

**Why is the switch not physically connected?** Staging the environment, therefore the configured switch needs to be disabled.

**Why does the configured switch need to be disabled?** In order to get rid of the 'disconnected switch' call that is alarming 

 

Scenario:

 

1. You have a room configured in ECT with a bath switch configured but not connected.
2. To stop the bath switch from alarming you disable the bath switch in ECT.
3. With the switch still disconnected, when you enable it in ECT, you don’t get a Disconnected Switch alert.
4. You have to delete the switch, save the configuration and then add the switch back in, and only then you will get a Disconnect Switch alert.

Expectations: the 'disconnect switch' call should display in required places (active calls list in ECT, Staff Console etc.) when the configured switch is re-enabled and not physically connected.

 

We believe that this is a defect against an existing product requirement.

root_cause_summary: Customer-site network/PoE port issue affecting device connectivity and operation. When tested on bench was not able to reproduce the issue. No hardware fault identified.
investigation_details: Customer initially reported that the GRS10H was unable to establish audio and displayed the error message “Temporary problem placing call please try again later.” The customer replaced the device locally in an attempt to resolve the issue. During the on-site follow-up, the replacement device was then found to be unable to obtain an IP address. Once the port issue was addressed on the customer side, the replacement device was able to obtain network connectivity, be configured, and operate successfully. The original returned device was later evaluated in R&D and no fault was reproduced. The unit configured normally and was able to place and receive calls on the bench.
troubleshooting_steps: FCT Logs Attached in the comments. FCT passed for all the hardware tests on this device.

R&D Investigation:

* Reviewed the reported issue on primary GRS10 at 10.23.186.207 after the customer observed the message “Temporary problem placing call, please try again later” when answering calls.
* Confirmed the customer had already verified all RCB ports and did not identify any port-level fault.
* Checked the GRS10 for active alarms, alerts, or other visible fault indications at the time of investigation.
* Attempted to validate the issue condition, but the behavior was not reproducible during review.
* Bench-tested the returned original device in R&D by configuring the unit and verifying successful call placement and call reception.

Investigation from Field Notes and Service Engineering Team: (As per the Salesforce and Conversation with the Field Technician)

* Reviewed field service communication and technician notes from the on-site investigation.
* Verified that after the customer replaced the unit, the replacement device was initially unable to obtain an IP address.
* Confirmed with the field technician that on-site IT and FST investigated the connected port and PoE/network path.
troubleshooting_results: The returned original GRS10H device did not have any fault during the bench testing. It was configured on the ECT Server. Same firmware was used on RCB3 and GRS7 as that of GRS10H. The device was able to be configured and was able to place and receive calls in the lab environment. When the hospital received the new device, it initially could not obtain the IP Address until the network port issue was cleared by the Hospital IT Team. After the port/network condition was corrected, the replacement device was configured and used successfully. These findings do not support a hardware failure of the returned original device.

root_cause_summary: The 4 RCB3's that powered up fine were probably wrongly diagnosed by the installer and the failure was probably due to a bad Cat6 ethernet cable connection.  The RCB3's with the U1 and U2 failures may have failed because of a power surge on the POE Cat6 ethernet cable.  The POE switch may have been powered up when the RCB3s were  connected.  The POE switch should be powered down when connecting devices.  The Dart failure may have been a hardware failure of the module, with no root cause.
investigation_details: There were 8 RCB3's received. 4 of them power up fine and were tested on DFCT and there was no fault found. One had the C13_POE broken off the PCB, as reported by the installer.  This failure could have occurred at the manufacturer or by the installer because of rough handling.  One has a U1_POE short. Another has a U2_POE failure. The last one has a failed DART. This DART was investigated and found to be defective (Hardware failure).
verification_summary: Device replacement resolved issue.    
No corrective actions were identified; therefore, closing RCA.
rca_review_comments: The 4 RCB3's that powered up fine were probably wrongly diagnosed by the installer.  The other 4 each had a different failure.  The RCB3's with the U1 and U2 failures may have failed because of a power surge on the POE Cat6 ethernet cable.  The POE switch may have been powered up when the RCB3s were connected which can cause this type failure.  The POE switch should be powered down when connecting devices.  The Dart failure may have been a hardware failure of the module, with no root cause.  C13_POE broken off the PCB, as reported by the installer could have occurred at the manufacturer or by the installer because of rough handling.

comment_summary: Code Blue pull switches were reported as failing, with the inner red plunger becoming stuck so the system does not place a code blue when the lever is pulled. Twenty-five switches of different revisions were received and tested, five of which failed out of the box with the same sticking micro-switch behavior, recorded on video; the micro-switches recovered shortly after the lever was pulled, but sticking in brand-new and one to two year old units was flagged as a concern. Bench work found the issue mitigated by disassembling and reassembling a switch with its original parts, and also by fitting parts from a known-good switch, suggesting something may not be seated correctly during assembly and causing excess friction, confirmed on two switches. The supplier investigation could not reproduce the failure mode and identified material fatigue as a potential root cause leading to reduced spring force over time, with no material, process or environmental nonconformances found; a design enhancement request NCBL-4156 was created and the issue will be monitored through complaint trending.

root_cause_summary: The material fatigue results in insufficient spring force to disengage the switch, causing the button to remain stuck.
investigation_details: The issue is confirmed, 3 out of 4 switches received have the stuck micro switches.

The lever mechanism keeps the microswitch (with the red plastic cap) continuously engaged. It is believed that the microswitch used in this design is not intended to remain in a permanently depressed state. Over time, the rubber or silicone actuator material loses elasticity due to constant compression, reducing its ability to return to its original shape and release the button.

 Comparing a good switch to the stuck one showed a noticeable reduction in the bad switch's spring force.

It’s possible that the tolerances have changed, causing the lever to push the microswitch with excessive force, jamming it inside the case. Later, I compared the force applied by failed devices versus known good ones, and it appears that the good devices are much gentler on the microswitches.

* Customer says that a Code Blue in the CVIR did not go to the PBX

* These are Code Blue levers not A/S
* VNC into GRS-10 for Cardia Cath

* Dan said he did not test every room but he tested most of them
* We tested in Lab05 and IRLab01
* Had him pull the lever in Lab01; no call appeared
* Changed the config from Supervised to Standard; no change
* Changed it back to Supervised
* Had him put the Switch from Lab05 in Lab01; Call showed up
* Had him put the switch from Lab01 in Lab05; Call did not work
* This issue appears to be a problem with the physical switches themselves
* Customer asked we send him 10 Code Blue pull levers and an FST on site to replace and test them
* 7/29/19
* Customer states that a live, non-test code blue call was placed, and that the call blue switch did nothing- did not notify primary console, did not place call.
* Customer states that hospital personnel then used a phone in the room to contact medical response team
* Says that patient was not adversely affected.

root_cause_summary: The age of the P2520B06 switches was a definite factor in the failure of switches.  Some had a stuck plunger and would not release the contacts due to  failure on the rubber gasket around the switch plunger.  Others had tarnished switch contacts.  These switches all had a 2010 date code.  The HR Help Center says under Cautions: “The hospital should perform periodic testing and maintenance of the code blue and emergency calls, to ensure the system is working properly.”  If this testing had been done then these failures would have been found early and replaced before a crisis could occur.
investigation_details: See comments.
rca_review_comments: Hardware age and wear, not a software defect. Of 26 returned legacy Code Blue switches (P2520B06, 2010 date code), 9 failed (4 hard failures, 5 intermittent) because of the small PCB-mounted internal switch: stuck plungers from gasket failure and tarnished contacts, made worse by Code Blue switches rarely being used. 17 worked. None of the 40 returned new-style switches (P2520NNC2B06, 2018) failed; that design no longer uses the internal switch. No fluid intrusion was found. A live Code Blue failed to call, and staff used the room phone; the patient wasn't harmed. Corrective action: replace legacy P2520B06 switches with P2520NNC2B06; replacements and an FST were sent to the site. Reinforce to customers the Help Center caution that Code Blue and emergency call switches must be tested and maintained regularly.

description: When there are a large amount of staff added Admin Client is experiencing slow performance and UI delays when loading staff data, editing profiles, and interacting with search. Issue is reproducible across browsers and on the server.   
  
  
Staff List Loading Delay:  
Verified a consistent delay of approximately 7–15 seconds when loading the staff member list. During this period, the "Add Staff" button remains active and clickable, which is contrary to expected behavior for Staff Sync customers. Once the staff list fully loads, the button correctly transitions to a disabled state.



Staff Profile Interaction Lag:  
Upon selecting a staff member, the profile pop-up exhibits a 7–15 second delay before rendering. Subsequent interactions within the pop-up, such as editing roles or home units, incur an additional 15–20 second delay per action. Save and cancel operations within the modal also experience a 4–7 second delay.



Search Bar Input Lag:  
Staff reported that initiating a search by typing a staff member’s name immediately after login slightly reduces the overall delay. However, even with early input, there remains a 4–6 second lag between keystroke entry and character display in the search field.



Browser Freezing:  
Confirmed intermittent freezing of the browser during usage of the Admin Client. Freezing are more common at larger site.



Environment Validation:

The issue was reproduced in both Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge browsers.  
The same behavior was successfully duplicated on the server environment, confirming that the issue is not isolated to a specific client machine or browser.

summary: Voalte Admin Client Not Loading or has inconsistent load times when opening Admin Client tabs
description: * Nurse Call version is 4.1.100
* Client PCs have inconsistent load times when opening Admin Client tabs
* We tested two client PCs, one with 1ms latency and one with \~20ms latency

    * Client with 1ms latency loaded in 10 seconds
    * Client with 20ms latency loaded in 1.5-2 minutes
    
* Penn Presby has 2581 active staff records in the DB
* Upon opening Admin Client's Staff tab, 3 DB queries are run per staff record, resulting in about 7500 individual queries being run each time the tab is loaded

    * This was captured via SQL profiler
    
* By comparison, a 4.0.404 system with 9999 test staff records captures the same information from the DB in about 20 queries

    * The optimizations for Smart Client were discovered and implemented after investigation of RCA-575
    * These optimizations appear to be missing in 4.1.100
    
* More detail in the attached txt document

Intermittent (appears to be latency dependent)

Ran through SQL profiler tests while client PCs connected to Admin Client.
root_cause_summary: Large number of sql statements issued when data could be retrieved with a much smaller number of statements.
investigation_details: Oliver Thompson supplied a wireshark capture which showed the large number of sql statements generated by loading the staff admin tab.  Code debugging revealed the location of defect, in the patient staff service host, file PatientStaffDAL/PatientStaffDal.Staff.cs, method GetStaffList().   A strategy is employed of 1) Get a list of staff id’s, then 2) for each id in the list, select pieces of data like nursing unit assignments, device assignments, and application roles.   This gives correct results, but generates a large number of sql statements that can take a long time to execute on a slow network link.   A more optimized strategy would be to bring back the entire contents of the tables involved with a half dozen sql statements, and perform the join ‘in memory.’     The use of the entity framework encourages this style of ‘chatty’ sql.
verification_summary: Identified defect https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/browse/NC-11013#icft=NC-11013 to be applied to future software release.
rca_review_comments: The same pattern of sql also occurs in ECT generate configuration.   It was also fixed in the old windows forms smart client.

summary: Voalte Admin Client not loading or loading slowly on staff tab.
description: This issue was seen at Penn Presby hospital.  There are 2581 active staff members in their database.   A client with 1 millisecond latency loads the staff tab in 10 seconds, while a client with 20 millisecond latency requires 1.5 to 2 minutes to load the staff tab.
impact_description: IMPACT ASSESSMENT SUMMARY

Fixed slow loading of the Voalte Admin Client Staff tab at large / high-latency sites. The staff-list load used an N+1 (query-in-a-loop) pattern, so the number of database round-trips grew with the staff count and load time scaled with network latency (e.g. Penn Presby: \~2,581 active staff, 1.5-2 minutes to load at 20 ms latency).

Before:  
The staff-list load issued three queries per staff member (application roles, nursing-unit associations, mobile-device assignments) inside the loop, and the org-unit expand path resolved each unit with a separate per-unit lookup. Query count scaled with staff and unit count.

After:  
Each related collection is now loaded once for all staff and matched up in memory, and the nursing units are loaded once and read from an in-memory dictionary. Query count is now constant regardless of staff count. Returned data is functionally identical.

Other areas affected:  
No. Changes are confined to the Patient/Staff service read path; output is functionally identical.

IMPACT ASSESSMENT

Product Functionalities affected:

* NCP - Voalte Admin - Staff Administration  –  Minor

Read-path query optimization only: no database schema change, no API or contract change, and no change to returned data.

SUGGESTED DIRECT TESTS (verify the fix)

* Load the Staff tab against a facility seeded with a large active-staff count (e.g. 2,000+) and confirm it loads within an acceptable time.
* Repeat with added network latency (e.g. \~20 ms to the database) to mirror the reported site conditions; confirm load time no longer scales with staff count or latency.
* Confirm the staff list content is unchanged and correct - spot-check a representative sample of staff (roles, nursing-unit associations, and mobile-device assignments), or run a script to audit all staff records against the database.
* Confirm the nursing-unit (org-unit) details shown for each staff member are correct.

SUGGESTED REGRESSION TESTS (confirm nothing else broke)

* Add / edit / delete a staff member and confirm changes reflect correctly on the Staff tab.
* Staff with empty collections (no roles, no nursing unit, or no mobile device) display correctly.
* Staff assigned to multiple nursing units show all of their units.
* Small-facility sanity check (few staff) remains fast and correct.
* API interface consumers of the staff endpoint return the same data as before the change.
* Staff tab search / filter / paging behave as before.

Selecting the "nnc-client" certificate in Mirth seems to send the whole certificate chain in the message to the Nurse Call services. This causes troubles for NGINX which reports an error ("certificate chain too long").  
Since the client applications do not need the whole certificate chain, I changed the script so that it copies the "\*\_cert.pfx" file to "nnc-client.pfx".  
The certificate thumb print is the same either way, but this will mean that the Mirth will be able to send messages to Nurse Call.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
The database column size of the MobileDeviceProvider's TrunkAccessDialString was increased to 256. The login process for a staff, executes a stored procedure which joins to the MobileDeviceProvider table to include mobile device information if the staff has a mobile device assignment. The stored procedure was not changed to increase the TrunkAccessDialString and was still designating the size to be 20. This caused the stored procedure to throw an exception which resulted in a failed login. The fix was to increase the size of the TrunkAcessDialString to 256.

Diagnostic steps were supplied to run fs_cli.exe -p voalte against the FreeSWITCH service on the Nurse Call Enterprise server to see whether RTC was routing the audio setup request to Nurse Call at all, with SIP-level tracing as the next step if it was. Because audio paths within Nurse Call, within Linq, and between them all worked, and because rebooting the audio station resolved it by forcing a re-download of staff wireless configuration, the theory settled on the audio station holding incorrect dialing information for that staff member, as happens when a staff member is assigned a Linq badge while CSA configuration in ECT is incorrect, since wireless device configuration updates do not trigger a staff mobile device assignment update. The site reported no known Wireless Device changes in ECT near the event, Gateway logs were not set to Verbose so data was limited, the issue was never reproducible, and no further occurrences were reported after an upgrade.

summary: When a Duress Alert is placed from a Linq badge it appears to send the alert two times in rapid succession
description: At Carson Valley Health where we are piloting Linq with NC 4.1.210, when a Duress Alert is placed from a Linq badge it appears to send 2 identical alerts in rapid succession to Nurse Call. It appears that the 1st alert is written to the DB but the 2nd alert is not.

The MessageServiceHost log shows we are receiving and processing both alerts, resulting in 2 calls sent to the Wireless Provider ( Voalte Mobile via WAVE, in this case).

The 1st Duress Alert gets assigned a valid Notification id and Callid. i.e. notification id “5DF4E01” and Callid “384846”, which is seen in the attached logs.

The 2nd alert however is assigned a notification id of “1” and Callid of “0”.

The end result is that both alerts are sent within the same second to the Wireless Provider.

After speaking and reviewing this with David Girardeau and Alec Kaufman, they believe this is a defect.

I’ve attached the MessagingServiceHost log as well as the HillRom.LocatingServiceHost log for the test call captured.

Additionally there is s spreadsheet that shows the calls in question filtered out.
comment_summary: A Duress Alert placed from a Linq badge appears to be sent twice in rapid succession. Analysis of the logs shows two Duress events arriving roughly 75ms apart for the same location, with the Locating Service logs lacking detail and the Message Service logs showing a CallID of 0 on the second event, suggesting the second Duress published over RabbitMQ was associated with a database INSERT failure that did not stop delivery because of behavior added years ago after a transaction log overflow stopped PubSub processing. The thread reasons that the second Duress likely arrived while the first was still being processed, preventing the duplicate-detection logic from catching it, and notes that Messaging Service determines alert uniqueness from the CallID rather than the CallGuid, so two different CallIDs were treated as two different notifications. A further Duress test was captured with the HillRom.LocatingServiceHost log set to trace, and the thread raises a possible relationship to a more extreme case at another site covered by a separate defect.

root_cause_summary: during a single button press event of any button press combination, the system by design should not be sending more than 1 event per button press event. 

However in the listed affects version builds the customer was able to perform a workflow that resulted in a single button press event generating 64 button press events.
investigation_details: See comments
troubleshooting_steps: 1. Setup Duress Alert (Call Type 115) in VNC > ECT to send out to Excel WAVE. 
2. Notification Procedure used is the same as that used to for sending all other alerts to WAVE.
3. Tested Duress Alert from Linq badge. WAVE received 2 alerts from VNC.
4. Check MessagingServiceHost log and found both Alerts notifications recieved and processed.
5. Created a new Notification Procedure for the Duress Alert that sends to WAVE with Send Once checked. WAVE received 2 alerts from VNC.
6. Check MessagingServiceHost log and found both Alerts notifications recieved and processed.
7. Created new CallType with same values as default Duress Alert.
8. Set new Duress Alert Call Type to be sent with button press on Linq badge.
9. Tested new Duress Alert Call Type from Linq badge pointing to new Send Once Notification Procedure for the Duress Alert. WAVE received 2 alerts from VNC.
10. Check MessagingServiceHost log and found both Alerts notifications recieved and processed.
troubleshooting_results: Regardless of creating new Notification Procedures and Call Type. Each test resulted in 2 Duress Alerts being sent from VNC to WAVE.

Noted in log that the findings that were posted in the Description above in this RCA
verification_summary: Record-review verification summary: Based on the existing Jira investigation, root-cause, review, and comment records. This summary documents previously recorded evidence; no new functional testing or independent verification was performed.

The record documents duplicate Duress notifications from a single Linq badge activation, including a second notification with CallID 0. Related corrective defect PL-2310 is Done/Resolved with released fix version PL 1.2.003; its reproduction used a model-counter manipulation and did not reproduce the natural customer workflow. The linked defect status and release support corrective-action traceability, but this RCA contains no documented post-fix Carson Valley retest establishing one downstream notification per button press. Verification of the customer scenario and confirmation of the deployed version remain outstanding in the reviewed evidence. Basis: Description, Root Cause Summary, investigation comments and current PL-2310 details.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Updated the patient staff service to pull the data for role Ids from the correct column in the database. 

Further Explanation - After a staff member was updated in voalte admin, the patientStaffService would create an aggregated staff object with the new data. The aggregated staff object would take this staff data and combine it with other relevant data, including a list of all roles the staff member was assigned to. The patient staff service would then send this object through the Rabbit bus, where it would eventually make its way to voalte admin when users were open to the staff admin page. Because the patientStaffService was pulling the Id for the roles from the wrong column, the incoming data would not match any existing roles, which is why it would 'disappear'.

root_cause_summary: I looks like when a staff logs in to a scotty badge CSA updates the practitioner bumping its version. Nurse Call's practitioner is now at a lower version. description: Matt & team,

We just went through the SmartSync upgrade at a site in Pensacola and were not able to see any improvement on beds reporting to Status Board. Below were our steps:

 

1. Upload the 4.0.403 smart sync install package to the server
2. Stop all nurse call services
3. Uninstall local smart sync (4.0.301 in this case)
4. Install 4.0.403 smartsync 

    1. Only configuration was including the ENT server IP
    
5. Restart all services

 

Steps 2-5 only took about 2 minutes, which was really quick, but we had users on site in front of beds and we couldn’t get them to report in. Am I fundamentally missing something in this process?
comment_summary: Bed data was not being processed for VersaCare beds at a site, and the problem was reproduced in some rooms by unplugging and reconnecting the beds while capturing the device details. Investigation covered why some VersaCare beds show bed data and others do not, including bed revision and firmware differences, and a fix for the Sidecom software version was confirmed working on at least one bed, which reported a '0.00' sidecom software version in SmartSync and did display on Status Board. Joint troubleshooting with the services team across multiple rooms found that 60 to 70 percent of the affected rooms had bed cabling issues such as cables not fully connected or bent pins, and no invalid serial numbers appeared in the logs. A SmartSync upgrade was scheduled at the site to remove that variable before further troubleshooting, and the customer issue was subsequently reported as resolved.

SmartSync 4.0.403 was also installed for the invalid SideCom version condition; Clifford Feather documented one affected bed displaying data after that fix. Investigation Details state that correcting the physical connection issues resolved the reported issue, and Reece Caldwell and Matthew Tague confirmed customer resolution in the 6 November 2024 comments. These records support the documented operational resolution. This review does not constitute new room-by-room testing or establish an additional monitoring period. Basis: Investigation Details, Root Cause Summary and 7 March/6 November 2024 comments.

Attached images showing North Kansas configs, Carson configs, St Michaels in WA, and privilege lists of a 4.1.200 upgraded to 4.1.210 system (mine) v. pre 4.1 system upgraded to 4.1.210 (North Kansas).

However, no work item or test case was ever identified to clean those tables up during an upgrade.

comment_summary: A site saw Lost NUC alerts attributed to NUCs monitoring other NUCs. RCB3 NUC logs were dominated by "Invalid URI when attempting to find an entry in the route table" plus "Send to 1.2.3.849B.61BC failed because the link is not active", with that URI absent from the database and possibly changed by a system reconfiguration; a correlation was also found between "Work item [mctControllerQueue] has exceeded its maximum running time" and a lost nursing unit controller call with call trigger Rcb3-04023013WM2. Full and differential backups were obtained but only the full backups applied, and because configuration had been regenerated after the logs were written the URIs no longer matched, leaving the attempt to tie a URI to a log statement inconclusive. The team observed RCB3 NUC reboots roughly matching lost NUC calls in the database to within a few minutes, ruled out the high CPU usage seen in a similar mismatched-URI issue, and closed without a definitive root cause, advising the customer to limit who makes NUC monitoring configuration changes.

comment_summary: Rebooting a room caused Lost Unit Server alerts and high CPU on the consoles, with RCB3 boards logging huge numbers of "Invalid URI when attempting to find an entry in the route table route table". A packet capture taken on the NUC RCB3 during a room reset showed the NUC being bombarded with nboSuppressAlertsMsg messages in a repeating cycle, with the message going from the NUC to an RCB3 board and coming straight back on the same socket connection, indicating a message loop. root_cause_summary: A Lost NUC would populate upon rebooting a room while other rooms in the same Unit were in a Disabled State.

The GRS10 for the unit will enter a very high cpu state, processing the flood of nboSuppressAlerts messages that are looping around the system.

Re-enabling the rooms fixed the issue. But the disabled rooms are in areas of the hospital under construction.

As a permanent fix, Michael Daughtery worked with HCA and has scheduled this fix to be part of VNC 4.0.404 which is currently scheduled for 1/22/24

comment_summary: A nursing unit repeatedly raised a Lost Secondary Console call that returned after the call was cancelled and the NUC rebooted. Reviewing the basesystemsettings folder showed every secondary console in the NUC's secondary list was heartbeating except the NUC's own route id, rcb3-037221Y2WM2, which was itself present in that list; the NUC was not heartbeating with itself on either the ethernet or loopback interface, and it was the only device in the hospital with its own route id in its secondary list. The cause was identified as a monitoring criteria for a single room pointing at itself, so the NUC expected connections and heartbeats from itself and raised a Lost Secondary call when they never arrived. The fix was validated on a restored copy of the customer database before deleting the self-referencing monitoring criteria at the site and pushing configuration, after which the lost secondary call cleared with no device reboot, and no new lost secondary calls appeared for a week.

root_cause_summary: Updated configuration to resolve
investigation_details: There was a lost secondary console call that could not be cleared by any procedures to clear stuck calls - like marking the call as cancelled in the database and bouncing device service / devices.   I examined the secondary console list for the NUC that was placing the call.   This was RB 5 MB RCB3 NUC (RCB3) - 10.155.66.0 - rcb3-037221Y2WM2.  The nuc’s own ip address appeared in the list, and this was unique for the whole site - no other device had a reference to itself as a secondary.   Looking to see where the list was coming from, I found table function dbo.SecondaryConsoleConfig_GetByOrgUnitId_45.  By running the sql contained in the function, I determined that the reference to itself was coming from a monitoring criteria consisting of only a single room, many call types, and 1 org unit.    This monitoring criteria was somehow orphaned (not deleted or left behind somehow.)   After testing for safety on my machine, I deleted the monitoring criteria with sql statements, pushed configuration, and the lost secondary call disappeared.
troubleshooting_steps: Confirmed correct sw on both RCB and GRS10H. 

Confirmed no call forwarding set for the GRS10H. 

Confirmed no additional monitored units for GRS10H. 

Checked syslogs. No errors for either device. Checked configuration service log. 

Did see some other devices in the syslogs showing the invalid URI lines. 

Confirmed both effected devices are checking in successfully. 

Ran netstat on both devices. Confirmed they successfully establish to each other. 

Performed global push. No change. Purged configuration. No change. 

Forced push sw to both. No change.
troubleshooting_results: The alert makes no sense since the RCB NUC itself is not showing lost. Also the netstat proves the nuc and GRS10h are connected.
verification_summary: Determined the reference to itself was coming from a monitoring criteria consisting of only a single room, many call types, and 1 org unit. Pushed configuration, and the Lost Secondary Console alert cleared. Proper operation was confirmed & there were no patient safety issues reported. Although updating the configuration resolved issue; unable to determine how issue was caused.
rca_review_comments: Unknown how the NUC got into this state but issue has been resolved.

summary: Unable to Clear Lost RCB without resetting NUC
description: Whenever they have to reboot an RCB3 (either due to troubleshooting or moving it from staging, etc.) there is a Lost RCB alert that is placed that stays on the system despite the RCB3 and GRS5 coming up properly (GRS5 displays a Primary Console Down message while in this state).  They have found that clearing the config and rebooting the NUC clears the alert as the RCB/GRS5 are online just fine.  We found that resetting the dhcp service on the NUC (via the command _sudo udhcpc renew_) clears the alerts as well.  Further strange behavior exists with the system as the end devices can ping the NUC, however the NUC was not able to ping any of the devices, but only the device that is rebooted is being reported as lost.  The NUC has been replaced as has the cable to rule them out.  This can be re-produced by simply rebooting any RCB3 on the 1st FL ED Unit.  All devices are on the correct firmware - 3.9.101.8.
comment_summary: A site could not clear a Lost RCB alert without resetting the NUC. Investigation reproduced the condition on site and found that after an RCB reboot the old socket on port 50005 was never released, so connections stacked up on the NUC until it was rebooted, though this was judged a symptom rather than the cause. Deeper testing showed that after an RCB reboot, ping worked but SSH and connectivity between the NUC and the RCB failed for 8 to 18 minutes before self-clearing, and packet captures taken with tcpdump on both devices showed an ARP duplicate-use warning for the NUC address 172.20.95.249 from an unknown MAC 54:75:d0:26:df:cc that was not present in the deviceconnection tables, plus duplicated hops in a traceroute from the RCB to the NUC while in the bad state. The customer found a NAT configuration on a Cisco device that was producing the duplicate IP behavior; after it was removed, rebooted RCBs reconnected automatically and the alerts cleared.
