2246 = Room 547  
2185 = Room 54
root_cause_summary: Two ADT admit messages for the same MRN reached \`PatientStaffServiceHost\` within the same millisecond on 2026-04-10 at 21:27:50.817 UTC. The MRN-uniqueness invariant is enforced only in C# (\`PatientDAL.cs:88\`/\`231\` calling \`dbo.Patient_UniqueMRN\` as a separate scalar SELECT before \`Patient_Insert_55\`), with no shared transaction and no unique index on \`dbo.Patient.MRN\` to back it up. Both threads passed the pre-check while the table was empty for that MRN and both \`Patient_Insert_55\` calls committed, producing two active rows (\`PatientID 337242\` and \`337243\`) sharing the same MRN. 

From that point forward, every subsequent ADT update or discharge attempt for the patient ran through \`PatientDAL.Update\`, which re-ran \`IsUniqueMrn\`, which now returned false because the **other** duplicate was still active — throwing \`PatientMRNNotUnique\`. The same exception fired in the discharge path (\`Inactivate → Update → IsUniqueMrn\`), where it surfaced to Voalte Admin Client as the generic "Unable to mark patient as deleted" / "Your action could not be completed" toast. The customer's ERM feed was correct; the duplicate state was created entirely on the Voalte side by a Time-Of-Check to Time-Of-Use race in our own admit pipeline. Resolved 2026-05-06 by transactional SQL cleanup that inactivated both duplicate rows after the patient physically left the facility; engineering follow-ups (filtered unique index, \`Inactivate\` skip-uniqueness) tracked separately to prevent recurrence.
investigation_details: ````
The customer reported one patient (Same MRN ) appearing in two rooms simultaneously in Voalte Admin Client at UPMC Pinnacle West Shore (NC 4.1.200): PatientID `337242` in Room 549 (LocationID `2185`) and PatientID `337243` in Room 547 (LocationID `2246`). Manual discharge from Voalte Admin Client failed with the generic toast "Your action could not be completed." HL7 ADT messages from the customer's EMR for this patient were also being silently rejected.
We pulled the customer's `AdvancedServiceLogs - UPMC Westshore.zip` archive (110 MB) and traced the failure end-to-end:
1. **Code path traced.** `PatientStaffServiceHost`'s admit pipeline (`PatientADTController.ProcessCoreADTAction` → `PatientADTService.ProcessAdmitAction` → `PatientAggregationService.CreatePatientAndAssignLocation`) validates MRN uniqueness via `PatientDAL.cs:88` (Insert) and `:231` (Update). The check calls `Patient.IsUniqueMrn` (`Patient.cs:557`) which executes a separate scalar `SELECT dbo.Patient_UniqueMRN(@MRN, @PatientId)` — independent of the subsequent `Patient_Insert_55` / `Patient_Update_55` stored proc. There is no shared transaction and no unique constraint or filtered unique index on `dbo.Patient.MRN`. The check-then-act pattern is therefore vulnerable to a Time-Of-Check to Time-Of-Use race.
2. **Race window observed in logs.** `PatientStaffServiceHost_00310.log` lines 45992–46033 (2026-04-10 21:27:50.817 UTC) shows two threads (T24 and T26) processing identical "Received transfer for Patient Id: 0 ... will be processed as an admission" messages within the same millisecond. Both reached `CreatePatientAndAssignLocation` (line 394). T26's location-assignment INSERT failed with `Patient Location Assignment failed. Table dbo.PatientLocationAssignment, Assignment already exists for LocationID 2185.` because `dbo.PatientLocationAssignment` *does* have a unique constraint on active `LocationID`. By the time that constraint fired, both threads' `Patient_Insert_55` had already committed, producing rows `337242` (T24, succeeded end-to-end and got Room 549) and `337243` (T26, orphaned — patient row stuck, location assignment rejected).
3. **Aftermath confirmed.** From 21:27:50.937 onward, every subsequent `PatientDAL.Update` (transfers, info updates, eventual A03 discharges) re-ran `IsUniqueMrn` and tripped because the *other* duplicate was still active. The exact stack shows up at `PatientStaffServiceHost_00313.log:19614` (2026-04-16 19:05:32.749 UTC) and recurs 10+ times through

description: ``The MRN-uniqueness invariant for `dbo.Patient` is enforced only in C# via `PatientDAL.cs:88` (Insert) and `:231` (Update), each of which calls `Patient.IsUniqueMrn` (`Patient.cs:557`) — a separate scalar `SELECT dbo.Patient_UniqueMRN(@MRN, @PatientId)` round-trip executed *before* the subsequent `Patient_Insert_55` / `Patient_Update_55` stored procedure. The two database calls share no transaction and `dbo.Patient` has no unique index or constraint on `MRN`, so the check is a classic Time-Of-Check-to-Time-Of-Use (TOCTOU) race.``  
  
``When two ADT admit messages for the same MRN reach `PatientStaffServiceHost`'s admit pipeline within the same millisecond (`PatientADTController.ProcessCoreADTAction` → `PatientADTService.ProcessAdmitAction` → `PatientAggregationService.CreatePatientAndAssignLocation`), both threads pass the pre-check while the table is still empty for that MRN, and both insert. `dbo.PatientLocationAssignment` *does* have a unique constraint on the active `LocationID`, so one thread's location assignment is rejected — but its `Patient_Insert_55` has already committed by then, leaving the duplicate `Patient` row stuck in the database.``

``From that point on, every `PatientDAL.Update` for the patient (transfers, info updates, both HL7-driven and Admin Client–driven discharges) re-runs `IsUniqueMrn`, which now returns false because the *other* duplicate is still active, throwing `PatientMRNNotUnique`. The discharge path (`Inactivate → Update → IsUniqueMrn`) wraps this as `ApplicationException("Unable to mark patient as deleted.")` and surfaces it to Voalte Admin Client as the generic toast `Your action could not be completed.` The system cannot self-heal — only direct DB cleanup unsticks the affected MRN.``
impact_description: IMPACT ASSESSMENT SUMMARY - impact assessment.
Under concurrent ADT admits for the same MRN, two admit requests could each pass a service-layer "is this MRN unique?" check and then both insert, producing two active Patient rows for a single MRN. Once duplicated, every subsequent update AND discharge for that MRN failed, leaving the patient permanently stuck in the system. Root cause was a time-of-check/time-of-use race: the uniqueness check and the insert were separate, non-atomic operations, so two callers could interleave between the check and the write. The fix moves uniqueness enforcement out of the service layer and into the database so the check and the write are a single atomic, serialized operation.
Before: 
The PatientService data-access layer (PatientDAL) called a C# pre-check (Patient.IsUniqueMrn / IsUniqueAccountNumber) and then, in a separate step, executed the insert/update stored proc. Two concurrent same-MRN admits could both pass the pre-check before either inserted, so both rows were written.
After: 
Uniqueness is enforced inside the stored procs (Patient_Insert_55, Patient_Update_55). Same-MRN callers are serialized with a SQL application lock, and uniqueness is re-verified atomically immediately before the write, so a duplicate admit is rejected cleanly. Discharge is deliberately never blocked by the uniqueness logic, so a patient already in a duplicated state can still be discharged. The user-facing error is unchanged (same PatientMRNNotUnique / PatientAccountNumberNotUnique message), so callers see the same behavior on a rejected duplicate as before. The now-unused C# pre-check helpers were removed.
Other areas affected: 
No. Changes are confined to the Patient admit/update/discharge path (two stored procedures and the PatientService data-access layer). The changed procedures are only invoked by PatientDAL; the uniqueness DB functions are only used by those procedures; and PatientDAL is only reached through the patient admit/update/discharge service. The error contract surfaced to upstream code is unchanged, so no consuming code required changes.
IMPACT ASSESSMENT
Product Functionalities affected:
* NCP - Voalte Admin - Patient Administration – Major
* NCP - Inbound ADT/HL7 – Major
* NCP - Voalte Admin - API Interface – Minor
Rationale: The fix changes the concurrency/write behavior on the core patient admit and update path, which the Admin Client and inbound ADT/HL7 both exercise; those two are rated Major. The API interface surface 
steps_taken: PRE-CONDITIONS 
 - NC 4.1.200 stack running. Mirth's inbound ADT channel deployed in its 
 default state and confirmed processing a happy-path A04 (single-message 
 admit successfully creates one Patient row and one PatientLocationAssignment). 
 - Note Mirth's MLLP listener address and port for the ADT channel 
 (typically tcp://:6661, but check the channel's Source 
 connector — Properties → Listener Address / Port). 
 - Note the HL7 facility / building / floor / point-of-care / room / bed 
 values that resolve to a valid empty LocationID in dbo.Location for the 
 target unit. (Use the value of HL7PointOfCare on the Location row, plus 
 HL7RoomName / HL7BedName.)
STEP 1 — Construct two ADT^A04 admit messages for the same MRN 
 Build two HL7 v2.3.1 ADT^A04 messages that: 
 \* carry the SAME MRN in PID-3.1 (e.g., MRN_RACE_TEST_001) 
 \* carry the SAME PV1-3 facility/building/floor/POC/room/bed pointing at 
 the empty target LocationID 
 \* carry DIFFERENT MSH-10 message control IDs so Mirth does not de-duplicate 
 them at the channel level (e.g., RACE_TEST_001_A and RACE_TEST_001_B) 
 \* carry the SAME effective time in EVN-2 / PV1-44 (this is what the customer's 
 HIS would do if it duplicated a single emission, and matches the 
 pattern observed in RCA-1820 where both admit log lines show identical 
 bodies at 21:27:50.8174 UTC)
 Sample skeleton (substitute facility-specific values): 
 MSH|^\~\\&|HIS|FAC|VOALTE|VNC|20260615120000||ADT^A04|RACE_TEST_001_A|P|2.3.1 
 EVN|A04|20260615120000 
 PID|1||MRN_RACE_TEST_001^^^FAC^MR||DOE^JOHN^Q||19700101|M 
 PV1|1|I|UNIT^ROOM^BED^FAC^^BLDG^FLR
STEP 2 — Send both messages so they arrive at Mirth within the race window 
 The race window observed in production is \~1 ms (RCA-1820: both threads 
 logged at exactly 2026-04-10 21:27:50.8174). Anything under \~10 ms reliably 
 reproduces; anything under \~50 ms reproduces most of the time. Use whichever 
 approach is most convenient for the QE setup:
Approach A — Two HAPI Test Panel instances (manual, easiest to set up) 
 1\. Open two HAPI Test Panel windows on the same machine. 
 2\. In each, paste one of the two ADT^A04 messages from Step 1. 
 3\. Configure both panels to send to Mirth's MLLP listener (Send menu → 
 MLLP Sender → host:port from pre-conditions). 
 4\. Click "Send" in panel A, then "Send" in panel B as fast as possible 
 (target: well under 1 second between clicks). 
 5\. Reproduces \~30-50% of attempts. Repeat until reproduced.
STEP 3 — Observe the result
actual_results: ```
- Both concurrent admits commit Patient_Insert_55 successfully, producing two
 active Patient rows sharing the same MRN. PatientID values are consecutive
 (e.g., 337242 and 337243 in the UPMC West Shore case).
- The location-assignment INSERT for the losing thread fails with
 SqlException: Patient Location Assignment failed.
 Assignment already exists for LocationID .
 but its Patient row has already committed and is not rolled back.
- From this point on, every PatientDAL.Update on the affected MRN fails with
 Exception: MRN is already in use by another patient!
 thrown at PatientDAL.cs:234.
- The Inactivate path (used by both HL7 A03 and Admin Client manual discharge)
 calls Update internally, so it also fails, wrapped as
 ApplicationException: Unable to mark patient as deleted.
- Voalte Admin Client surfaces this to clinicians as the generic toast
 "Your action could not be completed. Try again after a few moments or
 contact your Technical Support Team."
- The system remains in this stuck state indefinitely — the defect is not
 self-correcting. Mirth retries continue to fail. Manual UI clicks continue
 to fail. The patient cannot be discharged from Voalte through any in-product
 path.
```
expected_results: ```
- At most one active Patient row exists for any given MRN at any time.
- One of the two concurrent admit operations succeeds end-to-end (creates the
  Patient row, creates the location assignment).
- The other concurrent operation fails fast with a deterministic error that
  ADTIntegrationService can surface as a FaultException, allowing Mirth to NACK
  the duplicate ADT message back to the HIS.
- Subsequent ADT updates and Admin Client discharge attempts for the affected
  patient succeed.
- No manual SQL intervention is required.
```
work_around: Manual SQL cleanup by Tech Support / customer DBA. Procedure documented in 
RCA-1820, Section 4.3:
 1\. Identify the duplicate Patient rows for the affected MRN (pre-flight 
 queries inspect dbo.Patient, dbo.PatientLocationAssignment, 
 dbo.StaffPatientApplicationRoleAssignment, dbo.PatientNote). 
 2\. In a single transaction, set IsActive = 0 on the duplicate Patient rows, 
 close all active PatientLocationAssignment rows 
 (EffectiveThru = SYSUTCDATETIME()), close all active staff-patient 
 assignments (EffectiveThruUtc = SYSUTCDATETIME()), and inactivate any 
 active patient notes. 
 3\. Verify dbo.Patient_UniqueMRN(, ) returns 0 before 
 COMMIT.

Also seeing Patient MRNs have a leading character “.” however some of these patients are admitted successfully it may be causing a backend issue on some messages. Could be nothing but worth noting

root_cause_summary: Revising this to a defect.  We made a change that allows a patient to be fully admitted and become active on an INFO action even if they do not have an assigned location.  This means that when the A01 comes thru to admit them it will be rejected because this patient is active in the system.  

The below is no longer accurate but is being left here for continuity.   
ADT message are being used incorrectly.  Customer messages are A08 (patient update) followed by A01 (admit patient to healthcare facility).  The A08 will make the patient active in our system, essentially admiting them without a location if none is provided.  When the A01 arrives the patient is detected as already admitted and to avoid admitting the same patient twice, the message is logged and rejected.  An A02 (transfer patient) would move the patient into a location.
investigation_details: if a patient is already active, whether or not they are in a HR location/bed, an A01 message, or ADMIT, will be rejected because the patient is already active.  an A02, transfer, is the correct message to move the patient from one location to another or into a location once they are active.  

Further, it seems like subsequent attempts were made with modified MRNs in a few cases.  These MRNs had a '.' prepeneded to them.  These rows need to have their MRN changed to remove the '.' and any other missing information for that patient added.
troubleshooting_steps: To get the patients back in the bed, take the last A08 (update message), turn it into an A03 (discharge, copying MSH-7 date/time for PV1-45 discharge date/time) and then turning that A03 into an A13 (cancel discharge).   
(convert the messages into discharge and then convert it into a cancel discharge, we can then admit the patient)
troubleshooting_results: Patient can be admitted if message is altered and re-admitted

1. **Code path traced.** `PatientStaffServiceHost`'s admit pipeline (`PatientADTController.ProcessCoreADTAction` → `PatientADTService.ProcessAdmitAction` → `PatientAggregationService.CreatePatientAndAssignLocation`) validates MRN uniqueness via `PatientDAL.cs:88` (Insert) and `:231` (Update). There is no shared transaction and no unique constraint or filtered unique index on `dbo.Patient.MRN`. The check-then-act pattern is therefore vulnerable to a Time-Of-Check to Time-Of-Use race.
2. **Race window observed in logs.** `PatientStaffServiceHost_00310.log` lines 45992–46033 (2026-04-10 21:27:50.817 UTC) shows two threads (T24 and T26) processing identical "Received transfer for Patient Id: 0 ... will be processed as an admission" messages within the same millisecond. 3. **Aftermath confirmed.** From 21:27:50.937 onward, every subsequent `PatientDAL.Update` (transfers, info updates, eventual A03 discharges) re-ran `IsUniqueMrn` and tripped because the *other* duplicate was still active. The two database calls share no transaction and `dbo.Patient` has no unique index or constraint on `MRN`, so the check is a classic Time-Of-Check-to-Time-Of-Use (TOCTOU) race.``  
  
``When two ADT admit messages for the same MRN reach `PatientStaffServiceHost`'s admit pipeline within the same millisecond (`PatientADTController.ProcessCoreADTAction` → `PatientADTService.ProcessAdmitAction` → `PatientAggregationService.CreatePatientAndAssignLocation`), both threads pass the pre-check while the table is still empty for that MRN, and both insert. `dbo.PatientLocationAssignment` *does* have a unique constraint on the active `LocationID`, so one thread's location assignment is rejected — but its `Patient_Insert_55` has already committed by then, leaving the duplicate `Patient` row stuck in the database.``

``From that point on, every `PatientDAL.Update` for the patient (transfers, info updates, both HL7-driven and Admin Client–driven discharges) re-runs `IsUniqueMrn`, which now returns false because the *other* duplicate is still active, throwing `PatientMRNNotUnique`. The discharge path (`Inactivate → Update → IsUniqueMrn`) wraps this as `ApplicationException("Unable to mark patient as deleted.")` and surfaces it to Voalte Admin Client as the generic toast `Your action could not be completed.` The system cannot self-heal — only direct DB cleanup unsticks the affected MRN.``
impact_description: IMPACT ASSESSMENT SUMMARY - impact assessment.
Under concurrent ADT admits for the same MRN, two admit requests could each pass a service-layer "is this MRN unique?" check and then both insert, producing two active Patient rows for a single MRN. Once duplicated, every subsequent update AND discharge for that MRN failed, leaving the patient permanently stuck in the system. Root cause was a time-of-check/time-of-use race: the uniqueness check and the insert were separate, non-atomic operations, so two callers could interleave between the check and the write. The fix moves uniqueness enforcement out of the service layer and into the database so the check and the write are a single atomic, serialized operation.
Before: 
The PatientService data-access layer (PatientDAL) called a C# pre-check (Patient.IsUniqueMrn / IsUniqueAccountNumber) and then, in a separate step, executed the insert/update stored proc. Two concurrent same-MRN admits could both pass the pre-check before either inserted, so both rows were written.
After: 
Uniqueness is enforced inside the stored procs (Patient_Insert_55, Patient_Update_55). Same-MRN callers are serialized with a SQL application lock, and uniqueness is re-verified atomically immediately before the write, so a duplicate admit is rejected cleanly. Discharge is deliberately never blocked by the uniqueness logic, so a patient already in a duplicated state can still be discharged. The user-facing error is unchanged (same PatientMRNNotUnique / PatientAccountNumberNotUnique message), so callers see the same behavior on a rejected duplicate as before. The now-unused C# pre-check helpers were removed.
Other areas affected: 
No. Changes are confined to the Patient admit/update/discharge path (two stored procedures and the PatientService data-access layer). The changed procedures are only invoked by PatientDAL; the uniqueness DB functions are only used by those procedures; and PatientDAL is only reached through the patient admit/update/discharge service. The error contract surfaced to upstream code is unchanged, so no consuming code required changes.
IMPACT ASSESSMENT
Product Functionalities affected:
* NCP - Voalte Admin - Patient Administration – Major
* NCP - Inbound ADT/HL7 – Major
* NCP - Voalte Admin - API Interface – Minor
Rationale: The fix changes the concurrency/write behavior on the core patient admit and update path, which the Admin Client and inbound ADT/HL7 both exercise; those two are rated Major. The API interface surface 
steps_taken: PRE-CONDITIONS 
 - NC 4.1.200 stack running. Mirth's inbound ADT channel deployed in its 
 default state and confirmed processing a happy-path A04 (single-message 
 admit successfully creates one Patient row and one PatientLocationAssignment). 
 - Note Mirth's MLLP listener address and port for the ADT channel 
 (typically tcp://:6661, but check the channel's Source 
 connector — Properties → Listener Address / Port). 
 - Note the HL7 facility / building / floor / point-of-care / room / bed 
 values that resolve to a valid empty LocationID in dbo.Location for the 
 target unit. (Use the value of HL7PointOfCare on the Location row, plus 
 HL7RoomName / HL7BedName.)
STEP 1 — Construct two ADT^A04 admit messages for the same MRN 
 Build two HL7 v2.3.1 ADT^A04 messages that: 
 \* carry the SAME MRN in PID-3.1 (e.g., MRN_RACE_TEST_001) 
 \* carry the SAME PV1-3 facility/building/floor/POC/room/bed pointing at 
 the empty target LocationID 
 \* carry DIFFERENT MSH-10 message control IDs so Mirth does not de-duplicate 
 them at the channel level (e.g., RACE_TEST_001_A and RACE_TEST_001_B) 
 \* carry the SAME effective time in EVN-2 / PV1-44 (this is what the customer's 
 HIS would do if it duplicated a single emission, and matches the 
 pattern observed in RCA-1820 where both admit log lines show identical 
 bodies at 21:27:50.8174 UTC)
 Sample skeleton (substitute facility-specific values): 
 MSH|^\~\\&|HIS|FAC|VOALTE|VNC|20260615120000||ADT^A04|RACE_TEST_001_A|P|2.3.1 
 EVN|A04|20260615120000 
 PID|1||MRN_RACE_TEST_001^^^FAC^MR||DOE^JOHN^Q||19700101|M 
 PV1|1|I|UNIT^ROOM^BED^FAC^^BLDG^FLR
STEP 2 — Send both messages so they arrive at Mirth within the race window 
 The race window observed in production is \~1 ms (RCA-1820: both threads 
 logged at exactly 2026-04-10 21:27:50.8174). Anything under \~10 ms reliably 
 reproduces; anything under \~50 ms reproduces most of the time. Use whichever 
 approach is most convenient for the QE setup:
Approach A — Two HAPI Test Panel instances (manual, easiest to set up) 
 1\. Open two HAPI Test Panel windows on the same machine. 
 2\. In each, paste one of the two ADT^A04 messages from Step 1. 
 3\. Configure both panels to send to Mirth's MLLP listener (Send menu → 
 MLLP Sender → host:port from pre-conditions). 
 4\. Click "Send" in panel A, then "Send" in panel B as fast as possible 
 (target: well under 1 second between clicks). 
 5\. Reproduces \~30-50% of attempts. Repeat until reproduced.
STEP 3 — Observe the result
actual_results: ```
- Both concurrent admits commit Patient_Insert_55 successfully, producing two
 active Patient rows sharing the same MRN. PatientID values are consecutive
 (e.g., 337242 and 337243 in the UPMC West Shore case).
- The location-assignment INSERT for the losing thread fails with
 SqlException: Patient Location Assignment failed.
 Assignment already exists for LocationID .
 but its Patient row has already committed and is not rolled back.
- From this point on, every PatientDAL.Update on the affected MRN fails with
 Exception: MRN is already in use by another patient!
 thrown at PatientDAL.cs:234.
- The Inactivate path (used by both HL7 A03 and Admin Client manual discharge)
 calls Update internally, so it also fails, wrapped as
 ApplicationException: Unable to mark patient as deleted.
- Voalte Admin Client surfaces this to clinicians as the generic toast
 "Your action could not be completed. Try again after a few moments or
 contact your Technical Support Team."
- The system remains in this stuck state indefinitely — the defect is not
 self-correcting. Mirth retries continue to fail. Manual UI clicks continue
 to fail. The patient cannot be discharged from Voalte through any in-product
 path.
```
expected_results: ```
- At most one active Patient row exists for any given MRN at any time.
- One of the two concurrent admit operations succeeds end-to-end (creates the
  Patient row, creates the location assignment).
- The other concurrent operation fails fast with a deterministic error that
  ADTIntegrationService can surface as a FaultException, allowing Mirth to NACK
  the duplicate ADT message back to the HIS.
- Subsequent ADT updates and Admin Client discharge attempts for the affected
  patient succeed.
- No manual SQL intervention is required.
```
work_around: Manual SQL cleanup by Tech Support / customer DBA. Procedure documented in 
RCA-1820, Section 4.3:
 1\. Identify the duplicate Patient rows for the affected MRN (pre-flight 
 queries inspect dbo.Patient, dbo.PatientLocationAssignment, 
 dbo.StaffPatientApplicationRoleAssignment, dbo.PatientNote). 
 2\. In a single transaction, set IsActive = 0 on the duplicate Patient rows, 
 close all active PatientLocationAssignment rows 
 (EffectiveThru = SYSUTCDATETIME()), close all active staff-patient 
 assignments (EffectiveThruUtc = SYSUTCDATETIME()), and inactivate any 
 active patient notes. 
 3\. Verify dbo.Patient_UniqueMRN(, ) returns 0 before 
 COMMIT.

root_cause_summary: Revising this to a defect.  We made a change that allows a patient to be fully admitted and become active on an INFO action even if they do not have an assigned location.  This means that when the A01 comes thru to admit them it will be rejected because this patient is active in the system.  

The below is no longer accurate but is being left here for continuity.   
ADT message are being used incorrectly.  Customer messages are A08 (patient update) followed by A01 (admit patient to healthcare facility).  The A08 will make the patient active in our system, essentially admiting them without a location if none is provided.  When the A01 arrives the patient is detected as already admitted and to avoid admitting the same patient twice, the message is logged and rejected.  An A02 (transfer patient) would move the patient into a location.
investigation_details: if a patient is already active, whether or not they are in a HR location/bed, an A01 message, or ADMIT, will be rejected because the patient is already active.  an A02, transfer, is the correct message to move the patient from one location to another or into a location once they are active.  

Further, it seems like subsequent attempts were made with modified MRNs in a few cases.  These MRNs had a '.' prepeneded to them.  These rows need to have their MRN changed to remove the '.' and any other missing information for that patient added.

summary: Proper cleanup is not done on patient discharge of the patient when transferred to the location via HL7 message with a future timestamp
description: Based on the CWS-PRQ-13148 ‘Effective Date’, the timestamp from the transfer message (A02) header should be used for patient transfer. If for some reason (Incorrect System Clock, Time Zone Offset Issues, Deferred/Batch Processing, etc.) a transfer message from EMR has a future timestamp in the header, Nurse Call creates a patient-location assignment with that future timestamp (EffectiveOn value in PatientLocationAssignment table in the database). And if the patient is discharged before that future timestamp happens, the proper cleanup is not done: safety alerts are not canceled, the room status is not set to ‘Out of Room’, patient information is not removed from Status Board and Voalte Admin Client grids. 
The root cause of the issue is that the system creates a future patient-location assignment. I think, the assumption was that MSH.7 segment will always have the current timestamp in it and we never discussed or implemented the guardrails for future timestamps in the header.

summary: ADT INFO will admit patient when they have no location
description: an ADT INFO action can result in a patient being admitted if they are not active in our system.  Prior to August 2021, and after March of 2019, there was a check for a valid location prior to allowing an INFO to admit a patient.   
Some EMR systems will send an A08 prior to an A01 /ADMIT as part of their workflow.  Often the A08/INFO does not have location information as that comes later with the A01.  What we end up with is the A08 causing the patient to be admitted with no location and then the A01 gets rejected because the patient is already active and we reject all A01/ADMIT for an already active patient to avoid double admission.  Now, we’ve got essentially orphaned patients with no location and no easy way to discharge them. 

---

## Task Description

* GOAL: Fix code that prevents an ADT-A01 (ADMIT) from processing due to a previous ADT-A08 (INFO) having already been processed.
* BACKGROUND: A change to the `PatientStaffService` was made so that when an ADT-A08 is processed it will perform an ADMIT action (TACO-5406). However, some hospital EMR’s use an ADT-A08 as a “Pre-Admit” (instead of using an ADT-A04. In these hospitals they will send an ADT-A08 then later send an ADT-A01.  
    
  The processing of ADT messages can be complicated due to the business rules that we have implemented. Currently, when the ADT-A01 comes across it first checks to see if the “Master Patient ID” is “active” and if it is then it logs a message (“An active patient is already admitted at location…) and continues – basically ignoring the admit (“dropping it on the floor”).  
    
  I believe the fix may be to do one of the following:  
  \# 1. Augment the call to Patient.IsMasterPatientIdActive to include the location or action  
  \# 2. Add logic to the PatientADTService.ProcessAdmitAction so that it checks to see if the location is not set and the action is “ADMIT”, then we should merge the information and continue with the ADMIT action (need to check with Bill T to be sure there are no adverse issues)  
* CONSTRAINTS:

    * Minimal changes to the existing code base
    * 
    
* ASSUMPTIONS:

    * Automation suite will cover the formal testing
    * With this specific scenario the plan is that the A08 (treated as an admit) will be to a non-Baxter location. And the A01 will be to a Baxter location. This will be treated as a “Transfer” of the patient.
    * The issue that Michael N is having seems different from the brief explanation that I got from JVA.
    
        
comment_summary: The defect is that an ADT INFO message will admit a patient who has no location. The proposed handling was to treat an incoming A01 admit as a transfer when the patient is already present in Nurse Call for any reason, and to ignore an A08 information update as a pre-admission message when it has no PV1 assigned location and the patient is not active in the database. The regression was traced to earlier changes made on the Nurse Call side and the Mirth side under two linked tickets. A field workaround of altering the Mirth ADT channel to set the actionType to XFER when it resolves to ADMIT was proposed but flagged as needing validation on all versions from 4.1.000 and as risking loss of configured patient risks when Nurse Call receives a transfer. The issue was reported live at a customer with a patient safety concern, an RCA was opened, and the upgrade team sought a way to assess which customers would be affected; the code change broke several automated tests that were fixed and re-executed, and all planned tests eventually passed.

root_cause_summary: Revising this to a defect.  We made a change that allows a patient to be fully admitted and become active on an INFO action even if they do not have an assigned location.  This means that when the A01 comes thru to admit them it will be rejected because this patient is active in the system.  

The below is no longer accurate but is being left here for continuity.   
ADT message are being used incorrectly.  Customer messages are A08 (patient update) followed by A01 (admit patient to healthcare facility).  The A08 will make the patient active in our system, essentially admiting them without a location if none is provided.  When the A01 arrives the patient is detected as already admitted and to avoid admitting the same patient twice, the message is logged and rejected.  An A02 (transfer patient) would move the patient into a location.

Further, it seems like subsequent attempts were made with modified MRNs in a few cases.  These MRNs had a '.' prepeneded to them.  These rows need to have their MRN changed to remove the '.' and any other missing information for that patient added.

comment_summary: Status Board did not reflect patient transfer information. Investigation found a problem introduced in the Bridge Service in 3.9.300: the Admit Patient message includes a null check that defaults missing values to an empty string before the message is sent, but Transfer and Swap messages do not. When a patient is admitted in Smart Client without some name fields, those values are stored as empty strings, whereas the ADTIntegrationService converts them to NULL before sending to the patient staff service, so NULL is persisted and the defect only appears on ADT transfers. The immediate solution chosen was a database trigger that replaces inserted NULL values with empty strings on patient admission and update, covering Smart Client and A01/A08 messages, and the decision for already-affected patients was to let them age out naturally through discharge rather than run a SQL correction script.

root_cause_summary: This is only an issue for ADT admitted patients with missing name fields that are later transferred. When patients are admitted on Smart Client, they are admitted with empty strings rather than null values. The ADT suite verifies at the database level, but the problematic code was introduced in the bridge service. Unless Status Board is the verification point, you will not see the issue. ADT tests will be updated to include Status Board as a verification point for end to end testing.
investigation_details: Recap of troubleshooting from 15/5/2019 @ 10:00am

1. Smart Client patient transfer test was successful.
2. This leads us to believe that the issue is with how Mirth handles transfers and swaps.
3. Next Ashif and Phil and UVA will test transfers of test patient for intra and inter-unit via EPIC (and then same patients again via Smart Client) and get back to the team with results.
4. Jim is checking the transfer logic in the code to see where the breakdown could potentially be occurring.

Further testing revealed that the issue is with how NNC reads the Mirth data. If there is no Middle Name in the HL7 message, the NULL value then causes SB to ignore that message. (See notes below)
rca_review_comments: Workaround deployed at UVA.

Defect created and linked.

KB created and awaiting SME and QA approval: [https://hill-rom.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CTS/pages/1096679594/Status+Board+does+not+reflect+patient+transfers](https://hill-rom.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CTS/pages/1096679594/Status+Board+does+not+reflect+patient+transfers)

summary: NNC - 4.1.101 - Mirth not Assigning Preadmitted Patients to Assigned Rooms
description: Customer encountering an issue when transferring a preadmitted patient to a room.  
  
Using ControlID Q3165584123T4304834494X114724 in Mirth to examine what is going on, we are seeing the following:

1. A preadmit message enters the system as an A08 message and enters the patient into our database without a room assignment
2. Once it is decided to admit the patient, they are then transferred to a room with an A01 message. The system appears to ignore this message, as the transfer message is present and recognized by Mirth, but no changes are made in the database
3. The same goes for an ORU message attempting to assign a Falls Risk to this patient.

The end results is a failure to assign a falls risk to the room, and Status Board and Smart Client not displaying the patient's info. We ended up re-running the message transferring the patient to their room as an A02, which caused it to hit the database.
root_cause_summary: Functioning as expected/designed
investigation_details: The behavior noted above is how the code is written and is not a bug.  The A01/Admit code path checks to see if there is an active patient (checks by MasterPatientID and IsActive flag) and if there is it will log an Info level message that there is already an active patient at that location.   Because of the inclusion of the location information, I would say the pre-admit without a location scenario was not considered and should be discussed.  
  
Also, the ORU message does update the risks for that patient in the database.  It does not put the patient into a room.
verification_summary: No problem found.
rca_review_comments: System is functioning as designed.

summary: ADT INFO will admit patient when they have no location
description: an ADT INFO action can result in a patient being admitted if they are not active in our system.  Prior to August 2021, and after March of 2019, there was a check for a valid location prior to allowing an INFO to admit a patient.   
Some EMR systems will send an A08 prior to an A01 /ADMIT as part of their workflow.  Often the A08/INFO does not have location information as that comes later with the A01.  What we end up with is the A08 causing the patient to be admitted with no location and then the A01 gets rejected because the patient is already active and we reject all A01/ADMIT for an already active patient to avoid double admission.  Now, we’ve got essentially orphaned patients with no location and no easy way to discharge them. 

---

## Task Description

* GOAL: Fix code that prevents an ADT-A01 (ADMIT) from processing due to a previous ADT-A08 (INFO) having already been processed.
* BACKGROUND: A change to the `PatientStaffService` was made so that when an ADT-A08 is processed it will perform an ADMIT action (TACO-5406). However, some hospital EMR’s use an ADT-A08 as a “Pre-Admit” (instead of using an ADT-A04. In these hospitals they will send an ADT-A08 then later send an ADT-A01.  
    
  The processing of ADT messages can be complicated due to the business rules that we have implemented. Currently, when the ADT-A01 comes across it first checks to see if the “Master Patient ID” is “active” and if it is then it logs a message (“An active patient is already admitted at location…) and continues – basically ignoring the admit (“dropping it on the floor”).  
    
  I believe the fix may be to do one of the following:  
  \# 1. Augment the call to Patient.IsMasterPatientIdActive to include the location or action  
  \# 2. Add logic to the PatientADTService.ProcessAdmitAction so that it checks to see if the location is not set and the action is “ADMIT”, then we should merge the information and continue with the ADMIT action (need to check with Bill T to be sure there are no adverse issues)  
* CONSTRAINTS:

    * Minimal changes to the existing code base
    * 
    
* ASSUMPTIONS:

    * Automation suite will cover the formal testing
    * With this specific scenario the plan is that the A08 (treated as an admit) will be to a non-Baxter location. And the A01 will be to a Baxter location. This will be treated as a “Transfer” of the patient.
    * The issue that Michael N is having seems different from the brief explanation that I got from JVA.
    
        
comment_summary: The defect is that an ADT INFO message will admit a patient who has no location. The proposed handling was to treat an incoming A01 admit as a transfer when the patient is already present in Nurse Call for any reason, and to ignore an A08 information update as a pre-admission message when it has no PV1 assigned location and the patient is not active in the database. The regression was traced to earlier changes made on the Nurse Call side and the Mirth side under two linked tickets. A field workaround of altering the Mirth ADT channel to set the actionType to XFER when it resolves to ADMIT was proposed but flagged as needing validation on all versions from 4.1.000 and as risking loss of configured patient risks when Nurse Call receives a transfer. The issue was reported live at a customer with a patient safety concern, an RCA was opened, and the upgrade team sought a way to assess which customers would be affected; the code change broke several automated tests that were fixed and re-executed, and all planned tests eventually passed.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
The processing of the ADT-A01 message in the PatientStaffService code was changed so that if the patient already exists in Nurse Call the A01 information will update the existing patient.  
All test scenarios have been communicated via this confluence page:  
[https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/NC/pages/7161905624/NC-21805+Development+Testing+Notes](https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/NC/pages/7161905624/NC-21805+Development+Testing+Notes)  
Impact Assessment:  
NCP - Inbound ADT/HL7 - MINOR  
Platform Impact:  
N/A  
Product Labeling Impact:  
N/A  
Regression Meeting:  
Date:  20/APRIL/2026  
Attendees - Paul McSwain (Development Engineering), Eric Davis (Quality Engineering)  
Minutes - This fix is to make the system work correctly when we admit a patient with no location (non-Baxter) and then admit them again to a Baxter location. It is agreed that direct tests are sufficient and regression tests should include patient persistence tests (risks, notes, patient information), Patient/Staff Assignment tests and any admission test with A01, A08, A60 and A13 messages.

Test that can be removed from regression list:  
BAS device  
Out of room  
Swaps  
Merges  
SSL  
Configuration specific tests
steps_taken: Update an inactive patient using the EMR without assigning a location.  Admit the patient using the EMR.
actual_results: The admission is rejected because the A08 caused that patient that patient to become active.
expected_results: The patient will be admitted
work_around: Workaround: To get the patients back in the bed, take the last A08 (update message), turning it into an A03 (discharge, copying MSH-7 date/time for PV1-45 discharge date/time) and then turning that A03 into an A13 (cancel discharge).   
(convert the messages into discharge and then convert it into a cancel discharge, we can then admit the patient)

There may be others but this is one.

description: The Staff’s reference to its Application User record is removed during practitioner reconciliation when CSA’s practitioner version is greater than NC’s practitioner version. impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Isolated change in NC Directory server which sets the ApplicationUserId on the StaffDto before updating the staff record in the database. If a staff logs in to a linq device while the directory service is stopped, the login process updates the practitioner's version in CSA. When directory service is restarted, reconciliation is executed. The reconciliation rules for practitioner calls out updating the nurse call staff with the contents in CSA if CSA's prectitioner's version is greater than nurse call's prectitioner's version. The update of the staff nulls out the ApplicationUserId column in the staff table.

Needed to update the the NavicareEnterprise and NavicareAuditing DatabaseBuildVersion and MarketingVersion

summary: TrunkAccessDialString column size in database functions causes exceptions and prevents Voalte Admin login
description: While logged into the Voalte Linq badge, if you also try to login to Voalte Admin Client, an exception caused by the database function NavicareEnterprise.PC.Staff_GetByUsernameDomainId appears in the PatientStaffService logs. This is because the TrunkAccessDialString column size (20) specified in the function is different from its column size (256) in MobileDeviceProvider when that table is joined. As a result, any TrunkAccessDialString length greater than 20 will be truncated and cause an exception.
impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
The database column size of the MobileDeviceProvider's TrunkAccessDialString was increased to 256. The login process for a staff, executes a stored procedure which joins to the MobileDeviceProvider table to include mobile device information if the staff has a mobile device assignment. The stored procedure was not changed to increase the TrunkAccessDialString and was still designating the size to be 20. This caused the stored procedure to throw an exception which resulted in a failed login. The fix was to increase the size of the TrunkAcessDialString to 256.

comment_summary: A site sporadically could not call a particular Linq device: Nurse Call to Nurse Call audio worked, Linq to Linq audio worked, and other stations could call the same badge, but one specific station to that Linq badge failed until the audio station was rebooted. Diagnostic steps were supplied to run fs_cli.exe -p voalte against the FreeSWITCH service on the Nurse Call Enterprise server to see whether RTC was routing the audio setup request to Nurse Call at all, with SIP-level tracing as the next step if it was. Because audio paths within Nurse Call, within Linq, and between them all worked, and because rebooting the audio station resolved it by forcing a re-download of staff wireless configuration, the theory settled on the audio station holding incorrect dialing information for that staff member, as happens when a staff member is assigned a Linq badge while CSA configuration in ECT is incorrect, since wireless device configuration updates do not trigger a staff mobile device assignment update. The site reported no known Wireless Device changes in ECT near the event, Gateway logs were not set to Verbose so data was limited, the issue was never reproducible, and no further occurrences were reported after an upgrade.

summary: When a Duress Alert is placed from a Linq badge it appears to send the alert two times in rapid succession
description: At Carson Valley Health where we are piloting Linq with NC 4.1.210, when a Duress Alert is placed from a Linq badge it appears to send 2 identical alerts in rapid succession to Nurse Call. It appears that the 1st alert is written to the DB but the 2nd alert is not.

The MessageServiceHost log shows we are receiving and processing both alerts, resulting in 2 calls sent to the Wireless Provider ( Voalte Mobile via WAVE, in this case).

The 1st Duress Alert gets assigned a valid Notification id and Callid. i.e. notification id “5DF4E01” and Callid “384846”, which is seen in the attached logs.

The 2nd alert however is assigned a notification id of “1” and Callid of “0”.

The end result is that both alerts are sent within the same second to the Wireless Provider.

After speaking and reviewing this with David Girardeau and Alec Kaufman, they believe this is a defect.

I’ve attached the MessagingServiceHost log as well as the HillRom.LocatingServiceHost log for the test call captured.

Additionally there is s spreadsheet that shows the calls in question filtered out.
comment_summary: A Duress Alert placed from a Linq badge appears to be sent twice in rapid succession. Analysis of the logs shows two Duress events arriving roughly 75ms apart for the same location, with the Locating Service logs lacking detail and the Message Service logs showing a CallID of 0 on the second event, suggesting the second Duress published over RabbitMQ was associated with a database INSERT failure that did not stop delivery because of behavior added years ago after a transaction log overflow stopped PubSub processing. The thread reasons that the second Duress likely arrived while the first was still being processed, preventing the duplicate-detection logic from catching it, and notes that Messaging Service determines alert uniqueness from the CallID rather than the CallGuid, so two different CallIDs were treated as two different notifications. A further Duress test was captured with the HillRom.LocatingServiceHost log set to trace, and the thread raises a possible relationship to a more extreme case at another site covered by a separate defect.

root_cause_summary: during a single button press event of any button press combination, the system by design should not be sending more than 1 event per button press event. 

However in the listed affects version builds the customer was able to perform a workflow that resulted in a single button press event generating 64 button press events.
investigation_details: See comments
troubleshooting_steps: 1. Setup Duress Alert (Call Type 115) in VNC > ECT to send out to Excel WAVE. 
2. Notification Procedure used is the same as that used to for sending all other alerts to WAVE.
3. Tested Duress Alert from Linq badge. WAVE received 2 alerts from VNC.
4. Check MessagingServiceHost log and found both Alerts notifications recieved and processed.
5. Created a new Notification Procedure for the Duress Alert that sends to WAVE with Send Once checked. WAVE received 2 alerts from VNC.
6. Check MessagingServiceHost log and found both Alerts notifications recieved and processed.
7. Created new CallType with same values as default Duress Alert.
8. Set new Duress Alert Call Type to be sent with button press on Linq badge.
9. Tested new Duress Alert Call Type from Linq badge pointing to new Send Once Notification Procedure for the Duress Alert. WAVE received 2 alerts from VNC.
10. Check MessagingServiceHost log and found both Alerts notifications recieved and processed.
troubleshooting_results: Regardless of creating new Notification Procedures and Call Type. Each test resulted in 2 Duress Alerts being sent from VNC to WAVE.

Noted in log that the findings that were posted in the Description above in this RCA
verification_summary: Record-review verification summary: Based on the existing Jira investigation, root-cause, review, and comment records. This summary documents previously recorded evidence; no new functional testing or independent verification was performed.

The record documents duplicate Duress notifications from a single Linq badge activation, including a second notification with CallID 0. Related corrective defect PL-2310 is Done/Resolved with released fix version PL 1.2.003; its reproduction used a model-counter manipulation and did not reproduce the natural customer workflow. The linked defect status and release support corrective-action traceability, but this RCA contains no documented post-fix Carson Valley retest establishing one downstream notification per button press. Verification of the customer scenario and confirmation of the deployed version remain outstanding in the reviewed evidence. summary: NC Directory Service reconciliation process disables user logins under certain conditions
description: The Staff’s reference to its Application User record is removed during practitioner reconciliation when CSA’s practitioner version is greater than NC’s practitioner version. When CSA’s practitioner version is greater, Nurse Call updates its local staff with data from CSA. This update is clearing out the Staff record’s ApplicationUserID column. impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Isolated change in NC Directory server which sets the ApplicationUserId on the StaffDto before updating the staff record in the database. If a staff logs in to a linq device while the directory service is stopped, the login process updates the practitioner's version in CSA. When directory service is restarted, reconciliation is executed. The reconciliation rules for practitioner calls out updating the nurse call staff with the contents in CSA if CSA's prectitioner's version is greater than nurse call's prectitioner's version. The update of the staff nulls out the ApplicationUserId column in the staff table.

Needed to update the the NavicareEnterprise and NavicareAuditing DatabaseBuildVersion and MarketingVersion

summary: Job Roles for Practitioners with Same Global Staff IDs Shared Across Multiple Facilities disappear when updates made to Staff Name
impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Updated the patient staff service to pull the data for role Ids from the correct column in the database. 

Further Explanation - After a staff member was updated in voalte admin, the patientStaffService would create an aggregated staff object with the new data. The aggregated staff object would take this staff data and combine it with other relevant data, including a list of all roles the staff member was assigned to. The patient staff service would then send this object through the Rabbit bus, where it would eventually make its way to voalte admin when users were open to the staff admin page. Because the patientStaffService was pulling the Id for the roles from the wrong column, the incoming data would not match any existing roles, which is why it would 'disappear'.

summary: NNC - dbo.ReportingApplication Table is not populating the URL after configuring or rebuilding SQL Server replication
description: The dbo.ReportingApplication table in the NavicareEnterprise database URL field is not being populated with configuring or rebuilding SQL server. Users are then unable to launch Status Board from Smart Client or users receive an error when launching Unit Dashboard from Smart Client. See attached.
root_cause_summary: The URL value is being taken from the “Reporting Services URL” textbox control value in order to make sure we have the latest (possibly modified) URL value. The issue here is that the textbox control will not be created unless the user enters the “Report Model Database->Publish Reports” “Publish Reports” page.
investigation_details: 1. Why are users unable to launch Status Board from Smart Client?  
  Because the dbo.ReportingApplication table in the NavicareEnterprise database URL field is not being populated
2. Why is the dbo.ReportingApplication table in the NavicareEnterprise database URL field is not being populated?  
  Because the URL value is being taken from the “Reporting Services URL” textbox control value in order to make sure we have the latest (possibly modified) URL value. The issue here is that the textbox control will not be created unless the user enters the “Report Model Database->Publish Reports” “Publish Reports” page.
3. Why is it necessary to modify the logic?  
  Because the wizard should default to the URL value in config setting and only be overwritten if the textbox control exists.

=== Case ===
CaseNumber: 00829961
Reported software version: NNC 3.9.200
case_summary.summary: Multiple alerts, mainly bed exit and chair alarm calls, became stuck on the status board after an upgrade, even though they cleared correctly on end devices. Investigation found a race condition in the multi-threaded device service that injected duplicate call records into the RabbitMQ bus; limiting the device service to a single processing thread, along with a later device service fix, resolved the stuck calls.
case_summary.reported_issue: Multiple alerts were becoming stuck on the status board after an upgrade, while clearing normally on end devices such as GRS5, GRS7, and GRS10.
case_summary.product: Nurse Call - Status Board / Device Service
case_summary.actions_taken: Logged into the ENT server and status board and confirmed stuck bed exit calls on a unit
Restarted RabbitMQ and verified connections
Monitored call publish/remove behavior for normal and bed-disconnect calls
Restarted status board services as a temporary workaround to clear stuck calls
Set MaxNumprocessing threads to 1 for the device service
Implemented a device service fix
case_summary.resolution: Set MaxNumprecessing threads to 1 for device service
case_summary.status: resolved
case_summary.key_points: Root cause: a race condition from recent multi-threaded processing changes in the device service, injecting duplicate calls into RabbitMQ
Log evidence found showing duplicate call creation
Restarting status board services cleared the stuck calls every time prior to the fix
Issue occurred site-wide, most prevalent on North tower 4th floor
KB article ids: JoIvlQ

issue_type: rca
status: Done
version_reported: (none)
version_fix: (none)
version_rule: issue_version_unknown
summary: Calls not clearing from Status board (intermittent)
description: VNC 4.1

After the upgrade site is experiencing intermittent stuck calls on status board, These calls are not showing on end devices, GRS5,GRS7 or GRS10’s only Status board

Most of the stuck calls are Bed exit and chair alarm calls

However I have seen a call cord disconnect be stuck, we went to the room, placed another call cord disconnect call, plugged call cord in, the newest call cleared but the old did not, which it remained on status board.

Tried multiple tests around 12:30 pm local, 3:30 est, North tower 4th floor RM 71. we placed bed exit calls, entered the room. adjusted the bed and canceled from the GRS7, alert then cleared from Status board.

While cleaning up the test room, customer turned bed exit off. Took weights off bed, zeroed the bed, call triggered and remained active in status board but not on the GRS10. Had to restart services to clear.

Restarting status board services clears the calls every time

This issue seemingly is happening across the whole site, North tower 4th floor showing the most issues.
comment_summary: Calls intermittently failed to clear from the Status board at sites running 4.1.200, severely enough that one customer paused remaining upgrade projects. Device Service Host logs for a stuck call showed the de-duplication logic failing to trigger, producing a SQL error 2601 "Cannot insert duplicate key row in object 'NCC.V_ActiveCall' with unique index 'AK_UniqueActiveCallGUID'" so call creation was abandoned, after which every subsequent status update (Answered, Cancel) failed with SQL error 257 "Implicit conversion from data type nvarchar to timestamp is not allowed" and the call never cleared. The suspicion was that a secondary or monitoring console reports the alert with the same BaseCallID but a different RequestingDeviceId, causing IsDuplicateAlertNotification() in AlertMessageHandler.cs to fail, and the affected units all used secondary consoles and unit monitoring. A separate bug was also found in the call_update stored procedure, where the row edition check compares @RowEdition to itself rather than to the stored RowEdition. The workaround that resolved it was setting MaxNumMessageProcessingThreads to 1 in the Device Service appsettings.json file, after which no further stuck-call reports were made at either site.

root_cause_summary: The root cause of this issue is unknown. The most likely cause is a race condition with the processing threads on the Mirth server that ended up freezing up the impacted customers channels. Other potential causes have been eliminated. The CPU/RAM and Memory on the Mirth server look healthy at the time of the incident and not every customer was impacted, which eliminates most issues with the Mirth VM itself. Another thought was a potential database issue, but restarting the channels resolved the issue with no further action taken to clear up database space, which makes that unlikely. If this happens again, we know what to check on the Mirth server to verify this being a processing threads race condition, but with no clear way to recreate the issue, we ultimately can't confirm the cause.
investigation_details: RabbitMQ nodes looked healthy and all up and functional, along with the federations. Next we looked to Mirth, where I found that a number of customers (six total, including the three in the RCA) were beginning to queue up. In the channels for these customers, I found that they were up and actively receiving and queueing messages, but were not processing anything new. The last processed message in any of these customers channels was about the same time (7:16am). 

To try and resolve this, I restarted the ADT channels for these customers. After they came up again, they all began processing messages again. While messages had queued up for a few hours (we resolved this issue around 9:30am), most customers had cleared and were caught up to normal again by the early afternoon.
verification_summary: Root cause inconclusive. After restarting ADT, messages started to process. Further investigation would be needed if issue were to recur.
rca_review_comments: If this happens again, we know what to check on the Mirth server to verify this being a processing threads race condition, but with no clear way to recreate the issue, we ultimately can't confirm the cause. We have monitored Mirth the past week since the incident and this has not happened again.

summary: Race Condition with Call creation from monitored units
description: https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-1625   
  
When units are being monitored, the system will report multiple of the same call (GUID/BaseCallID) to the Device Service, one from the NUC of the unit where the call was generated, and N number of calls from the Consoles that are monitoring the NUC.  The system will add the call to the SQL database and then onto an in-memory list.  The system will look on the in-memory list to determine if a call that has been reported has already been raised.  Occasionally the 2nd notification of the call will come in before the injection into SQL and adding onto the in-memory list has finished occurring.  This race condition will cause the system to incorrectly identify the monitoring console’s report as a new call.  This will fail to process and eventually result in a call that is stuck in both the database and StatusBoard (RabbitMQ specifically).  
  
In the customer environment, they have a separate SQL server and other external factors that could contribute to this race condition occurring that would have to be emulated for testing.

A SQL loop repeatedly selecting from dbo.call with a half second delay was used to put load on the system while attempting reproduction. The defect could not be reproduced on PDR0 and the direct test P1575-TEST-3707 passed there after being blocked in PDP28.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Moving the default value from 2 to 1 for the MaxNumMessageProcessingThreads in the appsettings.json and code causes the service to only process 1 message at a time.  This allows the system to avoid the race condition while minimizing code changes/regression.  
Before: Failure to process a SQL Insert before a monitored NUC reports a call results in calls incorrectly being identified as a new call instead of a duplicate, throwing errors in the DeviceService log and having the calls stuck in the DB & on StatusBoard.  
After: Device Service correctly identifies the calls as duplicates.  
Impact Assessment:  
NCP - Error Handling and System Alerting - Trivial  
Platform Impact:  
N/A  
Regression Meeting:  
Date:  27/OCT/2025  
Attendees - Josh Watkins (Development Engineering), Kate Papalava (Quality Engineering)  
Minutes - The call processing logic is not impacted by the change, so the direct test is sufficient for verification.  
Additional Software Components:  
N/A
steps_taken: 1\. Configure a console to monitor another unit for Normal Calls.  
2\. Set up a method to prevent the SQL call completing before the 2nd notification comes in.  
3\. Place a normal call from a monitored location.
actual_results: The system treats the 2nd notification as a new call, causing SQL errors in the Device Service log and the call is stuck in the database and in Statusboard.
expected_results: The system should detect that the 2nd notification is a duplicate and not re-process the call.
work_around: Restarting RabbitMQ service

root_cause_summary: SmartSync version mismatch
investigation_details: Customer was working ok on 3.9.201.  Was upgraded to 3.9.401 and now experiencing this issue which only seems to affect the bed exit status.  See screenshots.  Rails work and weight works, etc.  Only issue appears to be bed exit status on status board and on GRS5s.

* Restarted all advanced services and service fabric.  No changes.
* Checked firmware version and all devices seem to be on correct version 3.9.401.
* Checked version of SmartSync and it was mismatched, running on 3.9.201.
verification_summary: Installation issue - process documented in the Help Center.   
Verified information added to the KB  (KB-01920-B7X4 Loss of Bed Data) Approved on 30DEC20.
rca_review_comments: Reviewed this RCA and concluded that the SmartSync upgrade step was missed. Help Center already has the correct information. 

Information about checking SmartSync versions will be added to KB [https://hill-rom.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CTS/pages/884900011/Loss+of+Bed+Data](https://hill-rom.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CTS/pages/884900011/Loss+of+Bed+Data) to cover this RCA.

=== Case ===
CaseNumber: 00851184
Reported software version: Voalte Nurse Call 4.1.200
case_summary.summary: A hospital reported that cancelled calls at a 1st floor ED exam room were still showing active on the status board. Investigation tied the behavior to a race condition introduced by multi-threaded processing in the device service, which caused duplicate call entries; the recorded fix was to limit the device service to a single processing thread, and follow-up monitoring showed no further stuck calls.
case_summary.reported_issue: Cancelled calls at an ED exam room remained displayed on the status board instead of clearing.
case_summary.product: Nurse Call Server / Device Service (Voalte Nurse Call 4.1.200)
case_summary.actions_taken: Confirmed the same errors reported under RCA-1625 were occurring at this site
Reviewed logs showing duplicate key insert errors in the active call table
Implemented R&D's proposed device service fix
Monitored the site over the following days
Spot-checked the system and confirmed no new calls were stuck
case_summary.resolution: Set max number of processing threads to 1 in device service
case_summary.status: resolved
case_summary.key_points: Software version: Voalte Nurse Call 4.1.200
Cause: race condition from recent move to multi-threaded device service processing injected duplicate call notifications into the RabbitMQ bus
Log evidence: SQL error 'Cannot insert duplicate key row in object dbo.V_ActiveCall with unique index AK_UniqueActiveCallGUID'
Related to prior RCA-1625 issue reported at other sites

summary: Calls not clearing from Status board (intermittent)
description: VNC 4.1

After the upgrade site is experiencing intermittent stuck calls on status board, These calls are not showing on end devices, GRS5,GRS7 or GRS10’s only Status board

Most of the stuck calls are Bed exit and chair alarm calls

However I have seen a call cord disconnect be stuck, we went to the room, placed another call cord disconnect call, plugged call cord in, the newest call cleared but the old did not, which it remained on status board.

Tried multiple tests around 12:30 pm local, 3:30 est, North tower 4th floor RM 71. we placed bed exit calls, entered the room. adjusted the bed and canceled from the GRS7, alert then cleared from Status board.

While cleaning up the test room, customer turned bed exit off. Took weights off bed, zeroed the bed, call triggered and remained active in status board but not on the GRS10. Had to restart services to clear.

Restarting status board services clears the calls every time

This issue seemingly is happening across the whole site, North tower 4th floor showing the most issues.
comment_summary: Calls intermittently failed to clear from the Status board at sites running 4.1.200, severely enough that one customer paused remaining upgrade projects. Device Service Host logs for a stuck call showed the de-duplication logic failing to trigger, producing a SQL error 2601 "Cannot insert duplicate key row in object 'NCC.V_ActiveCall' with unique index 'AK_UniqueActiveCallGUID'" so call creation was abandoned, after which every subsequent status update (Answered, Cancel) failed with SQL error 257 "Implicit conversion from data type nvarchar to timestamp is not allowed" and the call never cleared. The suspicion was that a secondary or monitoring console reports the alert with the same BaseCallID but a different RequestingDeviceId, causing IsDuplicateAlertNotification() in AlertMessageHandler.cs to fail, and the affected units all used secondary consoles and unit monitoring. A separate bug was also found in the call_update stored procedure, where the row edition check compares @RowEdition to itself rather than to the stored RowEdition. The workaround that resolved it was setting MaxNumMessageProcessingThreads to 1 in the Device Service appsettings.json file, after which no further stuck-call reports were made at either site.

root_cause_summary: Recent moves to multi-threaded processing in the Device service introduced a race condition where a secondary notification from a console monitoring the location was treated as a new call rather than a duplicate.  This caused an issue where it would inject a secondary copy of the call into the RabbitMQ bus, which caused it to appear as a duplicate while the call is still active, and a stuck call when the active call is cancelled.

This caused an issue where it would inject a secondary copy of the call into the RabbitMQ bus, which caused it to appear as a duplicate while the call is still active, and a stuck call when the active call is cancelled.

summary: Race Condition with Call creation from monitored units
description: https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-1625   
  
When units are being monitored, the system will report multiple of the same call (GUID/BaseCallID) to the Device Service, one from the NUC of the unit where the call was generated, and N number of calls from the Consoles that are monitoring the NUC.  The system will add the call to the SQL database and then onto an in-memory list.  The system will look on the in-memory list to determine if a call that has been reported has already been raised.  Occasionally the 2nd notification of the call will come in before the injection into SQL and adding onto the in-memory list has finished occurring.  This race condition will cause the system to incorrectly identify the monitoring console’s report as a new call.  This will fail to process and eventually result in a call that is stuck in both the database and StatusBoard (RabbitMQ specifically).  
  
In the customer environment, they have a separate SQL server and other external factors that could contribute to this race condition occurring that would have to be emulated for testing.
comment_summary: The defect concerns a race condition in call creation from monitored units. Development stated the potential race condition has existed since 2012, with no explanation yet for why it only appeared with 4.1.200 and why not all 4.1.200 sites see it, and noted the same change must also be made in the cc-nc-lib-alertComponent repository. A SQL loop repeatedly selecting from dbo.call with a half second delay was used to put load on the system while attempting reproduction. The defect could not be reproduced on PDR0 and the direct test P1575-TEST-3707 passed there after being blocked in PDP28.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Moving the default value from 2 to 1 for the MaxNumMessageProcessingThreads in the appsettings.json and code causes the service to only process 1 message at a time.  This allows the system to avoid the race condition while minimizing code changes/regression.  
Before: Failure to process a SQL Insert before a monitored NUC reports a call results in calls incorrectly being identified as a new call instead of a duplicate, throwing errors in the DeviceService log and having the calls stuck in the DB & on StatusBoard.  
After: Device Service correctly identifies the calls as duplicates.  
Impact Assessment:  
NCP - Error Handling and System Alerting - Trivial  
Platform Impact:  
N/A  
Regression Meeting:  
Date:  27/OCT/2025  
Attendees - Josh Watkins (Development Engineering), Kate Papalava (Quality Engineering)  
Minutes - The call processing logic is not impacted by the change, so the direct test is sufficient for verification.  
Additional Software Components:  
N/A
steps_taken: 1\. Configure a console to monitor another unit for Normal Calls.  
2\. Set up a method to prevent the SQL call completing before the 2nd notification comes in.  
3\. Place a normal call from a monitored location.
actual_results: The system treats the 2nd notification as a new call, causing SQL errors in the Device Service log and the call is stuck in the database and in Statusboard.
expected_results: The system should detect that the 2nd notification is a duplicate and not re-process the call.
work_around: Restarting RabbitMQ service

root_cause_summary: The root cause of this issue is unknown. The most likely cause is a race condition with the processing threads on the Mirth server that ended up freezing up the impacted customers channels. Other potential causes have been eliminated. The CPU/RAM and Memory on the Mirth server look healthy at the time of the incident and not every customer was impacted, which eliminates most issues with the Mirth VM itself. Another thought was a potential database issue, but restarting the channels resolved the issue with no further action taken to clear up database space, which makes that unlikely. If this happens again, we know what to check on the Mirth server to verify this being a processing threads race condition, but with no clear way to recreate the issue, we ultimately can't confirm the cause.
investigation_details: RabbitMQ nodes looked healthy and all up and functional, along with the federations. Next we looked to Mirth, where I found that a number of customers (six total, including the three in the RCA) were beginning to queue up. In the channels for these customers, I found that they were up and actively receiving and queueing messages, but were not processing anything new. The last processed message in any of these customers channels was about the same time (7:16am). 

To try and resolve this, I restarted the ADT channels for these customers. After they came up again, they all began processing messages again. While messages had queued up for a few hours (we resolved this issue around 9:30am), most customers had cleared and were caught up to normal again by the early afternoon.
verification_summary: Root cause inconclusive. After restarting ADT, messages started to process. Further investigation would be needed if issue were to recur.
rca_review_comments: If this happens again, we know what to check on the Mirth server to verify this being a processing threads race condition, but with no clear way to recreate the issue, we ultimately can't confirm the cause. We have monitored Mirth the past week since the incident and this has not happened again.

   Because the load script was attempting to insert a record with the same unique key into the dbo.ProtocolPropertyEnum table.
3. Why was it necessary to alter the table dbo.ProtocolPropertyEnum?  
   Because the script alters the AK_ProtocolPropertyEnum  alternate key on the NavicareReporting.dbo.ProtocolPropertyEnum table to match the key on the NavicareEnterprise.dbo.ProtocolPropertyEnum table.

root_cause_summary: Two ADT admit messages for the same MRN reached \`PatientStaffServiceHost\` within the same millisecond on 2026-04-10 at 21:27:50.817 UTC. The MRN-uniqueness invariant is enforced only in C# (\`PatientDAL.cs:88\`/\`231\` calling \`dbo.Patient_UniqueMRN\` as a separate scalar SELECT before \`Patient_Insert_55\`), with no shared transaction and no unique index on \`dbo.Patient.MRN\` to back it up. Both threads passed the pre-check while the table was empty for that MRN and both \`Patient_Insert_55\` calls committed, producing two active rows (\`PatientID 337242\` and \`337243\`) sharing the same MRN. 

From that point forward, every subsequent ADT update or discharge attempt for the patient ran through \`PatientDAL.Update\`, which re-ran \`IsUniqueMrn\`, which now returned false because the **other** duplicate was still active — throwing \`PatientMRNNotUnique\`. The same exception fired in the discharge path (\`Inactivate → Update → IsUniqueMrn\`), where it surfaced to Voalte Admin Client as the generic "Unable to mark patient as deleted" / "Your action could not be completed" toast. The customer's ERM feed was correct; the duplicate state was created entirely on the Voalte side by a Time-Of-Check to Time-Of-Use race in our own admit pipeline. Resolved 2026-05-06 by transactional SQL cleanup that inactivated both duplicate rows after the patient physically left the facility; engineering follow-ups (filtered unique index, \`Inactivate\` skip-uniqueness) tracked separately to prevent recurrence.
investigation_details: ````
The customer reported one patient (Same MRN ) appearing in two rooms simultaneously in Voalte Admin Client at UPMC Pinnacle West Shore (NC 4.1.200): PatientID `337242` in Room 549 (LocationID `2185`) and PatientID `337243` in Room 547 (LocationID `2246`). Manual discharge from Voalte Admin Client failed with the generic toast "Your action could not be completed." HL7 ADT messages from the customer's EMR for this patient were also being silently rejected.
We pulled the customer's `AdvancedServiceLogs - UPMC Westshore.zip` archive (110 MB) and traced the failure end-to-end:
1. **Code path traced.** `PatientStaffServiceHost`'s admit pipeline (`PatientADTController.ProcessCoreADTAction` → `PatientADTService.ProcessAdmitAction` → `PatientAggregationService.CreatePatientAndAssignLocation`) validates MRN uniqueness via `PatientDAL.cs:88` (Insert) and `:231` (Update). The check calls `Patient.IsUniqueMrn` (`Patient.cs:557`) which executes a separate scalar `SELECT dbo.Patient_UniqueMRN(@MRN, @PatientId)` — independent of the subsequent `Patient_Insert_55` / `Patient_Update_55` stored proc. There is no shared transaction and no unique constraint or filtered unique index on `dbo.Patient.MRN`. The check-then-act pattern is therefore vulnerable to a Time-Of-Check to Time-Of-Use race.
2. **Race window observed in logs.** `PatientStaffServiceHost_00310.log` lines 45992–46033 (2026-04-10 21:27:50.817 UTC) shows two threads (T24 and T26) processing identical "Received transfer for Patient Id: 0 ... will be processed as an admission" messages within the same millisecond. Both reached `CreatePatientAndAssignLocation` (line 394). T26's location-assignment INSERT failed with `Patient Location Assignment failed. Table dbo.PatientLocationAssignment, Assignment already exists for LocationID 2185.` because `dbo.PatientLocationAssignment` *does* have a unique constraint on active `LocationID`. By the time that constraint fired, both threads' `Patient_Insert_55` had already committed, producing rows `337242` (T24, succeeded end-to-end and got Room 549) and `337243` (T26, orphaned — patient row stuck, location assignment rejected).
3. **Aftermath confirmed.** From 21:27:50.937 onward, every subsequent `PatientDAL.Update` (transfers, info updates, eventual A03 discharges) re-ran `IsUniqueMrn` and tripped because the *other* duplicate was still active. The exact stack shows up at `PatientStaffServiceHost_00313.log:19614` (2026-04-16 19:05:32.749 UTC) and recurs 10+ times through
