comment_summary: Group pages produced stuttering audio, and investigation traced the problem to the Windows version of FreeSWITCH, which cannot launch or schedule the separate processing threads needed to record the caller (A-Leg) while the paged devices (B-Legs) stream simultaneously; the same configuration ran perfectly every time on Linux. A long configuration-only search for a workaround proved non-viable, so a revised paging model was prototyped in which FreeSWITCH records the page to .wav files and VoIP Service acts as the control point, opening and closing B-Leg channels, timing the page, and cleaning up the streaming files. Testing confirmed the new model pages without stutter at the cost of a 1-2 second delay before audio opens and some wander between devices because each streams independently, and a small dialplan change allows flipping back to the original model for comparison. The thread notes no OS tweak or configuration setting can prioritize the audio and that the stutter could occur with as few as two devices, and the issue was ultimately closed as resolved by the 4.2.000 upgrade.

comment_summary: The thread covers a report that paging group receiving devices are automatically checked when clicking another paging group. Investigation reproduced it only after setting a new VoIP extension range and then creating paging groups before saving devices, so the devices had no VoIP addresses yet; one view was that this is expected behavior and the user must save devices first. Reviewers argued the scenario is easy for a customer to hit and could result in pages going to every room, and asked for a clearer ECT warning message. The item was deferred out of 4.1 because only 3CX was supported and the functionality would be disabled in ECT, then moved to the FreeSwitch release, where it could not be reproduced in 4.1.200 and was closed as not reproducible.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Multi-room paging in Nurse Call was using a conference bridge to establish an audio page using FreeSWITCH.  It is a simple model and requires minimum setup effort. Unfortunately, FreeSWITCH in Windows has an issue related to audio pacing of conference calls.  At the OS level, Windows cannot reliably feed the audio stream to the devices.  A buffer underrun occurs which causes momentary gaps that sound like a stutter.  The issue is deeper than task priority, RAM, or CPU core affinity of which no adjustments can fix the issue reliably.

To address this problem, an alternate strategy is needed that avoids the pacing (at least until we can move to containers based on Linux which do not have the pacing problem).  The change involves separating the recording of the page from the participant playback. The following describes how it works.  
1\. When the page is initiated, audio from the caller is recorded to .wav files local to FreeSWITCH.  The .wav files contain one second of the audio from the caller.  
2\. After 1 second of audio has been recorded, the participating devices are invited to start playing the audio stream.  As soon as each device joins, it plays back the audio files starting from the beginning.  
3\. When the caller completes his/her page and hangs up, the audio files stop being recorded.  
4\. Participating devices continue to play back the audio files until all of the audio is played out and then they hang up.  
5\. As soon as all of the participating devices have closed audio and detected as hung-up, the collection of paging audio files is removed.

Due to latency in processing the invite and the fact that a device plays the whole page regardless of when they begin, there can be an odd delay in the audio playback.  This is different than the previous model in which delayed participants would not receive the first part of the page if they joined late. 

If the VoIP Service is shutdown or crashes while in the middle of a page, it loses knowledge/understanding of the existence of the page.  This does not affect the end-of-page processing for the devices.  They will close as soon as they reach the end of the audio files.  However, special consideration is needed regarding the audio files that were produced.  When VoIP Service starts/re-starts, it checks to see if there are any existing audio page files.  If there are any, it will remove them as part of service initialization.

In order to validate the change, the origin
steps_taken: Run wireshark on the ethernet interface.  
Perform a group page, talking steadily during the page.  
Terminate the group page, and stop the wireshark.
actual_results: Audio coming in from the originating GRS10(H) is of high quality, but audio going out to the devices is broken and choppy.
expected_results: High quality audio going to all room devices.
work_around: none

comment_summary: A site reported a 4-5 second delay in paging audio. Wireshark analysis measured an average delay of about 3 seconds and established this as expected behavior, because a fix for stuttering paging audio introduced a deliberate 2 seconds of silence transmitted before audio is sent at the start of a page, plus roughly another second for the full audio path to be established after invites go out. The investigator confirmed the captured performance meets expected performance levels and that no further investigation is required. The thread notes 3CX was definitely faster than the current FreeSWITCH solution at opening a page, that the 1-2 second delay figure is informal and not documented in release notes, and that the stated long-term fix is to move FreeSWITCH to Linux.

summary: Authentication Failure on push config causes multiple thread of execution.
description: This appears to have been caused by a change made by SecureBlackBox in the updated version we are now using is triggering the delivery of two contradictory events. The gist of it is, when the authentication failure described above occurs, a callback that wasn't getting called in a previous version is now getting called. Our code in that callback, on an authentication failure, is to fire off a completion event with an error state of 'Authentication Failure.' What is happening at the same time is that the main-line code is continuing to process and it checks to see if all download attempts (3) have been tried before giving up. So, it fires off another Download attempt. The authentication failure completion event cleans up resources needed by the Download event and, boom, we have a problem.



Based on assessment to date, we expect to see a lost device system alert (due to device registration failures) prior to the config push. Appears to be a precursor with the exception of a checksum error on the configuration file that’s pushed to the device.
comment_summary: The defect is that an authentication failure during a push of configuration causes multiple threads of execution. Commentary stressed the scope and field impact: the problem can occur on any ECT config push, including MAC and break-fix service activity rather than just planned upgrades, and devices in recovery mode cannot always be identified or replaced beforehand because the parts and labor are billable without a GOLD level SMA. It was also noted that upgrading to 4.1.200 changes the extension format from 3CX to FreeSwitch, so any device that fails to receive its config is left with no audio, which was argued to carry a potential safety impact. The defect was tested and verified in nc_pd_release_4.1.210_5/ST3 and closed as Done.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Before: call back that is called by SecureBlackBox code was handling a failure case and successful transfer of data case.  
After: we only want this call back to handle the success case.  This is because the behavior out of SecureBlackBox related to this call back has changed.  In previous versions it was only called once a transfer was actually begun and now it is also called if there is a verification error when connecting to the device.  When that happens there are 2 separate code paths that are handling what is, essentially, the same error and there is a conflict.   
So, removed the error handling in the callback

Impact Assessment:  
NCP - Configuration - Organization and Devices - trivial

Platform Impact:  
N/A

Regression Meeting:  
Date: 21/AUG/2025  
Attendees- Cam Frye (Development Engineering), Akaash Tuteja (Quality Engineering) and David Girardeau (Development Engineering)  
Minutes - This issue was able to be reproduced on a large hospital scenario like environment ( MEGA 2022) since the issue triggered from a complaint/RCA from a large hospital, The fix for the configuration service was applied and was verified to have the issue related to devices past the bricked devices failing push configuration resolved. The below direct and regression test cases were agreed upon. Change is trivial so no additional testing is required. 

Additional Software Components:  
N/A
steps_taken: Log into ECT  
change something, we used the Room to Room Audio Timer value.   
Push config
actual_results: The RCB will fail and any devices following it that need configuration pushed to them will fail almost immediately.
expected_results: Most config will push successfully with the exception of the RCB and any downstream stream devices.
work_around: Find the first device in the Configuration Service log that fails to take the new configuration.

Option 1: Swap out the problematic device

Option 2: Power down the PoE switch port connected to the problematic device.

If there is a checksum failure on config push, just push config again.

In the field, we removed that device, which was actually in an error state of some sort.

summary: Cannot establish connection to Philips Emergin
description: For version 4.0.405 a connection to Emergin cannot be established.

We are trying to establish a connection to Emergin from a Nurse Call server at New York Presbyterian (601772).  The connection was successfully established in June when the server was on version 4.0.402.  The integration was not fully tested and no further work was done on the project until August. At that time I noticed that the connection was down, and had been since July 28th.  Despite bringing this to the customer’s attention, no troubleshooting was performed.  On October 16th the server was upgraded to 4.0.405.  Since then we have been trying to reestablish the connection to Emergin but have been unsuccessful.  At this time it is unclear if the cause of the current failure is the same as the cause of the initial failure in July.  It is not clear if the upgrade to 4.0.405 is contributing.
root_cause_summary: Security configuration issue on the Emergin side.
investigation_details: The attached log file shows a code 13 coming back from Emergin.  This is Emergin invalid credentials.  We verified this also with a wireshark capture on site that showed the code 13 coming back from the GetSystemStatusSc post.

Looking on the emergin gateway side, security was set to 0 which means Emergin supplies the username password between the  Emergin gateway and the Emergin Server.   The supplied username did not match the expected value in the Emergin web.config file.  When we changed the username values to match, the system started working.
verification_summary: After correctly configuring the Emergin username on the gateway, the system functioned normally.   No changes were needed on the nurse call side.
rca_review_comments: Configuration issue on the Emergin side.

summary: Customer cannot login to Status Board with correct credentials.
description: Active Directory account is unable to login to Status board with correct credentials on production server.   Logging in on a test server with the same credentials does work.
impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
The authentication service currently calls ValidateCredentials (username, password) to check LDAP credentials.  
There is a third parameter, ContextOptions, which we do not use.  
This parameter controls what protocol the ValidateCredentials call uses.  
See [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.directoryservices.accountmanagement.contextoptions?view=net-9.0-pp](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.directoryservices.accountmanagement.contextoptions?view=net-9.0-pp).  
The fixed code will try the ValidateCredentials (username, password) call, but if that call throws an exception,  
it will be caught, and the other form of ValidateCredentials (username, password, ContextOptions) will be tried.  
ContextOptions is an enum that can be parsed from a string, and this value will be in the Settings.xml file  
for the AuthenticationService as key 'RetryContextOptions' with a default value of 1  (which is negotiate, which will go over NTLM or Kerberos, not SSL).

Impact Assessment:  
NCP Status Board - Trivial

Platform Impact:  
Windows (Service Fabric)

Regression Meeting:  
Date:  28/APR/2025  
Attendees - Clifford Feather (Development), Nicholas Jenkins (Quality Engineering)  
Minutes - After discussion with developer, Impact Assessment lowered to Trivial impact. The only change was to Authentication microservice. No impact to Status Board functionality, if we are able to login, then testing is successful. Verify Positive and Negative login tests.

For each Product Functionality / Technical Risk other than trivial:  
N/A

N/A

comment_summary: A site converted from NCM to VNC experienced widespread short-lived RCB Switch Disconnect alerts and random RCB3/GRS7 reboots, which the customer called phantom calls. A long investigation ruled out wiring, recrimping, additional and replacement PoE switches, cable type (found to be CAT6 Superslim), the firewall and the smoke alarm interface, while swapping a trouble room from RCB3/GRS7 to RCB2/GRS5 made the problem disappear and the reverse swap made a quiet room start alarming. Evidence collected included GRS7 brownout events, ntpdate step time adjustments of over 500 days at each restart, device reboots with no exception logs as if power had been lost, and a correlation with rooms configured with a supervised fire alarm push button switch. The issue was finally resolved by disabling all security scanning on the PoE switch and the downstream Linux-based nurse call devices (the Linux-side scanning had been missed earlier) and hard power cycling the PoE switch, after which the unit ran about 39 days without a random reboot.

So the communication to/from RCB3 was disrupted without a power loss in these instances, pointing to issues with data from PoE as well. comment_summary: Multiple SRS units failed at a customer site and were returned for analysis; all four returned units had a shorted LM4675 audio amplifier, with the short between +5V and common, leaving the SRS apparently dead and unable to be rebooted. Database event review showed that around the time of the Lost Primary Audio Station alerts the affected rooms had various unrelated call types (Normal Call, Bed Disconnect, Pillow Speaker Disconnect, Staff Call), with some rooms looping in and out of the Lost Primary Audio Station alert until the SRS was replaced. The same pattern then appeared at a second customer, and syslogs were collected per device for several rooms, while acoustic settings were compared against a working system. The thread ends without an identified cause for the amplifier shorts.

investigation_details: **HW Investigation**

No hardware faults found. Device passes DFCT tests, except for version checks for Linux Kernel, Application, PSoC and PSoC Failsafe. These tests are expected to fail since this device is not the latest hardware/firmware version. Note that VPD read/write and security certificate tests were skipped, in case an overwrite would interfere with firmware’s investigation. FCT logs attached.

In addition to the GRS7, it looks like its associated RCB was also replaced at the customer site:

```
Got the audio working. Conn problem. 
However had to replace RCB. 
Old SN 3013050WIS
New SN 03260B6WM2
```

After the RCB was replaced, the issue was fixed. However, only the GRS7 device was returned by the customer. This makes me think there was an issue with the old RCB and/or it was a configuration/connection issue.

Case Title: Domes and Zones not annunciating correctly

POC: Marcin Kuc
root_cause_summary: Defect
investigation_details: Marcin went onsite and was able to reproduce this on every floor. Stanford 500P Hospital uses RCB2's and Rev B devices.

Setup:

1. Create Room A with a Dome light (port 1).
2. Create a Zone light off Room A's RCB (port 2).
3. Create Room B.
4. Zone Room B on the Zone light.
5. Set Code Blue call (or any call used in this test) to tone on Zone light.
6. Reboot or power-cycle Room A.
7. Place a Code Blue in Room B.  
   (Room A's Dome light will now tone. Zone light works as programmed)
8. Place a Code Blue call from Room A.  
   (problem goes away)
9. Reboot or power-cycle Room A again to reproduce the problem.

Defect opened in Jama under CWS-BUG-2109
rca_review_comments: A software design defect was identified in the Nurse Call system's handling of dome lights and zone lights on RCB2 hardware. Following a reboot or power cycle of a room containing both a dome light and a zone light, call-tone associations could become incorrectly initialized. As a result, Code Blue (and other configured) calls placed from a zoned room triggered audible tones on an unrelated dome light, even though the dome light did not illuminate and the zone light functioned as configured. The condition persisted until a call was placed from the rebooted room, which restored the correct call-tone mapping. The issue was reproducible across multiple floors at Stanford 500P Hospital and was documented under defect **CWS-BUG-2109**

The site is newer and all RCB3s and GRS7s with RCB3 NUCs, and the occurrences are spread across multiple units and campuses rather than isolated to one location; in every observed instance it was the dome light for the originating location, matching the audio station in the affected room. Reviewing the syslogs with a live example found nothing helpful, so APLMOD and DOMELIGHT logging was enabled on all RCBs in two units to capture location, time of occurrence and base call id on the next report.

root_cause_summary: When a child grs7 abnormally disconnects from parent rcb3 abnormally ( In this case the grs7 application experienced a segfault. ).  The rcb3 clears the alert and notifies devices connected to of the cancel.  But doesn’t process the annunciation of the alert which would clear the dome lights, toning, etc… for the alert.

The grs7 is experiencing a seg fault in this scenario while in the RoombusProtocol::sendMessageSync function.  

When logging is turned up to everything in verbose mode the rcb3 can experience a seg fault.  Turning up logging this high is not recommended because of how much it can affect performance.  But the log should be fixed if this is needed for short periods for debugging.
investigation_details: Found issue and created a linked defect.
troubleshooting_steps: Investigated a live example with R&D members, Cliff Feather and Corey Rose. No substantial data gleaned from the device with its current logging levels. Still confirmed issue clears with an RCB reboot
troubleshooting_results: Issue clears with an RCB reboot

root_cause_summary: Bad U1_PWR and bad audio amplifier U9_AUD likely due to an ESD event or hot plugging or a known issue with the bed connector cable (bent pins).
investigation_details: **HW Investigation**

Device would not power up because all power rails were shorted to Ground, which trips fuse RT1. So it failed to initialize on the DFCT (no logs to attach). Confirmed with DMM continuity test that U1_PWR input and output were shorted (pins 2 and 4). Removed U1_PWR and +5V rail was still shorted to Ground but other power rails were normal resistance. U9_AUD was removed and +5V rail and ground were no longer shorted.

Replaced U1_PWR and U9_AUD with known good components. Device now passes DFCT tests, see attached logs. Note that VPD read/write test was skipped in case there were other issues that required firmware investigation.

We have seen this issue before, resulting from bent pins on the bed connector cable, hot plugging, ESD, etc. (Reference https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-1866, https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-1685, https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-1075  and others.)

Conclusion: Bad U1_PWR and bad audio amplifier U9_AUD likely due to an ESD event or hot plugging or a known issue with the bed connector cable (bent pins).

summary: Low Audio from 9 Out of box SRS devices - Fairbanks Memorial
description: 9 SRS devices have poor audio quality (low Audio)   
These were all brand new out of the box, being used for a new install  
Devices have been sent to Cary for RMA > sent to John Fetzner

**Steps taken by Oliver T.**  
Fairbanks is installing a new campus on an existing server running NNC 3.9.401 with NaviCare devices (RCB3s, SRSs, and GRS10s).   
Some of the semi-private rooms have dual SRSs off of the RCB3. In locations with dual SRSs, one of the SRSs has noticeably lower audio volume/quality than the other.  
This happens for SRSs on both RS1 and RS2 depending on the room, we're not sure why the issue presents on different RS ports in different rooms.

I thought it might be a power issue at first. This was supported by the fact that we were seeing brown outs and SRSs not booting.   
We troubleshot and eventually replaced the customer's unsupported Cisco 9300-48P (PoE+) switches with supported Cisco 9300-48U (UPoE) switches.   
We confirmed that the brown outs were resolved and that the RCB3s are now negotiating four pair power, however, the audio issue remains.

Here are some of the other things we've tried:

Reboot RCB3 (no good)  
Re-push firmware (no good)  
Replace RCB3 (no good)  
Move RCB3 and SRS to Hillrom switches (maybe good, inconsistent feedback from onsite resource)  
Test GRS10s on Cisco and Hillrom switches (no good)  
Test with different GRS10s (no good)  
Confirmed NTP (date and time correct, customer does not use low volume period)  
Increased unit volume from 70 to 90 (did increase volume but some SRSs are still noticeably different)  
Captured audio from the VoIP server (audio sounds consistent in the captures)  
Unplugged working SRS and tested rooms with only the non-working SRS (no good, non working SRS still doesn't work)  
This is another indication that it might not be power related

It seems that the issue only occurs when connected to Ciscos, but there has been inconsistent feedback on testing and I'm not confident in saying the switch is the problem.   
That being said, we haven't looked at QoS or packet manipulation yet so that's TBD.  
Oliver was able to look at the acoustic level query, All settings were correct

**Final update**  
Update on the SRS audio issue I posted about the other day. Turns out the issue was with the SRSs. As unlikely as it seems, we had 9 bad SRSs in the batch they used for this install.

_Devices affected_   
Here’s the list of devices with SNs and RCB port they were on:

P2594NNC1B11- SRS W/CODE,
root_cause_summary: No root cause could be determined.  All 9 returned SRSs performed as expected and passed the FCT.  Jared repeated his testing and did not find any issue with the audio.  There is no adjustment or setting in the SRS that can change the audio volume.
investigation_details: J. Fetzner: 9 SRS's that were opened were tested on the FCT and all passed.  Jared Ne-Kindinga: did not find any fault with the units he tested. Each unit’s audio performed as expected within his environment (system).  The 9 serial numbers are listed in the attached spreadsheet.

# SW Investigation Begin:

## Checklist

* \[x\] Device discovers? ✅
* \[x\] Device installs update? ✅ 
* \[x\] Device can configure? ✅ 
* \[x\] Device processes Nurse Call? ✅ 
* \[x\] Device opens audio? ✅ 
* \[x\] If connectivity issues reported, does device not display same behavior at the office?

Reply from IT support:

“In the case comments, the original device was showing offline. The customer had already swapped out the GRS-5 for the GRS-7 and the RCB that was already in the room. During the troubleshooting process, the customer input the new RCB3 in which was having an inconsistent network connection while the customer was also attempting to swap out the audio station. The customer inputted the original device back in the room but swapped out the GRS-5. After so, I configured the GRS-7. And the customer was able to do a functions check.”

# Conclusion: 

No software faults found. Issues with connectivity likely do to environment factors (faulty cable, network interruption at the time, etc.) Tech support conversation suggests network connectivity ~~may have precluded replaced RCB3 (device sent back)~~ . Tech support confirmed connectivity issues were introduced with new RCB3. Given The stable connection at the office, the issue was likely a loose connection or the rj-45 connector not completely seated in the PoE port.

3. Customer checked cabling

6. Device sent back

12 East

The customer confirmed the incident was reported at 9:20 am local time in a specific room, and the team was arranging onsite resources to reproduce the event. No cause or corrective action is established in the thread.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:

Impact Assessment: 
The root cause is an assignment of unit default protocol monitoring settings to a patient as part of a transfer/swap/swing without regard for licensing in the destination unit. Patient safety, as a byproduct of BENO functionality, does not evaluate patient safety licensing and is entirely driven by monitoring values assigned to the patient via the Patient Staff Service.
The solution involves a check on the licensing in the destination unit before assigning monitoring values to a patient. If the destination unit is licensed for a particular risk type, the unit defaults for that risk type are assigned to the patient. If the unit is not licensed for the risk, the monitoring attributes are not added to the patients patient safety monitoring protocol. This functionality is wrapped into the same logic associated risk management for the patient on transfer.
NPS - Licensing - Trivial 
NPS - Protocol Assignment and Removal - Trivial

N/A

Date: Jan/16/2025 
Attendees - David Girardeau (Development Engineering), Rajini Choudhary (Quality Engineering), Bhargav Bhalodia (Quality Engineering), Curtis Jones (Quality Engineering), Akaash Tuteja (Quality Engineering)

QE made all the efforts to update/create the tests and hand pick the TC's related to NPS/BPS functionality that involves assignment and removal of Risks/Protocols. Based on the code changes made, Dev agreed that the listed TC's under Direct and Regression Tests are good to test the changes made to the code and suggested to remove few TC's that are listed below. Disarm Bed Exit
actual_results: Bed Exit Off alert is generated
expected_results: No Patient Safety alerts are placed.
work_around: Enable Patient Safety feature in ECT  
Go to Configure Patient Safety risks page  
At the Enterprise level, Uncheck all check boxes for settings for Falls Risk, Pulmonary Risk, and Skin Risk  
Ensure that these settings are also unchecked for all nursing units.  
Save.  
Disable the Patient Safety Feature.  Save.  
This will fix all new admits, but existing patients can still alert.  
These patients must be either discharged and re-admitted or transferred to a bed IN ANOTHER UNIT and then back to their original bed.

summary: ERM - Warehouse Database StaffTitleKey Missing in Model.DimStaff Table
description: The NavicareReportingNode1Warehouse Model.DimStaff Table contains null values for the StafftTitleKey.
root_cause_summary: StaffTitleId was never populated in the datastore because it was never used on ERM reports. When ERM+ reports came around this field was added to those reports and testing missed that the field is never populated.
investigation_details: The StaffTitleId column in the DataStore dbo.Staff table was never populated. The StaffTitle Id is acutally the TitleId field  
in that table. The column was never populated becasue during the initial release of ERM the StaffTitle was not used on any of  
the canned reports. During the implmentation of several reports on ERM + the StaffTitleId was used as a filtering mechanism for the reports  
and it seems that testing missed this for the release of the product.

It was also brought to our attention of several custom views created by internal teams are pulling the StaffTitleId from the FactStaffVisits table  
where it the value seems to be consistently populated rather than in the Staff record. As a work around I updated the StaffTitleId to match the TitleId  
in the staff table and triggered a full process of the ETL so that data will be pulled into the model. I also add a small trigger to the table so that  
any inserts or updates to the staff record will automatically sync the StaffTitleId with the TitleId.

This is a change that should be implemented for ERM+ so that other customer do not experience the missing filteing on the handleful of ERM+ reports.

summary: Certify Full report is not evaluating call deviations based on the user specified start datetime.
description: **Affected Versions: From initial release (3.9.000) to current.**

The full report call-deviation section (**Certification Deviations - Uncertified Call Devices**) and all-call-certification section (**Certification Details - Certified and Uncertified Call Devices**) do not factor in the user specified start time. investigation_details: **See FCT reports attached here for both devices.**

**45240BAWM2:**

* The unit came with the mfg image (wasn’t upgraded at the customer’s location.)
* No HW or functional issues - FCT full pass.
* (SW Investigation) No deviations from software functionality. 

    * Device functions as expected
    * With OOB failures where device has not yet been updated, there are a number of possible causes related to the hospital’s network environment, and the device’s interaction with that environment that can incorrectly be interpreted as bad out of the box without a little extra time troubleshooting.
    * Without further details of the installation process, and given the device functions as expected in my environment, the root cause is inconclusive.
    

  
**362408CWM2:**

* Touchscreen unresponsive - confirmed during initial bench power-up and FCT too.
* The unit came with the mfg image (wasn’t upgraded at the customer’s location.)
* Further HW analysis in progress.
* **10JUL2025:**

    * After removing the back cover (metal) and connecting the device to RCB3 again, the touchscreen worked as intended without glitches.
    * After unplugging the device from RCB3, the metal cover was mounted back on, and then reconnected to power - and the TS was unresponsive.

comment_summary: GRS7 devices at two customers running 4.0.402.0 became unresponsive to touch, alongside mass RCB3 reboots. Investigation traced a corrupt msglAlertRequest packet being sent from the device service and captured it with Wireshark on port 50005, although the packet appeared to be discarded at the NUC and was judged a symptom rather than the cause; logging was raised on the alert socket, gateway service socket and config update server, and the SmartSync socket was eliminated because many rebooting RCB3s have no SRS attached. The reboots were found to originate from the REBOOT ALL ROOMS function on the nurse console GRS10H, and after that option was removed from the GRS10Hs the GRS7 touchscreen cases stopped and declined hospital-wide. Four GRS7s were returned under NCMR0424865; bench testing reproduced a screen freeze five times within fewer than 1000 reboot iterations on field manufacturer code (OS 2.4.166-0-gdd730c2) and saw no issue over 3000 reboots on updated code (OS 2.4.168-1-gd84a07f), and the resulting investigational patch was applied at the second site across 84 GRS7s.

root_cause_summary: The combination of the removing i2c commands sent to the device in the linux kernel driver when the nurse call application would startup or exit before reboot and the removing reset gpio being triggered at startup resolved the issue.  The gpio reset not successful resetting the touchscreen part seems to be a hardware flaw that can be worked around by this software modification.
investigation_details: The scenario where the device is rebooted remotely via the primary console or secondary console reboot rooms screen seems to put the touchscreen part into a state where it can’t be reset via the reset gpio pin.  During a soft or hard reboot the reset gpio is typically used to reset the device.

The driver also had some behaviors that could have contributed to getting the device in a state that would not allow it to reset.  There were several state changes that triggered i2c command being sent to the touchscreen controller when the nurse call application would start up and connect to the touch controller for event notification. 

Removing both the attempt to reset the touchscreen part with the gpio pin and the additional unnecessary commands being sent in the driver resolved the issue.
verification_summary: Opened NCMR0424865. 

Removing both the attempt to reset the touchscreen part with the gpio pin and the additional unnecessary commands being sent in the driver resolved the issue.

Submitted NCBL-3369 to change the startup sequence with the touchscreen controller to address issue.

summary: When a GRS7 hardware revision with part number P2594VNC7C11 is soft rebooted in some cases the touchscreen does not accept touch input.
description: When the REBOOT ALL ROOMS function on the GRS-10 is used there is potential for the touchscreen on the GRS-7’s to freeze up and one would need to reboot the GRS-7 to resolve the problem.
impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Before:  Touchscreen drivers were compiled into the linux kernel for the grs7 and grs10h.  And a gpio reset was defined for each touch screen controller driver for different hardware revs of the grs7 or grs10h.  Compiling the modules into the kernel caused them to be run one at a time at boot.  
After: Touchscreen drivers are compiled as kernel modules.  An init script is used during boot to load each one in a specified order until a touchscreen device is detected.  The atmel max touch driver used by the GRS7 hardware rev with part number P2594VNC7C11 will be attempted first.  And the gpio reset will not be used for the driver.  Using the gpio reset was determined to cause the issue.

Impact Assessment:  
NCP - Hardware - Minor

Platform Impact:  
GRS10H, GRS7

Regression Meeting:  
Date - 18/NOV/2024

Attendees:   
Quality Engineering - Bhargav Bhalodia  
Development Engineering - Steve Moore

Minutes -  
Brief Summary on the changes:    
\--> There was a change done on GRS7 and GRS10H to use the correct UI drivers upon boot up. The testing identified covers the usage of correct drivers and some reliability testing. 

Does Impact description describe the changes: Yes  
If no, more info needed?: Nope.   
Test scenario's discussed: UI testing, Upgrade test and which all devices to test.   
Other areas impacted and discussed: None

All test according to above Filter: No  
If No, then why?: Changes are mainly around using of correct drivers. The Product functionality yielded more hardware specific test so they were not included as regression. Check the "NC-7998.xls" file for tests that are not considered.   
New Objectives needed: No.  
Is performance testing needed: No  
Upgrade vs New install test needed: No  
Patient Safety impacted:  No

summary: Calls not clearing from Status board (intermittent)
description: VNC 4.1

After the upgrade site is experiencing intermittent stuck calls on status board, These calls are not showing on end devices, GRS5,GRS7 or GRS10’s only Status board

Most of the stuck calls are Bed exit and chair alarm calls

However I have seen a call cord disconnect be stuck, we went to the room, placed another call cord disconnect call, plugged call cord in, the newest call cleared but the old did not, which it remained on status board.

Tried multiple tests around 12:30 pm local, 3:30 est, North tower 4th floor RM 71. we placed bed exit calls, entered the room. adjusted the bed and canceled from the GRS7, alert then cleared from Status board.

While cleaning up the test room, customer turned bed exit off. Took weights off bed, zeroed the bed, call triggered and remained active in status board but not on the GRS10. Had to restart services to clear.

Restarting status board services clears the calls every time

This issue seemingly is happening across the whole site, North tower 4th floor showing the most issues.
comment_summary: Calls intermittently failed to clear from the Status board at sites running 4.1.200, severely enough that one customer paused remaining upgrade projects. Device Service Host logs for a stuck call showed the de-duplication logic failing to trigger, producing a SQL error 2601 "Cannot insert duplicate key row in object 'NCC.V_ActiveCall' with unique index 'AK_UniqueActiveCallGUID'" so call creation was abandoned, after which every subsequent status update (Answered, Cancel) failed with SQL error 257 "Implicit conversion from data type nvarchar to timestamp is not allowed" and the call never cleared. The suspicion was that a secondary or monitoring console reports the alert with the same BaseCallID but a different RequestingDeviceId, causing IsDuplicateAlertNotification() in AlertMessageHandler.cs to fail, and the affected units all used secondary consoles and unit monitoring. A separate bug was also found in the call_update stored procedure, where the row edition check compares @RowEdition to itself rather than to the stored RowEdition. The workaround that resolved it was setting MaxNumMessageProcessingThreads to 1 in the Device Service appsettings.json file, after which no further stuck-call reports were made at either site.

comment_summary: A certification deviation report listed Lost RLR calls whose originating locations were not from the nursing unit selected in the report parameters, had no RLRs configured and no active Lost RLR calls, and whose device URIs corresponded to device types other than RLRs. A previously used fix from a related RCA did not help. Investigation found the stored procedure behind the report queries across multiple databases, which can join data incorrectly; passing a comma delimited list of the nursing unit's locations into Cert.CertificationReport_GetSystemAlerts reproduced the same three rows, and a modified copy of the stored procedure returned the expected Locator device type rows. The site could proceed with certification without a code fix by power cycling three named RCBs to clear the lost RLR calls or by removing the RLRs from ECT, and the resulting defect NCBL-1614 was later closed with no fix planned because RLRs are not supported after 3.9.300.

summary: When a GRS7 hardware revision with part number P2594VNC7C11 is soft rebooted in some cases the touchscreen does not accept touch input.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Before:  Touchscreen drivers were compiled into the linux kernel for the grs7 and grs10h.  And a gpio reset was defined for each touch screen controller driver for different hardware revs of the grs7 or grs10h.  Compiling the modules into the kernel caused them to be run one at a time at boot.  
After: Touchscreen drivers are compiled as kernel modules.  An init script is used during boot to load each one in a specified order until a touchscreen device is detected.  The atmel max touch driver used by the GRS7 hardware rev with part number P2594VNC7C11 will be attempted first.  And the gpio reset will not be used for the driver.  Using the gpio reset was determined to cause the issue.

NCP - Hardware - Minor

Platform Impact:

Regression Meeting:  
Date - 18/NOV/2024

Attendees:

Development Engineering - Steve Moore

Minutes -

summary: When a GRS7 hardware revision with part number P2594VNC7C11 is soft rebooted in some cases the touchscreen does not accept touch input.
description: When the REBOOT ALL ROOMS function on the GRS-10 is used there is potential for the touchscreen on the GRS-7’s to freeze up and one would need to reboot the GRS-7 to resolve the problem.
impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Before:  Touchscreen drivers were compiled into the linux kernel for the grs7 and grs10h.  And a gpio reset was defined for each touch screen controller driver for different hardware revs of the grs7 or grs10h.  Compiling the modules into the kernel caused them to be run one at a time at boot.  
After: Touchscreen drivers are compiled as kernel modules.  An init script is used during boot to load each one in a specified order until a touchscreen device is detected.  The atmel max touch driver used by the GRS7 hardware rev with part number P2594VNC7C11 will be attempted first.  And the gpio reset will not be used for the driver.  Using the gpio reset was determined to cause the issue.

Impact Assessment:  
NCP - Hardware - Minor

Platform Impact:  
GRS10H, GRS7

Regression Meeting:  
Date - 18/NOV/2024

Attendees:   
Quality Engineering - Bhargav Bhalodia  
Development Engineering - Steve Moore

Minutes -  
Brief Summary on the changes:    
\--> There was a change done on GRS7 and GRS10H to use the correct UI drivers upon boot up. The testing identified covers the usage of correct drivers and some reliability testing.

comment_summary: Multiple customers reported GRS10H light bars remaining active after a Code call with no active calls present, across versions 4.0.401, 4.0.402, 4.0.2.11 and 4.1.001. Remote checks confirmed an active light bar while the alerts list showed only device state lines and no active calls, and in one site's syslogs the line "Invalid URI when attempting to find an entry in the route table route table" appeared, though it was not found in the other affected devices' syslogs. The issue has generally appeared once per device and not recurred after a reboot, which customers use as a workaround, although one site reported it as ongoing and widespread for all call types. A defect NC-6563 was raised as a fix for the possible cause, targeted for 4.1.300, and a suggestion was made to make the APLMOD and ROOMBUS logging facilities verbose at installation to capture better evidence.

summary: GRS-10H light bar continues to flash without active call
description: Multiple customers have reported light bars remaining illuminated/flashing after calls are canceled (expected behavior is to cease illuminating flashing). R&D has not been able to reproduce the error.

R&D developers suspect the cause is a multithreading bug in the modgrs10h handler which would update the lightbar state out of order. That theory would explain both (1) how the light bar becomes out-of-sync with the call status and (2) why rebooting the device resolves the issue in the field as explained in https://hill-rom.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-1028. In layman’s terms, under certain conditions (which are difficult to replicate), programmed instructions that control lightbar illumination could execute out of the intended order.

The proposed fix in the Investigational Patch is twofold:

1. Change how the modgrs10h handler pushes lightbar actions to threads
2. ~~As a fallback, add a "LightbarEnabled" option in the /opt/local/hrapps/nnc/bin/env.json config file. This option turns the lightbar light off as long as the "LighbarEnabled" option is set to false.~~
comment_summary: The thread covers a field defect where the GRS-10H light bar continues to flash with no active call. Investigation identified an alert getting stuck on in the lightbar handler; the stuck alert does not preempt higher priority alerts, but once a higher priority alert clears the stale lower priority alert reappears. An investigational patch built as an emb-base-package GRS10H-only build was deployed to a customer site and appeared to resolve the problem, and a later bugfix build was produced for dry run. The team decided not to commercialize the contingency LightbarEnabled configuration option, added call placement and handling tests to regression, and closed the defect after all tests passed and the fix was verified.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Before:  
The modgrs10h handler had a possible multithreading bug which would update the lightbar state out of order. If the last update of the alert is on, then the lightbar will remain on until the next nnc reboot.  
After:  
The modgrs10h handler now pushes all lightbar actions to the correct thread, and looks up the most recent data instead of relying on possibly stale alert data. This should resolve any issues with the lightbar using old or out of order alert data to decide its state.

Impact Assessment:  
NNC - Call Placement and Handling - Minor: functionality should not be impacted except for the extremely rare bug specific to the lightbar, which is attempted to be fixed in this IP

Platform Impact:  
GRS10h

Regression Meeting:  
Date:  17/DEC/2024  
Attendees - Stephen Moore (Development Engineering), Bhargav Bhalodia (Quality Engineering), Kyle Willey (Quality Engineering)  
Minutes - Group discussed test coverage and strategy to try to surface a possible reproduction strategy for the direct test being created. Regressions are largely identified out of filter though the identified Impact area is considered the most appropriate for the Defect. Most of the testing in filter covers call placement and handling functionality unrelated to the GRS10h Lightbar. Supplemental tests specific to GRS10h Lightbar were added for suitable regression coverage. See CWS-FLD-4365 GRS10H Lightbar in Jama.

Additional Software Components:

investigation_details: HW Investigation: Device fails FCT test for Handset speaker (Measured 1.537V, Expected 0.8\~1.4V). Also fails App, PSoC and PSoC Failsafe verifications but since this device is not the latest hardware with the latest firmware, those version checks are expected to fail. See attached logs.
**UPDATE** 18 March 2026: Re-ran device on FCT and Handset speaker test is now passing. The earlier failure is likely due to a test setup issue; speaker/microphone tests are sensitive to placement and positioning of the device. App, PSoC and PSoC Failsafe verifications still fail because this device is not the latest hardware wth latest firmware, so this is expected. FCT logs attached (“P2500VNC3C00242414FWM2_R001_20260317_155601_FULL_FAIL.zip”).
**UPDATE** 8/6/2026: The GRS10H was bench-tested under controlled conditions to re-validate Code Blue annunciation. During testing, a Code Blue call was successfully received, and the device generated the expected audible tone. Tried out with multiple RCBs and GRS7s. Visual notification also performed as expected, with the light bar flashing correctly for the event. Repeated bench checks did not reproduce the no-audio condition reported in the field, and current observed behavior is normal for both audible and visual alerting.
At this stage, no additional historical logs were available for analysis because server-side logs had already been rotated/wiped prior to collection. As a result, direct event-level correlation for the original occurrence could not be completed. Based on current evidence, the issue appears transient/intermittent and is not presently reproducible in bench validation.

description: Complaint:

* New Install for Unit 1 ED - Unit is still in certification phase and is not a live site yet

Case Title: Domes and Zones not annunciating correctly

POC: Marcin Kuc
root_cause_summary: Defect
investigation_details: Marcin went onsite and was able to reproduce this on every floor. Stanford 500P Hospital uses RCB2's and Rev B devices.

Setup:

1. Create Room A with a Dome light (port 1).
2. Create a Zone light off Room A's RCB (port 2).
3. Create Room B.
4. Zone Room B on the Zone light.
5. Set Code Blue call (or any call used in this test) to tone on Zone light.
6. Reboot or power-cycle Room A.
7. Place a Code Blue in Room B.  
   (Room A's Dome light will now tone. Zone light works as programmed)
8. Place a Code Blue call from Room A.  
   (problem goes away)
9. Reboot or power-cycle Room A again to reproduce the problem.

Defect opened in Jama under CWS-BUG-2109
rca_review_comments: A software design defect was identified in the Nurse Call system's handling of dome lights and zone lights on RCB2 hardware. Following a reboot or power cycle of a room containing both a dome light and a zone light, call-tone associations could become incorrectly initialized. As a result, Code Blue (and other configured) calls placed from a zoned room triggered audible tones on an unrelated dome light, even though the dome light did not illuminate and the zone light functioned as configured. The condition persisted until a call was placed from the rebooted room, which restored the correct call-tone mapping. The issue was reproducible across multiple floors at Stanford 500P Hospital and was documented under defect **CWS-BUG-2109**

summary: GRS-10H light bar continues to flash without active call
description: Multiple customers have reported light bars remaining illuminated/flashing after calls are canceled (expected behavior is to cease illuminating flashing). R&D has not been able to reproduce the error.

R&D developers suspect the cause is a multithreading bug in the modgrs10h handler which would update the lightbar state out of order. That theory would explain both (1) how the light bar becomes out-of-sync with the call status and (2) why rebooting the device resolves the issue in the field as explained in https://hill-rom.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-1028. In layman’s terms, under certain conditions (which are difficult to replicate), programmed instructions that control lightbar illumination could execute out of the intended order.

The proposed fix in the Investigational Patch is twofold:

1. Change how the modgrs10h handler pushes lightbar actions to threads
2. ~~As a fallback, add a "LightbarEnabled" option in the /opt/local/hrapps/nnc/bin/env.json config file. This option turns the lightbar light off as long as the "LighbarEnabled" option is set to false.~~
comment_summary: The thread covers a field defect where the GRS-10H light bar continues to flash with no active call. Investigation identified an alert getting stuck on in the lightbar handler; the stuck alert does not preempt higher priority alerts, but once a higher priority alert clears the stale lower priority alert reappears. An investigational patch built as an emb-base-package GRS10H-only build was deployed to a customer site and appeared to resolve the problem, and a later bugfix build was produced for dry run. The team decided not to commercialize the contingency LightbarEnabled configuration option, added call placement and handling tests to regression, and closed the defect after all tests passed and the fix was verified.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Before:  
The modgrs10h handler had a possible multithreading bug which would update the lightbar state out of order. If the last update of the alert is on, then the lightbar will remain on until the next nnc reboot.  
After:  
The modgrs10h handler now pushes all lightbar actions to the correct thread, and looks up the most recent data instead of relying on possibly stale alert data. This should resolve any issues with the lightbar using old or out of order alert data to decide its state.

Impact Assessment:  
NNC - Call Placement and Handling - Minor: functionality should not be impacted except for the extremely rare bug specific to the lightbar, which is attempted to be fixed in this IP

Platform Impact:  
GRS10h

Regression Meeting:  
Date:  17/DEC/2024  
Attendees - Stephen Moore (Development Engineering), Bhargav Bhalodia (Quality Engineering), Kyle Willey (Quality Engineering)  
Minutes - Group discussed test coverage and strategy to try to surface a possible reproduction strategy for the direct test being created. Regressions are largely identified out of filter though the identified Impact area is considered the most appropriate for the Defect. Most of the testing in filter covers call placement and handling functionality unrelated to the GRS10h Lightbar. Supplemental tests specific to GRS10h Lightbar were added for suitable regression coverage. See CWS-FLD-4365 GRS10H Lightbar in Jama.

Additional Software Components:  
N/A

summary: GRS-10H light bar continues to flash without active call
description: Multiple customers have reported light bars remaining illuminated/flashing after calls are canceled (expected behavior is to cease illuminating flashing). R&D has not been able to reproduce the error.

R&D developers suspect the cause is a multithreading bug in the modgrs10h handler which would update the lightbar state out of order. That theory would explain both (1) how the light bar becomes out-of-sync with the call status and (2) why rebooting the device resolves the issue in the field as explained in https://hill-rom.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-1028. In layman’s terms, under certain conditions (which are difficult to replicate), programmed instructions that control lightbar illumination could execute out of the intended order.

The proposed fix in the Investigational Patch is twofold:

1. Change how the modgrs10h handler pushes lightbar actions to threads
2. ~~As a fallback, add a "LightbarEnabled" option in the /opt/local/hrapps/nnc/bin/env.json config file. This option turns the lightbar light off as long as the "LighbarEnabled" option is set to false.~~
comment_summary: The thread covers a field defect where the GRS-10H light bar continues to flash with no active call. Investigation identified an alert getting stuck on in the lightbar handler; the stuck alert does not preempt higher priority alerts, but once a higher priority alert clears the stale lower priority alert reappears. An investigational patch built as an emb-base-package GRS10H-only build was deployed to a customer site and appeared to resolve the problem, and a later bugfix build was produced for dry run. The team decided not to commercialize the contingency LightbarEnabled configuration option, added call placement and handling tests to regression, and closed the defect after all tests passed and the fix was verified.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Before:  
The modgrs10h handler had a possible multithreading bug which would update the lightbar state out of order. If the last update of the alert is on, then the lightbar will remain on until the next nnc reboot.  
After:  
The modgrs10h handler now pushes all lightbar actions to the correct thread, and looks up the most recent data instead of relying on possibly stale alert data. This should resolve any issues with the lightbar using old or out of order alert data to decide its state.

Impact Assessment:  
NNC - Call Placement and Handling - Minor: functionality should not be impacted except for the extremely rare bug specific to the lightbar, which is attempted to be fixed in this IP

Platform Impact:  
GRS10h

Regression Meeting:  
Date:  17/DEC/2024  
Attendees - Stephen Moore (Development Engineering), Bhargav Bhalodia (Quality Engineering), Kyle Willey (Quality Engineering)  
Minutes - Group discussed test coverage and strategy to try to surface a possible reproduction strategy for the direct test being created. Regressions are largely identified out of filter though the identified Impact area is considered the most appropriate for the Defect. Most of the testing in filter covers call placement and handling functionality unrelated to the GRS10h Lightbar. Supplemental tests specific to GRS10h Lightbar were added for suitable regression coverage. See CWS-FLD-4365 GRS10H Lightbar in Jama.

Additional Software Components:  
N/A

summary: NC- CCD GRS10 CPU spiking
description: Site :LOMA LINDA UNIVERSITY MED CNTR

Acct # 605005

NC version: 3.9.201.11

Effected GRS10: 1 East PBX Central Station PC 10.251.214.218  013202GZWIS

GRS10 software version(ServicePortal): A 3.9.3.4 K 3.9.100.3165 M 3.9.100.3165

Issue: GRS10 consistently using 99% CPU and flahsing Lost primary console. The lost primary console alert flashes for a second then clears. 

Context: CCD GRS10 is the  primary console for 1 East Wing CCD PBX Center. The unit only has the GRS10, a RCB3 NUC, and a RCB3.  
CCD is monitoring LLUH Building and LLUMC CTP Tower. 50 rooms for LLUH Building are being monitored. LLUMC CTP Tower has 1253 rooms being monitored. 

Steps taken:

Removed all plugins besides calls from CCD. No change to CPU usage.  
Purged config from CCD. No change.  
Removed floors 7-12 from secondary units from CCD. No change.

Increased logging levels for MSGCTLR, MODCONN,SYSBASE.  
Removed all units from secondary units from CCD. CPU usage stabilized. Monitored for 5 minutes. No alerting.  
Placed back all monitored units to CCD. CPU usage remained stable. Tested two code blue calls for different rooms. Confirmed CCD received calls.  
When i placed all units back to be monitored i just selected the whole unit. After testing with the customer i went back in to remove staff locations and zone lights.  
This begs the question why wouldn't the issue be present when technically after all units were added back it was monitoring more than it was initially. 

RCA request: Need to confirm the limitations for a CCD monitoring units.  
Need to determine why removal of units allowed CCD to stabilize but adding them back did not reproduce the issue.
comment_summary: A CCD GRS10 console was spiking in CPU and generating Lost Primary Console alerts. Syslogs and advanced service logs were collected and the console stabilised after the plugins enabled on it and the secondary monitored locations were temporarily removed; the combination of enabled plugins and the number of monitored units was identified as the cause of the spiking. The recommendation given was to add a second GRS10 CCD to split the workload if the site adds more rooms or units, though the thread notes there is no published specification for how many devices a CCD can monitor. A later comment links this behaviour to another RCA, suggesting removing monitored units helps because it removes the ability for the message to bounce around in the system.

summary: GRS-10H light bar continues to flash without active call
description: Multiple customers have reported light bars remaining illuminated/flashing after calls are canceled (expected behavior is to cease illuminating flashing). R&D has not been able to reproduce the error.

R&D developers suspect the cause is a multithreading bug in the modgrs10h handler which would update the lightbar state out of order. That theory would explain both (1) how the light bar becomes out-of-sync with the call status and (2) why rebooting the device resolves the issue in the field as explained in https://hill-rom.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-1028. In layman’s terms, under certain conditions (which are difficult to replicate), programmed instructions that control lightbar illumination could execute out of the intended order.

The proposed fix in the Investigational Patch is twofold:

1. Change how the modgrs10h handler pushes lightbar actions to threads
2. ~~As a fallback, add a "LightbarEnabled" option in the /opt/local/hrapps/nnc/bin/env.json config file. This option turns the lightbar light off as long as the "LighbarEnabled" option is set to false.~~
comment_summary: The thread covers a field defect where the GRS-10H light bar continues to flash with no active call. Investigation identified an alert getting stuck on in the lightbar handler; the stuck alert does not preempt higher priority alerts, but once a higher priority alert clears the stale lower priority alert reappears. An investigational patch built as an emb-base-package GRS10H-only build was deployed to a customer site and appeared to resolve the problem, and a later bugfix build was produced for dry run. The team decided not to commercialize the contingency LightbarEnabled configuration option, added call placement and handling tests to regression, and closed the defect after all tests passed and the fix was verified.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Before:  
The modgrs10h handler had a possible multithreading bug which would update the lightbar state out of order. If the last update of the alert is on, then the lightbar will remain on until the next nnc reboot.  
After:  
The modgrs10h handler now pushes all lightbar actions to the correct thread, and looks up the most recent data instead of relying on possibly stale alert data. This should resolve any issues with the lightbar using old or out of order alert data to decide its state.

Impact Assessment:  
NNC - Call Placement and Handling - Minor: functionality should not be impacted except for the extremely rare bug specific to the lightbar, which is attempted to be fixed in this IP

Platform Impact:  
GRS10h

Regression Meeting:  
Date:  17/DEC/2024  
Attendees - Stephen Moore (Development Engineering), Bhargav Bhalodia (Quality Engineering), Kyle Willey (Quality Engineering)  
Minutes - Group discussed test coverage and strategy to try to surface a possible reproduction strategy for the direct test being created. Regressions are largely identified out of filter though the identified Impact area is considered the most appropriate for the Defect. Most of the testing in filter covers call placement and handling functionality unrelated to the GRS10h Lightbar. Supplemental tests specific to GRS10h Lightbar were added for suitable regression coverage. See CWS-FLD-4365 GRS10H Lightbar in Jama.

Additional Software Components:  
N/A

comment_summary: Multiple customers reported GRS10H light bars remaining active after a Code call with no active calls present, across versions 4.0.401, 4.0.402, 4.0.2.11 and 4.1.001. Remote checks confirmed an active light bar while the alerts list showed only device state lines and no active calls, and in one site's syslogs the line "Invalid URI when attempting to find an entry in the route table route table" appeared, though it was not found in the other affected devices' syslogs. impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Before:  
The modgrs10h handler had a possible multithreading bug which would update the lightbar state out of order. If the last update of the alert is on, then the lightbar will remain on until the next nnc reboot.  
After:  
The modgrs10h handler now pushes all lightbar actions to the correct thread, and looks up the most recent data instead of relying on possibly stale alert data. This should resolve any issues with the lightbar using old or out of order alert data to decide its state.

Impact Assessment:  
NNC - Call Placement and Handling - Minor: functionality should not be impacted except for the extremely rare bug specific to the lightbar, which is attempted to be fixed in this IP

Platform Impact:  
GRS10h

Regression Meeting:  
Date:  17/DEC/2024  
Attendees - Stephen Moore (Development Engineering), Bhargav Bhalodia (Quality Engineering), Kyle Willey (Quality Engineering)  
Minutes - Group discussed test coverage and strategy to try to surface a possible reproduction strategy for the direct test being created. Regressions are largely identified out of filter though the identified Impact area is considered the most appropriate for the Defect. Most of the testing in filter covers call placement and handling functionality unrelated to the GRS10h Lightbar. Supplemental tests specific to GRS10h Lightbar were added for suitable regression coverage. See CWS-FLD-4365 GRS10H Lightbar in Jama.

Additional Software Components:  
N/A

comment_summary: Multiple customers reported GRS10H light bars remaining active after a Code call with no active calls present, across versions 4.0.401, 4.0.402, 4.0.2.11 and 4.1.001. Remote checks confirmed an active light bar while the alerts list showed only device state lines and no active calls, and in one site's syslogs the line "Invalid URI when attempting to find an entry in the route table route table" appeared, though it was not found in the other affected devices' syslogs. The issue has generally appeared once per device and not recurred after a reboot, which customers use as a workaround, although one site reported it as ongoing and widespread for all call types. A defect NC-6563 was raised as a fix for the possible cause, targeted for 4.1.300, and a suggestion was made to make the APLMOD and ROOMBUS logging facilities verbose at installation to capture better evidence.

summary: GRS-10H light bar continues to flash without active call
description: Multiple customers have reported light bars remaining illuminated/flashing after calls are canceled (expected behavior is to cease illuminating flashing). R&D has not been able to reproduce the error.

R&D developers suspect the cause is a multithreading bug in the modgrs10h handler which would update the lightbar state out of order. That theory would explain both (1) how the light bar becomes out-of-sync with the call status and (2) why rebooting the device resolves the issue in the field as explained in https://hill-rom.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-1028. In layman’s terms, under certain conditions (which are difficult to replicate), programmed instructions that control lightbar illumination could execute out of the intended order.

The proposed fix in the Investigational Patch is twofold:

1. Change how the modgrs10h handler pushes lightbar actions to threads
2. ~~As a fallback, add a "LightbarEnabled" option in the /opt/local/hrapps/nnc/bin/env.json config file. This option turns the lightbar light off as long as the "LighbarEnabled" option is set to false.~~
comment_summary: The thread covers a field defect where the GRS-10H light bar continues to flash with no active call. Investigation identified an alert getting stuck on in the lightbar handler; the stuck alert does not preempt higher priority alerts, but once a higher priority alert clears the stale lower priority alert reappears. An investigational patch built as an emb-base-package GRS10H-only build was deployed to a customer site and appeared to resolve the problem, and a later bugfix build was produced for dry run. The team decided not to commercialize the contingency LightbarEnabled configuration option, added call placement and handling tests to regression, and closed the defect after all tests passed and the fix was verified.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Before:  
The modgrs10h handler had a possible multithreading bug which would update the lightbar state out of order. If the last update of the alert is on, then the lightbar will remain on until the next nnc reboot.  
After:  
The modgrs10h handler now pushes all lightbar actions to the correct thread, and looks up the most recent data instead of relying on possibly stale alert data. This should resolve any issues with the lightbar using old or out of order alert data to decide its state.

Impact Assessment:  
NNC - Call Placement and Handling - Minor: functionality should not be impacted except for the extremely rare bug specific to the lightbar, which is attempted to be fixed in this IP

Platform Impact:  
GRS10h

Regression Meeting:  
Date:  17/DEC/2024  
Attendees - Stephen Moore (Development Engineering), Bhargav Bhalodia (Quality Engineering), Kyle Willey (Quality Engineering)  
Minutes - Group discussed test coverage and strategy to try to surface a possible reproduction strategy for the direct test being created. Regressions are largely identified out of filter though the identified Impact area is considered the most appropriate for the Defect. Most of the testing in filter covers call placement and handling functionality unrelated to the GRS10h Lightbar. Supplemental tests specific to GRS10h Lightbar were added for suitable regression coverage. See CWS-FLD-4365 GRS10H Lightbar in Jama.

Additional Software Components:  
N/A

expected_results: Light on GRS-10H is cancelled.

root_cause_summary: Out of 2 devices one is working fine, HW and SW testing completed. Other device DC regulator not working properly.
investigation_details: For more details about the devices, see attachments.

**GRS10H (MRB 58):**  
Bench Testing: Powered ON, couldn't replicate issue.  
RCB3 connection: Powered ON  
PoE power: Turning ON

FCT: Stand micro phone and handset speaker failed dues high voltage(volume) than expected.

After updating software with latest version, passed FCT.

**GRS10H(MRB 4):**  
Bench testing:  
Light Bar always dim red and flickering.  
Low screen brightness as per complaint.

FCT:  
Light Bar test failed.  
Low screen brightness

Putty Software:  
VPD Data: Run time :104Days,13 hours.

After opening the device:  
Continuity: checked Continuity from the PSOC to JWT connector and DC regulator, passed  
Checked voltage levels at LED Connector, pin1 getting \~ 34V instead of 12V.

Then checked With DC regulator U3_PWR:  
Input voltage: As expected 36V.  
Output:36V to 12V IC output voltage \~34V, almost equal to input

Final Observation:  
DC regulator U3_PWR(MAX5081ATE) not working properly, voltage at output \~34V which is not as expected(12V).

root_cause_summary: The connector should be modified to only raise button press events if there is one in the ModelUpdate.Events collection.
investigation_details: When the connector starts (or even when a tag is discovered and the connector is already running or when the connector re-connects), the HPL system will send an initial state of the tag to the rtls connector.  The RTLS connector will receive that message and, because it has a “buttonPress”, it’ll interpret it as a click even though the message also indicates the button press occurred at the beginning of time. So, every time the RTLS Connector disconnects and re-connects to HPL, we’d get one of these mass reporting events; with every single tag that’s assigned at that moment generating a duress call.

HPL does not re-set the timestamp back to `DateTime.MinValue` (ever). So it’ll only be that value if the button has never been clicked. So this fix could get tricky as you’d need to make a decision based on the last time the tag reported. Or something. I’d be happy to rubber duck solution options.
verification_summary: Defect identified; refer to https://hill-rom.atlassian.net/browse/NC-665#icft=NC-665.
rca_review_comments: Investigation determined there is a defect.  The connector should be modified to only raise button press events if there is one in the ModelUpdate.Events collection.

comment_summary: Duress alerts at a 4.0.400 site kept sounding after being cancelled. Investigation of the RTLS connector logs found Centrak sending duplicate button events in the same data packet (entries ending 'button2, button2'), and the IntegrationService log showed the IHEAdapter repeatedly failing to reach a development host with "The remote name could not be resolved: 'hi-dev-nnc1.hrdev.io'", a value hard-coded in the app config that applies to all sites without a PCD-05 integration. Packet captures on the Centrak UDP port and the locating TCP port showed the RTLS connector sending correct data while the IntegrationService was updating and placing new calls. Adding the server name to the clinical database connection key in ClinicalApi.CallAdapter.dll.config and turning off auto cancellation for the Duress call type stopped the repeat duress calls, and the behaviour was reproduced by running the clinical interface call adapter with no SQL server in the connection string and placing duress alerts rapidly, or by injecting a 10 second sleep in the same code path.

root_cause_summary: Code requiring a proper sql connection was placed in the integration service, but this connection is rarely filled out, because the related feature is not used at all sites.  The long period of time required for the sql connection to time out causes issues with other code functionality.

A sql server connection is attempted on a regularly scheduled basis, but no connection can be made, and this process takes 30 seconds or more.   Meanwhile, the button press messages back up behind the sql connection attempt and are not serviced promptly, causing the delay in cancellation.

summary: Status Board crashing due to Service Fabric CPU issues
description: Riddle Memorial Hospital started experiencing spiked 100% CPU on the Enterprise server.  The two processes taking the CPU mainly are Fabric.exe and Fabricgateway.exe.  Troubleshooting with customer they have crowdstrike installed and had set it in bypass mode.  No change.  No other AV or scanning agent appears to be installed on this server.  Stopping Service Fabric will cause the server to run normally, without statusboard of course.  Once Service Fabric is started, the CPU will begin to spike off and on and customer is getting status board down messages as the spiking comes and goes.  Seems to be frequent, but no rhythm to the spiking.  I’ve had statusboard running for as long as about 5-6 minutes, but usually every minute or so will cycle. 

removed the Statusboard mircroservice, had issues deploying it successfully.  Would stick on Copying application to image store...

Decided to remove the cluster

Uninstalled Service Fabric, reinstalled successfully

continued to have some issues deploying microservices, but deploying them one by one seemed to get everything back successfully.

Continue seeing same issue with CPU spiking 100% and status board going offline due to timeout.

asked customer IT if there are any issues seen with the VMware host this server is running on or anything that occurred prior to 3/14/23 before issue was reported.  Case opened on 3/14/23 at 10:14 AM EST

attached advanced service logs and HMS logs to case which were pulled on 3/15 prior to service fabric reinstall

Event Viewer shows FabricApplicationGateway crashes started occurring at 3/14/23 1:19:26 PM

Server was rebooted on 3/15 at approximately 3:45 to see if issue would go away, no change

Server had been running for over 21 days until reboot 3/15/23
root_cause_summary: Probable cause, not confirmed: a browser update broke Status Board's SignalR websocket connections. At Riddle Memorial (VNC 4.0.300) Fabric.exe and FabricGateway.exe drove the enterprise server to 100% CPU and Status Board dropped offline about every minute, starting on 3/14/2023 right after Microsoft Edge updated on the server. The customer lets Edge auto-update on about 10,000 workstations. Jim Price matched it to https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/browse/TACO-7604#icft=TACO-7604 (UVA), where a Chromium websocket change broke SignalR; that was fixed with new SignalR and Service Fabric versions in 3.9.602 and 4.0.400.
investigation_details: Steve Martin bypassed CrowdStrike, removed and redeployed the Status Board microservice and cluster, reinstalled Service Fabric and rebooted, with no change; stopping Service Fabric brought CPU back to normal (3/14-3/16/2023). Jim Price identified the https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/browse/TACO-7604#icft=TACO-7604 match (3/16/2023). Matt Tague, after discussion with Jim Price and Phanindra Atmakuri, recommended upgrading to 4.0.400 or later (3/17/2023).

Corrective action: upgrade to 4.0.400 or later. The ticket doesn't confirm Riddle upgraded or that the upgrade resolved it.

comment_summary: Rebooting a room caused Lost Unit Server alerts and high CPU on the consoles, with RCB3 boards logging huge numbers of "Invalid URI when attempting to find an entry in the route table route table". A packet capture taken on the NUC RCB3 during a room reset showed the NUC being bombarded with nboSuppressAlertsMsg messages in a repeating cycle, with the message going from the NUC to an RCB3 board and coming straight back on the same socket connection, indicating a message loop. The issue was eventually reproduced in a legacy code simulation with two nursing units, a secondary monitoring relationship and seven of ten rooms disabled, by rebooting a room from the other unit's GRS10 and restarting it, which drove the first unit's GRS10 into a very high CPU state processing the looping messages. At the customer site the problem stopped after secondary monitoring configuration was changed, and re-enabling about 20 disabled rooms on one unit also cleared it.

comment_summary: Dome lights at a site remained populated after calls were cancelled, with no active calls and no stuck calls in the database. The site is newer and all RCB3s and GRS7s with RCB3 NUCs, and the occurrences are spread across multiple units and campuses rather than isolated to one location; in every observed instance it was the dome light for the originating location, matching the audio station in the affected room. Reviewing the syslogs with a live example found nothing helpful, so APLMOD and DOMELIGHT logging was enabled on all RCBs in two units to capture location, time of occurrence and base call id on the next report.

root_cause_summary: When a child grs7 abnormally disconnects from parent rcb3 abnormally ( In this case the grs7 application experienced a segfault. ).  The rcb3 clears the alert and notifies devices connected to of the cancel.  But doesn’t process the annunciation of the alert which would clear the dome lights, toning, etc… for the alert.

The grs7 is experiencing a seg fault in this scenario while in the RoombusProtocol::sendMessageSync function.  

When logging is turned up to everything in verbose mode the rcb3 can experience a seg fault.  Turning up logging this high is not recommended because of how much it can affect performance.  But the log should be fixed if this is needed for short periods for debugging.
