summary: Bed Data drops off Status Board after multiple disconnect/reconnect messages
description: Smart Sync is improperly handling when it gets a situation where a universal collector sends multiple Online/Offline statuses hitting it.  It will process these messages until it hits a condition where it errors out and throws an error like this

2021-07-08 15:23:39.6652 T72 BanyanServer: client endpoint:10.179.4.148:35087 session:331 id:uc-005191EHWIS disconnected

2021-07-08 15:23:45.2670 T126 BanyanServer: failed to process server event: System.InvalidCastException: Unable to cast object of type 'HR.Normalizer.Asbc.BedConnectorDataNormalizer' to type 'HR.Lib.SmartSync.Common.INormalizeBedData'.

   at HR.Lib.BanyanGateway.BanyanGateway.ProcessBedConnected(BedSession bedSession, IEnumerable\`1 bedData) .....

Shortly after these errors occur, StatusBoard will lose all bed data until Smart Sync is restarted.

Remote Access:   
Securelink > HCA-NorthCarolinaDivision-NC-Mission-etc- via Nexus > CDVWPAPPNBM01  
Credentials: Passed Through
root_cause_summary: The issue was caused by a software defect in Smart Sync's handling of repeated bed connectivity state changes. When a Universal Collector generated multiple rapid Online/Offline status messages for a bed connection, Smart Sync eventually encountered an invalid object type during bed data processing and threw a System.InvalidCastException.

Specifically, Smart Sync attempted to cast a BedConnectorDataNormalizer object to the INormalizeBedData interface, resulting in a processing failure. After this exception occurred, Smart Sync stopped correctly forwarding bed data updates to downstream consumers, causing all bed data to disappear from Status Board. The condition persisted until the Smart Sync service was restarted.
investigation_details: See comments/summary
rca_review_comments: A software defect in Smart Sync caused bed data processing to fail when repeated bed disconnect/reconnect events were received from the Universal Collector. Under this condition, Smart Sync encountered an invalid object type conversion, resulting in an unhandled exception that interrupted bed data processing. Once the failure occurred, bed data updates were no longer forwarded to Status Board, causing bed information to disappear until Smart Sync was restarted.

root_cause_summary: The issue was caused by the interaction of two software defects affecting Smart Sync and bed connectivity. First, a change introduced in the GRS5 firmware to support the RCB3 driver increased the frequency of bed disconnections. Second, when a bed disconnected while Smart Sync was actively processing a command, Smart Sync could enter a hung state where its command-processing queue was never cleared, preventing it from processing subsequent bed control messages.

As a result, Patient Safety continued to receive and process staff location events and safety alert suppression events, but bed control commands were no longer being executed. This explains why safety alerts continued to function while bed exit alarm state changes stopped responding. Restarting the Smart Sync service temporarily restored functionality by clearing the blocked processing state.

Increased bed disconnect events, driven by a GRS5 firmware issue, could cause Smart Sync's command-processing queue to become stuck while handling a bed command. Once this condition occurred, Smart Sync could no longer process subsequent bed control requests, preventing Patient Safety from enabling or disabling bed exit alarms even though safety alert functionality continued to operate normally.

description: We have found an NPS issue at UT where a room's safety state was changed from Suppressed to Disabled after a service reset.  Here's the sequence of events that led to this:

1. Caregiver enters room
2. Safety State changes to Suppressed and bed is disarmed as expected
3. While the caregiver is in the room, BMS Proxy and Smart Sync services are reset
4. When Smart Sync service is started again, the Safety State of the room is changed from Suppressed to Disabled

comment_summary: At a site the NPS safety state changed from Suppressed to Disabled after a service restart, and a chronology showed patient safety suppressed by a locating event, bed exit disarmed, two one-second Lost Smart Sync alerts around a BMS Proxy service stop and start, and the patient safety status moving to Bed Offline and then Disabled. Smart Sync logs for the event contained only a disposed subscriber callback channel message and a BanyanClient message received before client initialization, and the Safety service logged repeated WCF CommunicationException/QuotaExceededException errors stating the maximum incoming message size quota of 1048576 had been exceeded. Reproduction attempts could not recreate beds failing to rearm, but confirmed that restarting the BMS Proxy service while Smart Sync is running always produces a one-second Lost Smart Sync alert, attributed to the SystemAlertProcessor starting before the BedCommController and briefly believing Smart Sync is disconnected. Review also flagged the 1048576 message size quota as too small and easily corrected in a config file; defect NCBL-1862 was created and a related triage defect was referenced for a 4.0.300 fix.

root_cause_summary: When the caregiver left the room, the BMS proxy service and the Smart Sync service were in an errored state and the bed did not rearm automatically.  There was a lost smart sync alert caused by the BMS proxy service restarting just before the caregiver left the room.  Restarting both the BMS Proxy service and the Smart Sync service corrected the issue.
investigation_details: In my testing I have not been able to reproduce the issue with the beds not rearming themselves. Every time I stopped the smart Sync service, simulated the caregiver leaving the room, and then started the smart sync service again, the simulated beds would rearm themselves. I have been able to confirm that anytime the BMS proxy service is Started/Restarted while the smart sync service is running, we will see a 1 second lost smart sync alert. Based on the logs it looks like the caregiver left the room during this one second lost smart sync alert. I believe the one second lost smart sync alerts are caused by BMS Proxy service when the SystemAlertProcessor starts before the BedCommController, briefly the SystemAlertProcessor thinks that the smart sync service is disconnected and makes the lost smart sync alert before the BedCommController can actually subscribe to the smart sync service.
verification_summary: Restarting both the BMS Proxy service and the Smart Sync service corrected the issue.  
Referenced Defect TRIAGE-390 - Fix has been assigned to Voalte Nurse Call 4.0.300.  
BMSProxy service startup has been corrected to no longer generate lost smart sync alert when the service is available.
rca_review_comments: Smart Sync service has a momentary loss in connection when the BMS Proxy Service is restarted, causing the services to not perform NPS actions appropriately until BMS Proxy Service is fully started.

Per RCA team standup:

* Multiple cases pertaining Lost Central Server were added to this RCA.
* All symptoms are similar in nature.
* R&D will investigate all issues with GRS10 losing connectivity and/or rebooting.

Additional cases added to this RCA pertaining Lost NUC's - GRS10's rebooting per R&D

comment_summary: A nursing unit repeatedly raised a Lost Secondary Console call that returned after the call was cancelled and the NUC rebooted. Reviewing the basesystemsettings folder showed every secondary console in the NUC's secondary list was heartbeating except the NUC's own route id, rcb3-037221Y2WM2, which was itself present in that list; the NUC was not heartbeating with itself on either the ethernet or loopback interface, and it was the only device in the hospital with its own route id in its secondary list. The cause was identified as a monitoring criteria for a single room pointing at itself, so the NUC expected connections and heartbeats from itself and raised a Lost Secondary call when they never arrived. The fix was validated on a restored copy of the customer database before deleting the self-referencing monitoring criteria at the site and pushing configuration, after which the lost secondary call cleared with no device reboot, and no new lost secondary calls appeared for a week.

root_cause_summary: Updated configuration to resolve
investigation_details: There was a lost secondary console call that could not be cleared by any procedures to clear stuck calls - like marking the call as cancelled in the database and bouncing device service / devices.   I examined the secondary console list for the NUC that was placing the call.   This was RB 5 MB RCB3 NUC (RCB3) - 10.155.66.0 - rcb3-037221Y2WM2.  The nuc’s own ip address appeared in the list, and this was unique for the whole site - no other device had a reference to itself as a secondary.   Looking to see where the list was coming from, I found table function dbo.SecondaryConsoleConfig_GetByOrgUnitId_45.  By running the sql contained in the function, I determined that the reference to itself was coming from a monitoring criteria consisting of only a single room, many call types, and 1 org unit.    This monitoring criteria was somehow orphaned (not deleted or left behind somehow.)   After testing for safety on my machine, I deleted the monitoring criteria with sql statements, pushed configuration, and the lost secondary call disappeared.
troubleshooting_steps: Confirmed correct sw on both RCB and GRS10H. 

Confirmed no call forwarding set for the GRS10H. 

Confirmed no additional monitored units for GRS10H. 

Checked syslogs. No errors for either device. Checked configuration service log. 

Did see some other devices in the syslogs showing the invalid URI lines. 

Confirmed both effected devices are checking in successfully. 

Ran netstat on both devices. Confirmed they successfully establish to each other. 

Performed global push. No change. Purged configuration. No change. 

Forced push sw to both. No change.
troubleshooting_results: The alert makes no sense since the RCB NUC itself is not showing lost. Also the netstat proves the nuc and GRS10h are connected.
verification_summary: Determined the reference to itself was coming from a monitoring criteria consisting of only a single room, many call types, and 1 org unit. Pushed configuration, and the Lost Secondary Console alert cleared. Proper operation was confirmed & there were no patient safety issues reported. Although updating the configuration resolved issue; unable to determine how issue was caused.
rca_review_comments: Unknown how the NUC got into this state but issue has been resolved.

summary: NNC Cannot complete ECT save, No device configurations affected message
description: HCA site.  When saving or trying to run global push receive the No device configurations affected message.  Seems to timeout and have looked for timeout settings to allow complete save to no avail.

Requested customer increase memory on SQL server and no response yet.

Had Marva do a check on the DB for indexing issues or any memory concerns.  DB looks to be good shape.

Put Configuration service in Debug mode.  It appears it retries 2-3 times then fails and doesn't successfully complete the task before retrying.
root_cause_summary: The timeout on the ECT was due to the connection timing out between ECT and the configuration service.  The configuration service has very poor performance due to sql in loops that return very small pieces of information.  Also not every column in table functions and scalar functions is indexed.
investigation_details: We requested the customer database for reproduction purposes.  On my machine, configuration would generate and start attempting to push in about 9 minutes and 53 seconds.  There were no devices to push to, so pushing config would fail - this was expected.  Investigating the time consumption, I found the method OrgUnitSettings.GetNursingUnitsForSetup() to be consuming a few seconds every time it was called.  Drilling down into the method, the bottleneck was in the scalar SQL function OrgUnit_HasDisabledNucOrPrimary().  This function is called repeatedly in a loop, and this loop is repeated continuously!  This method joins on two unindexed columns on the device table, and adding an index on these two columns reduced the configuration generation time from 9:53 to 1:53 on my machine.  Going further, I replaced the repeated calls with a strategy of call once and cache the data, this reduced the time further to 1:31.   Creating the index on the customer site allowed configuration to be generated in 3:00.
rca_review_comments: Defect logged and triaged

RST received the following error when a customer has been upgraded to 3.9.102 with 3.7 Platform Reporting on SQL 2016

Msg 1914, Level 16, State 3, Line 1

Index cannot be created on object 'dbo.QueryNotificationErrorsQueue' because the object is not a user table or view.
root_cause_summary: This is not an issue in ERM and will not be logged as a defect in Platform Reporting.
investigation_details: Why's  
1) Why was the index maintenance jobs failing.  
Because the index job is returning three System Queues when it’s building a list of the database objects that resulted in this error.

2) Why is this not applicable to ERM?

Because in ERM there is a call to proc Maintenance.RebuildIndexes for Bed Data indexes and for Nurse Call indexes. This proc rebuilds indexes for specific table names. There is no generic list generated from a "select \* from ..." as there is in the Platform Reporting index maintenance job.

 

See additional information below:

RST dug into the error message and it looks like the index job is returning three System Queues when it’s building a list of the database objects.

SELECT \*  
FROM sys.objects  
where type = 'SQ'

name  
QueryNotificationErrorsQueue  
EventNotificationErrorsQueue  
ServiceBrokerQueue

If I alter the job and exclude these objects, then it has no issues. I also didn’t see this issue with a 3.9.102 upgrade yesterday with SQL 2014.  
I would like you to escalate it for RCA. It needs to be looked at to see if it’s an issue that needs to be addressed by R&D.

Description: Customer has had issues with their patient assignments since 2:46 AM CST. The messages look to be processing within SDC, but the caregivers are not being assigned to the patients or rooms.

root_cause_summary: The Mirth SQL database reached 100% utilization. After increasing the database size, ADT messages were able to process again. At some point on 2/1, the connection stopped receiving new messages on the SDC side as a result of this database issue. We don't have a way to log this in SDC, and all appeared healthy with the connection. The ADT feeds needed to be restarted by redeploying the customer ADT Mirth channels. The ADT channels resumed receiving and processing messages after this restart. After the channels caught up with the backlog, all system behavior was back to normal. 

To prevent this issue moving forward, we're working on active monitoring and alerts around the Mirth database. Previously, alerts we thought had been configured were not fully implemented. Alerts and monitoring will allow us to prevent this issue before customer reports in the future.
investigation_details: In the morning on 2/1, I was notified that SDC was down, impacting all production customers. It was discovered that day that the issue was with SDC Mirth’s SQL database. The database had reached 100% utilization in the late evening of 1/31, and as a result new messages were not processing and instead getting queued up. The Dev Ops team increased the size of the database by 1 TB (also on 2/1), and messages began to process in the afternoon.

In the morning on 2/2, I was notified that several customers were reporting ADT messages queueing on their end and not being received by SDC. In SDC, the connection looked fine, and it was not immediately clear that the connection was not functional. After restarting the ADT connection on our end, messages began to come through. All customer connections were redeployed in the morning, which created new queues for the customers. By the afternoon, a majority of these backup queues were depleted, and the system was back to normal. By Sunday, all customers had their backup queues depleted.
verification_summary: Patient data was not updating for Voalte users due to consumption of the Mirth SQL database reaching ed 100% utilization.  
DB size was increased and ADT connections redeployed.

At some point on 2/1, the connection stopped receiving new messages on the SDC side as a result of this database issue. We don't have a way to log this in SDC, and all appeared healthy with the connection. The ADT feeds needed to be restarted by redeploying the customer ADT Mirth channels. The ADT channels resumed receiving ADT after this restart. 

To prevent this issue moving forward, we're working on active monitoring and alerts around the Mirth database. Previously, alerts we thought had been configured were not fully implemented.

summary: ADT messages with ROL segments processed incorrectly.
description: ADT HL7 patient messages with staff assignments (indicated by ROL) are incorrectly translated to json in a few cases:

1. In the case of multiple assignments for the same staff member, and historical assignments precede the active assignment, the active assignment will have an end date filled out - it **should** be null.  This end date often precedes the start date for that assignment, causing clinical interface to **reject** the whole hl7 message.
2. In the case of ROL segments with missing staff information, the json will contain null staff data.  This will cause clinical interface to **reject** the whole hl7 message.   These assignments should be left out of the json.
impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
In Care Assignments, Build Care Assignment Array, a temporary variable in a loop was not getting reset to null at the top of the loop.  
The temporary variable would retain the value from the previous loop in the case of a staff assignment with no end date.  
This could cause the end date to precede the start date, causing the whole HL7 message to be rejected.  
Also, Staff assignments with no employee id are not added to the message forwarded to nurse call, because this will cause the  
whole HL7 message to be rejected.

Before: Staff Assignment HL7 messages with historical staff assignments followed by current assignment would cause the whole message to be rejected, in the case the last historical staff assignment message had an end date PRIOR to the current assignment start date.  
After: Current staff assignments are now sent with a null end date like they should be.  The HL7 message is properly processed.  
Before:  HL7 staff assignment messages with no employee id causes the whole HL7 message to be rejected  
After: HL7 staff assignments with no employee id are not forwareded on to nurse call, but the rest of the HL7 message is.

comment_summary: The defect reported that upgrading firmware with two GRS5 or two SRS devices attached to an RCB2/3 starts upgrading the second device while the first is still upgrading. The response established that this is by design: firmware may be applied concurrently to child devices under a single RCB, and logs show the firmware management service waits for the child GRS5 apply to complete before starting the parent RCB apply. It also established that the two test cases asserting otherwise were wrong, including their expectation about the APPLY status colour, since the applied status does not need to be green and green only indicates the updated device manifest matches the downloaded firmware. The defect was therefore judged invalid and the test updates were dry run.

summary: Delays in message processing in the device service cause false lost heartbeats and dropped sockets.
description: This issue was reported by HCA JFK Hospital.   When the call table purge job is run nightly at 3:30 am, this causes locking on the call table.   If calls are being updated or inserted into the database at the same time, this will cause the processing of those calls to wait for access to the call table. 

The device service processes all messages on an action block with a parallelism of 1.   When a call insert is being performed and the call table is locked, all other processing will wait, **including heartbeat processing.**  Because the heartbeat timers are still running, they will time out and the device service will drop that socket, **even though wireshark shows heartbeats coming in from the device.**   The recognition of the heartbeat is delayed due to the action block waiting on sql.

  
**Summary of what occurs:**

1. **Database purge job runs, locking the database's call table.**

    1. Details: The nurse call database purge job runs, which can lock the nurse call database's call table for extended periods (1-2 minutes). 
    
2. **A nurse call is placed.**

    1. Details: Each time a nurse call is placed, the Device Service is responsible for inserting the new call record into the database's call table as part of its standard functionality. However, in this scenario, the Device Service cannot do so while the purge job locks the database's call table.
    
3. **Device Service Stops Processing.**

    1. Details: Since the Device Service is single-threaded, it's unable to handle additional processing as it waits for the nurse call database's call table to become available to complete the call record insertion. 
    
4. **Nursing Unit Controllers (NUCs) heartbeats are not processed, causing the devices to appear lost.** 

    1. Details: While the Device Service has halted processing (due to the waiting in listed in step 3) Nursing Unit Controllers (NUC) heartbeat messages to the Device service are not acknowledged, resulting in heartbeat timer expiration. Once the heartbeat timer expires the device service drops its socket connection with every connected NUC on the system (because it falsely believes they stopped sending heartbeat messages). Note: This results in system alerts on nurse call user interfaces. 
    
5. **Database purge job releases lock on the database's call table.**

    1. Details: Once the purge job completes deleting historical call data >75 days old, it releases its lock on the database's call table.

steps_taken: System in normal use.   For reproduction purposes, a 32 second delay may be placed in the Call_Insert stored procedure, at the bottom, right before the last 2 lines 'end' and 'go'.    Then start Navicare and place and cancel calls, the fake lost heartbeats and device reconnects will occur.  
There is another reproduction method that requires no changes to the call_insert stored procedure:  
1\.  Open sql query analyzer  
2\.  Open a new query  
3\.  Paste the following sql into the query window:  
BEGIN TRAN    
SELECT TOP (1) 1 FROM call WITH (TABLOCKX)  
WAITFOR DELAY '00:05:00'   
ROLLBACK TRAN     
GO 

4\.  Execute the sql - a table lock will be placed on the call table for 5 minutes.   This time may be changed according to need.  
5\.  Place and cancel 20 or so staff and staff emergency calls.   The device service will execute the call_insert stored procedure and hang.  
6\.  After a period of time, lost heartbeats will be logged for devices connected to the device service.  These devices will attempt to connect again, but will be unable to establish a full handshake.   My grs-10 that is also a NUC will display a Lost Central Server system alert.  
7\.  When the 5 minute delay is completed on the table lock query, the device service will quickly process all outstanding inserts, and the action block will process messages again, causing the devices to reconnect.

root_cause_summary: The connector should be modified to only raise button press events if there is one in the ModelUpdate.Events collection.
investigation_details: When the connector starts (or even when a tag is discovered and the connector is already running or when the connector re-connects), the HPL system will send an initial state of the tag to the rtls connector.  The RTLS connector will receive that message and, because it has a “buttonPress”, it’ll interpret it as a click even though the message also indicates the button press occurred at the beginning of time. So, every time the RTLS Connector disconnects and re-connects to HPL, we’d get one of these mass reporting events; with every single tag that’s assigned at that moment generating a duress call.

HPL does not re-set the timestamp back to `DateTime.MinValue` (ever). So it’ll only be that value if the button has never been clicked. So this fix could get tricky as you’d need to make a decision based on the last time the tag reported. Or something. I’d be happy to rubber duck solution options.

Investigation of the RTLS connector logs found Centrak sending duplicate button events in the same data packet (entries ending 'button2, button2'), and the IntegrationService log showed the IHEAdapter repeatedly failing to reach a development host with "The remote name could not be resolved: 'hi-dev-nnc1.hrdev.io'", a value hard-coded in the app config that applies to all sites without a PCD-05 integration. root_cause_summary: Code requiring a proper sql connection was placed in the integration service, but this connection is rarely filled out, because the related feature is not used at all sites.  The long period of time required for the sql connection to time out causes issues with other code functionality.
investigation_details: This issue is caused by a missing connection string in the ClinicalApi.CallAdapter.dll.   A sql server connection is attempted on a regularly scheduled basis, but no connection can be made, and this process takes 30 seconds or more.   Meanwhile, the button press messages back up behind the sql connection attempt and are not serviced promptly, causing the delay in cancellation.
verification_summary: Workaround applied to resolve issue.

summary: RtlsConnector misinterprets HPL initial-state button info as real-time button events
description: RtlsConnector currently reads `buttonPress` sub-objects from an HPL model update’s `"created"` and/or `"changed"` objects, an interprets them as real-time button events. This results in false button presses sometimes being issued to the nurse call system from HPL, which depending on the configuration may enunciate as invalid duress calls, sometimes in large number at once.
To prevent this, RtlsConnector needs to be modified to only raise button press events if there is one in the `ModelUpdate.Events` collection (`"events"` object).
See https://hill-rom.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-1201 for the history on this topic and more details.
Please reach out to @Matthew Morgan with any questions.
